levels.effect: Gain access to Numina equal to Spiritus Sancti dots. Spend Vitae in place of Essence and use Blood Potency where Rank determines potency. The vampire learns one Numen when gaining this power and learns others by feeding an ephemeral being to discorporation. Replacing a known Numen requires a full day and night before using the new one.

levels.name: Consecration of the Self
levels.summary: Consecration of the Self, the 4-dot expression of Spiritus Sancti.
levels.requirement: Fill an ephemeral being's Corpus with lethal damage, then activate the power; a spirit with no Essence cannot resist.
levels.dicePool: Resolve + Occult + Spiritus Sancti vs. Resistance + Rank

rollResults.success: Devour the spirit and take on its traits. The vampire may exchange Vitae for another ephemera's Essence one-for-one, her fangs become a bane to ephemera, she may choose her own direction of gravity and move at normal Speed, and she may pass through beings and solid objects as an instant action unless Twilight is obstructed. Using the last benefit while Dodging adds Spiritus Sancti dots.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The transformation lasts nights equal to Blood Potency.
rollResults.failure: The spirit's Essence does not merge with the vampire.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The spirit possesses the vampire for the scene.

levels.name: The Kingdom of Heaven
levels.summary: The Kingdom of Heaven, the 5-dot expression of Spiritus Sancti.
levels.requirement: Scribe holy sigils in Vitae around the perimeter: three for a house or garden, six for a city block or cemetery, and nine for a megamall or city park.
levels.duration: One week per Blood Potency dot; longer while the vampire remains
levels.effect: Ephemera within the Kingdom gain Materialized. Entities in Twilight approaching within 10 − Blood Potency meters roll Resistance + Rank penalized by Spiritus Sancti; failure compels entry. Leaving without permission costs one Willpower and requires Power + Rank contested by Presence + Intimidation + Spiritus Sancti. The vampire always senses ephemera inside, pays no initial Vitae for Shape of the Divine there, and multiplies Cast Off the Scales' Kindred Senses range by Spiritus Sancti dots. After the duration, the effect ends only when the vampire leaves.

ritualDisciplines.name: Kimiya
ritualDisciplines.summary: Jaliniyya blood alchemy; each dot grants one free formula and additional formulae cost two Experiences.
ritualDisciplines.cost: 1 Vitae plus blood sacrifice equal to formula rating − 1, minimum 1

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The ritualist gains Jaded.
rollResults.success: The formula takes effect.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The ritualist gains Inspired.

ritualDisciplines.name: Therion
ritualDisciplines.statusRequirement: Tenth Choir membership in good standing
ritualDisciplines.summary: Tenth Choir blood sorcery; each dot grants one free Sacrilege and additional Sacrileges cost two Experiences.
ritualDisciplines.cost: Vitae equal to Sacrilege rating, acquired by feeding from a Grigor
ritualDisciplines.effect: If Humanity is not higher than the Sacrilege rating, committing it causes a breaking point with dice equal to the ritual rating.

ritualDisciplines.name: Gilded Cage
ritualDisciplines.summary: Architect blood sorcery that alters urban flows through prepared Ways and Means. Each dot grants one free Invocation; additional Invocations cost two Experiences.
ritualDisciplines.cost: The Invocation's Ways and Means must be present but are not consumed
ritualDisciplines.effect: Invocations affect defined urban areas. A dramatic failure inflicts Competitive instead of Humbled; an exceptional success on three successes also grants Convergence.

ritualDisciplines.name: Crúac
ritualDisciplines.statusRequirement: Circle of the Crone Status • to learn new Crúac or rites
ritualDisciplines.summary: Ritual Discipline of the Circle of the Crone. Each purchased dot normally grants one free rite, and known rites cannot exceed the Crúac rating.
ritualDisciplines.cost: Rites cost Vitae equal to rite rating before the casting roll
ritualDisciplines.action: Extended; base interval 30 minutes per roll, 15 minutes when Crúac exceeds the rite rating
ritualDisciplines.effect: The unmodified casting pool determines the maximum number of rolls. Rituals fail if interrupted. Standard blood-sorcery roll results and ritual-specific contested/resisted defenses apply.

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The ritual fails completely and the sacrifice is lost. Crúac grants Tempted; Theban Sorcery grants Humbled. The next ritual attempted suffers a –2 dice penalty.
rollResults.failure: No successes are accumulated. The ritualist may abandon the ritual or continue; continuing inflicts the Stumbled Condition.
rollResults.success: Accumulate successes. When the ritual's target number of successes is reached, its effect takes place immediately.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: In addition to accumulating successes, choose one: reduce the target successes by the Ritual Discipline dots; reduce the interval to 15 minutes (or 5 minutes if the Discipline exceeds the ritual rating); or gain Ecstatic (Crúac) / Raptured (Theban Sorcery) if the ritual succeeds.

suggestedModifiers.situation: Power targets or applies to a vampire with existing blood sympathy; Crúac doubles this modifier.
The ritualist is rushed or distracted; multiple distractions are cumulative.
The ritualist prepares an elaborate ritual beyond the minimum sacrifice.
Theban only: successful meditation; bonus equals meditation successes.
Crúac only: extra Vitae sacrificed beyond the requirement; bonus equals excess Vitae.

ritualDisciplines.name: Theban Sorcery
ritualDisciplines.statusRequirement: Lancea et Sanctum Status • to learn new Theban Sorcery or miracles
ritualDisciplines.summary: Ritual Discipline of the Lancea et Sanctum. Each purchased dot normally grants one free miracle, and known miracles cannot exceed the Theban rating.
ritualDisciplines.cost: 1 Willpower plus the miracle's sacrament before the casting roll
ritualDisciplines.action: Extended; base interval 30 minutes per roll, 15 minutes when Theban Sorcery exceeds the miracle rating
ritualDisciplines.effect: The unmodified casting pool determines the maximum number of rolls. Rituals fail if interrupted. The caster's Humanity must be at least the miracle's rating.

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The ritual fails completely and the sacrifice is lost. Crúac grants Tempted; Theban Sorcery grants Humbled. The next ritual attempted suffers a –2 dice penalty.
rollResults.failure: No successes are accumulated. The ritualist may abandon the ritual or continue; continuing inflicts the Stumbled Condition.
rollResults.success: Accumulate successes. When the ritual's target number of successes is reached, its effect takes place immediately.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: In addition to accumulating successes, choose one: reduce the target successes by the Ritual Discipline dots; reduce the interval to 15 minutes (or 5 minutes if the Discipline exceeds the ritual rating); or gain Ecstatic (Crúac) / Raptured (Theban Sorcery) if the ritual succeeds.

suggestedModifiers.situation: Power targets or applies to a vampire with existing blood sympathy; Crúac doubles this modifier.
The ritualist is rushed or distracted; multiple distractions are cumulative.
The ritualist prepares an elaborate ritual beyond the minimum sacrifice.
Theban only: successful meditation; bonus equals meditation successes.
Crúac only: extra Vitae sacrificed beyond the requirement; bonus equals excess Vitae.

devotions.name: After Hours
devotions.summary: Continues Bloodcrafting work with inhuman speed and endurance.
devotions.effect: If the vampire performs an extended action while she has the Lethargic Condition, she can activate this Devotion at the beginning of that task to add any penalties from the Condition as bonuses instead, channeling her exhaustion into laser focus. However, she still can’t spend Willpower. Once she completes the task, Lethargic applies as usual, and may have compounded in the meantime. This Devotion does not apply to blood sorcery. Alternate Constructions If you prefer, Bloodcrafting can operate under the Build Equipment rules from the Chronicles of Darkness Rulebook (p. 101). Use those systems with the following changes: Cost and dice pool remain the same as above. Determine how many modifications and how much Durability the object will need, and apply that number as a penalty rather than the one determined in Chronicles of Darkness. This modifier cannot exceed –5. On an exceptional success, apply an additional point of Durability or Size, if desired, and if these traits aren’t at their maximum already.

devotions.name: Lockpicker's Wrist
devotions.summary: Reshapes a crafted tool or limb for impossible access.
devotions.effect: The vampire slips out of a restraint, whether rope, handcuffs, duct tape, or any other object meant to hold her. If the object had less Durability than her Vigor dots, it takes a point of damage in the process. This Devotion applies whether the restraint is around the vampire’s hands or her feet, or even her torso. It doesn’t work in grapples, though it would apply to any use of the Restrain move. If a supernatural power is involved in the vampire’s restraint, a Clash of Wills takes place.

devotions.name: Work Fast, Not Hard
devotions.summary: Accelerates Bloodcrafting without sacrificing the finished object's function.
devotions.requirement: The vampire activates a Discipline or Devotion that takes an instant action, paying all costs.
devotions.effect: The vampire treats a supernatural power that would normally be an instant action as a reflexive action. If the effect costs Willpower, activating Work Fast, Not Hard is considered a discrete action. However, the vampire is limited in that he can only use this Devotion once per turn. An Acteius can use it after using another instant action power, but he cannot use the same effect twice in one turn.

devotions.name: Bad Trip
devotions.summary: Turns an infused treat into a terrifying altered state.
devotions.requirement: The vampire uses her bloodline gift and spends an additional Vitae, included in the cost.
devotions.effect: If a victim imbibes the tainted substance, he must succeed on a Stamina + Blood Potency roll penalized by the Candyman’s Dominate dots. On a failure, he gains the Intoxicated Condition, suffering strange and alarming hallucinations. The vampire is privy to the victim’s trip, and may, as a reflexive action, spend a Vitae to adjust the victim’s experience in one of the following ways: Content Warning The powers below involve supernatural malnourishment and compulsive eating. These can be difficult subjects for some players, so make sure everyone’s on board when using those aspects of the Candymen in your chronicles. John Stavropoulos’ X-Card (found here) is an indispensable tool for dealing with sensitive topics in roleplaying games. • H alve the victim’s Defense for a turn (rounding down). • C ause the victim to suffer from vertigo and nausea, imposing the Drugged Tilt for a turn (this stacks with Intoxicated). • I n combat, adjust the victim’s perceptions so they attack an ally rather than an intended target for a turn.

devotions.name: Everlasting Blood Doll
devotions.summary: Makes a treated vessel endure repeated feeding and addiction.
devotions.cost: 1 Vitae per victim Size and 1 Willpower
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have inflicted the Mesmerized Condition on the victim.
devotions.duration: One week per dot of Blood Potency
devotions.effect: The vampire encases a mortal victim in a prison of sweet ichor, resembling something between hard candy and amber. This shell is as hard as stone (Durability 2), and its Structure is equal to (victim Size + Durability). Through an exposed body part, the vampire can feed freely, and the encased victim heals lethal damage equal to the vampire’s Vigor dots every 24 hours. While encased, the victim is kept in stasis and doesn’t require food. However, they also remain partially aware, flitting in and out of fever dreams. These hallucinations are at once hellish and blissful, highly addictive and deeply unsettling. Should the victim escape their imprisonment, their shattered sense of reality manifests with the Fugue Condition (Vampire, p. 304). Furthermore, a released victim becomes a vector for the Peddler’s bloodline gift as long as Fugue lasts. If she feeds them a point of Vitae, anyone who drinks the victim’s blood treats it as though they were draining the Candyman. This includes Vincula, but isn’t sufficient for an elder vampire to sustain herself. Using this Devotion is a Humanity 1 breaking point.

devotions.name: Sugar Rush
devotions.summary: Converts the Candyman's product into a burst of speed and energy.
devotions.requirement: The vampire uses her bloodline gift and spends additional Vitae, included in the cost
devotions.effect: For the rest of the scene, all who eat the vampire’s product gain her Vigor dots as a bonus to Physical actions, pushing their bodies to the human limit. However, every exceptional success on these rolls self-inflicts a point of lethal damage. At the end of the scene, subjects suffer the Lethargic Condition until they get a full night’s rest, or another hit.

devotions.name: Sweet Tooth
devotions.summary: Creates an Overwhelming Hunger for the Candyman's chosen product.

rollResults.success: The victim is overwhelmed with hunger for a particular food. He gains the Overwhelming Hunger Condition.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The hunger is so complete that the victim also gains the Wanton Condition.
rollResults.failure: The victim isn’t any hungrier than they were before.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire triggers the wrong reflex in her victim. He gains the Steadfast Condition.

devotions.name: Thinner
devotions.summary: Makes a treated body or substance unnaturally slight and easy to move.
devotions.requirement: The victim must have been a victim of the vampire’s bloodline gift within the same week.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Intimidation + Nightmare vs. Stamina + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire curses a mortal victim with an aversion to eating. For the duration, he finds himself unable to willingly consume any form of nourishment. He’s repulsed by food (or blood), and must spend a Willpower not to vomit up anything more substantial than water. If mortal, he accumulates a lethal damage per day he fails to nourish himself, which he cannot heal until the duration expires or he seeks medical attention.

devotions.name: Dropping the Act
devotions.summary: Releases cultivated civility in a sudden display of the Beast.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have Playing the Role active.
devotions.effect: When attempting to force a mortal’s doors in Social maneuvering, the vampire can activate this Devotion and drop the effects of the Blush of Life and Playing the Role: The victim immediately (but briefly) becomes aware of the Cockerel’s malignancy as a blood-drinking corpse. She suffers a breaking point with a penalty equal to (10 – the vampire’s Humanity) divided by two, rounding up. Remove one of the victim’s Doors if she succeeds on the breaking point roll, or two if she fails.

devotions.name: Playing the Role
devotions.summary: Adopts a social part so completely that the performance becomes supernatural.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have the Blush of Life active when she uses this Devotion.

rollResults.success: The vampire suppresses her Predatory Aura to further affect a facsimile of mortality. While this Devotion is active, she subtracts her successes from any Humanity-based penalties when tempting or negotiating with mortals. If successes exceed the penalty, she gains no additional bonus. In addition, she does not register as a vampire to other Predatory Auras.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: As with a success, and if the number of successes exceeds the vampire’s Social penalties for low Humanity, she does add bonus dice equal to the difference.
rollResults.failure: The Blush of Life takes effect, but the Cockerel’s power of mimicry fails to overcome her unsettling nature.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: Not only does the Devotion fail to take effect, the Haunt’s attempt at imitation is deeply offputting. For the rest of the scene, mortals’ impressions of the vampire are treated as one level lower in Social maneuvering.

devotions.name: Iron Dogma
devotions.summary: Hardens declared faith into supernatural resistance against contradiction.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must inflict the Charmed Condition on the victim within the same scene.
devotions.effect: The victim treats the vampire's opinions, arguments, and beliefs as intrinsically true and cannot be convinced otherwise. Attempts to persuade the victim that the vampire lied suffer a penalty equal to the vampire's Majesty dots; halve this penalty, rounding up, when the victim is shown direct evidence such as photographs or video.

devotions.name: Kingdom of Heaven
devotions.summary: Extends selected Majesty powers across every witness inside the vampire's Oubliette.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be within his Oubliette when activating this Devotion.
devotions.effect: The vampire can use Confidant, Green Eyes, Loyalty, and Iron Dogma on groups, provided every victim can see and hear him and is wholly within his Oubliette. A group of humans resists using the highest appropriate Resistance Attribute among them; each Kindred present rolls separately. Green Eyes, Iron Dogma, and Loyalty require their Vitae cost only once per activation, regardless of the number of targets.

devotions.name: Master of the Maze
devotions.summary: Transforms a Labyrinth into a shifting Maze under the Keeper's complete spatial control.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must mark each entrance to the structure with a point of Vitae (front doors, fire exits, etc.) Windows, skylights, and holes in the walls do not need to be marked unless they’re considered regular access points.
devotions.duration: One week per dot of Blood Potency
devotions.effect: The vampire gains complete control over the layout of the Maze. By spending a Vitae and taking an instant action, they can alter the layout in any way they see fit, with two caveats. First, the Maze cannot change while being observed by an outsider. A victim might wander down a straight corridor, look over her shoulder at a distant sound, and turn back to discover she’s now at a crossroad. Second, the Maze must always have at least one pathway that can lead victims to an exit, even if that goal moves. The Warden instinctively knows the location of any being within their Maze, as well as the fastest way to reach her. They can travel at a pace equal to (Speed * [Blood Potency + 1]), which compounds further if the vampire uses the active effect of Celerity. Note that this Devotion is not an illusion, and no amount of Auspex will help see a victim through the Maze. The vampire can renew this Devotion by re-marking the entrances before the duration expires.

devotions.name: Abundance of Nyx
devotions.summary: Implants true darkness in a subject so it can be expelled to smother nearby light.
devotions.procedure: Working in total darkness, the Lygos opens a Kindred subject's abdomen and removes several internal organs. The procedure takes one hour and inflicts two lethal damage, or two hours without damage. Performing it on oneself requires Resolve + Stamina; failure prevents another attempt until the next night.
devotions.outcome: For the rest of the night, or until the subject expels it as an instant action, the subject carries true darkness. The expelled cloud extinguishes every light source except fire and sunlight within nine meters for minutes equal to the Lygos' Blood Potency; those lights cannot be reignited during that time.

devotions.name: Denial of the Enemy
devotions.summary: Makes ordinary light avoid the subject after burial in ritual darkness.
devotions.procedure: The Lygos smears one Vitae over the subject's eyes and buries the subject at least two meters underground in a light-proof container for one to six hours while chanting. The Vitae must remain in place. At the end, the Lygos unearths the subject and ritually snuffs a candle.
devotions.outcome: For as many hours as the subject was buried, ordinary light avoids them. Fire and sunlight are unaffected. The subject cannot be seen or detected by light-gathering technology, though other senses work normally. Supernaturally keen sight triggers a Clash of Wills against Truths of Erebus + Blood Potency. Auspex does not bypass the effect, and the subject cannot end it early.

devotions.name: Heart of Darkness
devotions.summary: Transmutes a subject through prolonged contact with absolute darkness.
devotions.procedure: In a pitch-black room, the Lygos opens a Kindred subject's ribcage, inflicting one lethal damage, paints the exposed heart with ash and blood, and seals the wound. The coating and Lesson last 24 hours. A Lygos cannot perform this Lesson on himself.
devotions.outcome: The subject's next breaking point during the Lesson automatically succeeds with one success. After the Heart absorbs the sin, the subject is detached from their highest Touchstone for the following night.

devotions.name: Bloody Good Flick
devotions.summary: Turns a staged horror scene into a stronger supernatural performance.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must use her bloodline gift on a copy of her film.
devotions.effect: Victims who watch the entire movie suffer the Spooked Condition, as every subconscious fear seems to leap from the shadows. Viewers can try to stop watching with a Resolve + Composure roll, penalized by the Nosferatu’s Blood Potency dots, but failure means they remain enrapt for the runtime. Even after Spooked ends, the audience can’t stop thinking about it. For one week, the vampire can inflict Discipline powers on a victim of her movie without paying the cost, using their lingering fears and fascination to fuel her tricks.

devotions.name: Death by Cliché
devotions.summary: Makes a familiar horror trope dangerously real.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must spread her Vitae at a central point in the area of effect.

rollResults.success: Anyone who enters the area starts to behave as if they were in the middle of a B-movie. The extent of this effect is up to (10 * Blood Potency) meters. Characters can contest this Devotion with Resolve + Blood Potency, but must exceed the vampire’s successes on the activation roll. Those who fail gain the Walking Cliché Tilt. Anyone subject to the vampire’s bloodline Gift cannot make a resistance roll — she’s already in their heads.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire delights in her victims’ turmoil so much she regains a point of spent Willpower when she springs her trap.
rollResults.failure: The vampire herself is the only cliché present.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire suffers the Walking Cliché Tilt for the rest of the scene.

devotions.name: Timeless Classic
devotions.summary: Preserves a performance's supernatural impact across generations.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must use her bloodline gift on a copy of her film.
devotions.effect: If the vampire is about to take an injury that would knock her into torpor or cause Final Death, she can choose to have her connected film take the brunt of the attack instead, refreshing the Willpower point she invested into the object. This is a reflexive action, and destroys the chosen copy of the movie. This Devotion doesn’t protect the vampire from further violence, but merely transfers the fatal blow, perhaps giving her enough time to escape. A vampire can only have one instance of this Devotion active at a time.

devotions.name: Watch Party
devotions.summary: Draws power from a live audience consuming the same horror.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must use her bloodline gift on a copy of her film.
devotions.effect: The vampire inherently knows when anyone watches her movie, and if she’s within (Blood Potency) miles of its location, she can extract a terrible price of admission. As the victims watch, the vampire can drink their blood as if she were physically present, at a rate of one Vitae per turn; for bookkeeping purposes, this is considered a violent feeding (Vampire, p. 94). This requires the Von Schreck to spend a Willpower per victim. This draining effect lasts (Vigor) turns per vessel. However, the vampire can only do this once per person in a night. As the body begins to drain, victims who want to look away from the screen must succeed a Resolve + Composure roll, penalized by the vampire’s Blood Potency dots. Success means the vampire can’t feed from them anymore. If the film is also subject to Bloody Good Flick, treat this as a single resistance action. If a victim is a vampire, the Vinculum and blood addiction applies as usual. This Devotion is an exception to the bloodline’s bane.

devotions.name: Mission from the Gods
devotions.summary: Receives a binding omen or task from the powers honored by the Yagnatia.
devotions.requirement: Use Entombed Command on the victim, then activate this Devotion.
devotions.effect: Instead of implanting a complete order, the vampire gives the victim an obsession and the Tasked Condition for the duration of Entombed Command or until it resolves. While it lasts, attempts to manipulate the victim into pursuing that goal exceptionally succeed on three successes.

devotions.name: Brain Dead
devotions.summary: Convince a Delusional victim to make reckless, shortsighted mistakes.
devotions.requirement: The victim must have the Delusional Condition.

rollResults.success: The victim is imbued with shortsighted invincibility (or just brain damage). For the rest of the scene, he suffers a penalty equal to successes on any Mental actions to evade, trick, or outwit the vampire.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: On normal failures, the victim dramatically fails affected actions.
rollResults.failure: The victim is as smart as he ever was.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire instills a true sense of invincibility in the victim: He gains the Steadfast Condition, and resolves Delusional.

devotions.name: Friend to Foe
devotions.summary: Redirect suspicion and hostility from the vampire onto a chosen bystander.
devotions.effect: For the rest of the scene, everyone in the immediate area redirects all suspicions, fears, or hostilities they feel for the vampire onto the victim. The Nosferatu gains no special advantage for this effect beyond a distraction, but it’s a good one: She or one of her allies could be carrying a chainsaw and a severed head and people would think she’s the least of their worries. Note also that this isn’t a mental compulsion, just a redirection of the vampire’s natural creepiness. People will react however they normally would to a threat. This effect ends if the Nosferatu attacks anyone other than the designated victim.
devotions.requirement: The vampire uses Touch of Shadow on the victim then activates this Devotion.

devotions.name: Gaslight
devotions.summary: Alter one visible detail of a room and make everyone but one victim accept it as normal.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Subterfuge + Obfuscate vs. highest Resolve + Blood Potency
devotions.requirement: The vampire spills the Vitae cost at a central point in the room before she activates this Devotion.

rollResults.success: Before the end of the scene she spilled her blood, the vampire can spend a Willpower to visibly alter a detail within the room, such as an occupant or an architectural detail. She might change the wallpaper from a sedate stripe pattern to a psychedelic paisley, or a singer’s hair from ash blonde to fiery red. Witnesses ignore this change, accepting it as normal. If questioned, they’ll justify it with obvious lies or absurd leaps of logic. For the purposes of bookkeeping, major Storyteller characters and player characters should take the equivalent of False Memories ( Vampire, p. 303), but side characters don’t need to track a Condition. Once the illusion forms, the vampire designates an individual who cannot ignore the change. For the rest of the night, others affected by this power treat this victim with hostility and scorn when he points out the alteration. People aren’t supernaturally compelled to behave this way, but once per scene, anyone who significantly chastises the victim refreshes a Willpower. At the end of the night, the others won’t recall the change at all, and memories of their behavior will become hazy. However, the victim will remember his suffering all too well.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The totality of the illusion is such that the vampire can add her Nightmare dots to any role to incite the crowd against her victim’s “ravings.”
rollResults.failure: Reality remains immutable.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire reflects her lies back on herself. She gains the Delusional Condition for the rest of the night, believing her Devotion worked.

devotions.name: Gaze of the Abyss
devotions.summary: Show a Frightened victim incomprehensible horrors that drain Willpower.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have inflicted the Frightened Condition on her victim.

rollResults.success: The vampire shows the victim horrors beyond comprehension, utterly demoralizing him and inflicting one point of Willpower loss per success.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vision of horror is so complete that the victim also gains the Fugue Condition for the rest of the night.
rollResults.failure: The victim’s mind is no worse for wear.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire has looked too closely into the abyss, and it echoes in her mind. She gains the Frightened Condition.

devotions.name: Hell Beast
devotions.summary: Warp a raised animal familiar into a larger and more frightening undead beast.
devotions.cost: 1 additional Vitae with Raise the Familiar
devotions.effect: The Nosferatu enhances her familiar. It gains a point of Size, stretching its dead skin against protruding bone and gnarled muscle, and distributes half the vampire’s Blood Potency among Strength, Dexterity, and Stamina (rounding up). Furthermore, it adds the Haunt’s Nightmare dots to its Intimidation Skill, even if that would raise the trait above its maximum. The creature also permanently benefits from the effect of Dread Presence, though the illusions it conjures up are cruder than those of a vampire. The Nosferatu herself is immune to this effect. The vampire must renew this Devotion along with Raise the Familiar. If not, the corpse’s form collapses in on itself, and cannot be resurrected. If the vampire knows Undying Familiar ( Vampire, p. 148), she can spend an additional Vitae when using that Devotion to assure her ghoul immediately rises as a hell beast if it dies in a violent encounter. If the vampire knows Face in the Crowd, she can spend an additional Experience into this Devotion to imbue the creature with that effect, causing mortals to ignore its monstrous appearance until it attacks.
devotions.requirement: The vampire spends an additional Vitae (included in the cost) as she uses Raise the Familiar.

devotions.name: Iron Façade
devotions.summary: Conceal all wounds and make the first use of Resilience demoralize attackers.
devotions.effect: For the rest of the scene, any wounds the vampire takes do not appear on his body, no matter how grievous; even severed limbs seem to hold together. The vampire doesn’t gain any physical advantage, but it’s an easy way to demoralize foes. Furthermore, the first time the vampire uses Resilience in the scene, witnesses must succeed on a reflexive Resolve + Composure – Blood Potency roll before attacking him. On a failure, they lose the 10-again quality on the attack.

devotions.name: Jump Scare
devotions.summary: Appear from concealment at a victim's most vulnerable instant.
devotions.effect: The vampire unleashes an aura of dread that distracts her prey, then appears before him at the height vulnerability. For the rest of the turn, the vampire ignores the victim’s Defense, and her first strike takes the 8-again quality. The vampire can only use this Devotion on a victim once per scene.
devotions.requirement: The victim must know the vampire is nearby, but not visible.

devotions.name: Living Nightmare
devotions.summary: Project an autonomous, intangible horror that channels the vampire's non-physical powers.
devotions.effect: The vampire projects an animate horror into the world. This creature is as ephemeral as any other illusion created with Nightmare or Obfuscate, but it can act independently of the vampire and follow simple commands. As a rule of thumb, it shouldn’t be bigger than a large human. As an extension of the Beast, the vampire maintains a mental link with the creature, and can channel her nonphysical Disciplines and Devotions through it. She can’t perceive what the creature does directly, but she has an impression of what it sees and hears, like a memory rather than direct observation. It can pass through walls and other barriers, and does not appear on video, audio, or any other kind of recording. It can also reflexively use the effect of Cloak of Night on itself. Any mortal who sees the living nightmare suffers a breaking point penalized by the vampire’s Blood Potency. A vampire can only create one living nightmare at a time.

devotions.name: Mania
devotions.summary: Overclock a victim's mind and inflict the Frantic Condition.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Empathy + Nightmare vs. Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire puts her victim’s brain into overdrive. He’s unable to concentrate on the same thing for more than a few minutes at a time, and finds himself picking up tasks just as quickly as he abandons them. He gains the Frantic Condition.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The Frantic Condition lasts for nights equal to Blood Potency
rollResults.failure: No spark sets off in the victim’s mind.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The Nosferatu goes off the rails, taking the Frantic Condition herself.

devotions.name: Mind Killer
devotions.summary: Seize a victim's reasoning center with sustained intimidation.
devotions.dicePool: Intelligence + Intimidation + Nightmare vs. Resolve + Blood Potency
devotions.requirement: The vampire must engage her victim in at least a full minute of conversation.

rollResults.success: Any action the victim takes with the Wits Attribute (including derived traits) is penalized by the vampire’s Nightmare dots. If it’s penalized below zero, he gains the Insensate Tilt on the first turn of any violent encounters.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim’s sense of cohesion is shattered, and he suffers the Confused Condition for the rest of the scene.
rollResults.failure: The victim is unfazed by the vampire’s intimidation tactics.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: Turnabout is fair play. The vampire’s attempts to shut her opponent’s mind down rebounds, and she gains the Confused Condition instead.

devotions.name: The Loathsome Foe
devotions.summary: Make one victim perceive the vampire as a person they deeply fear.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Intimidation + Obfuscate vs. Composure + Blood Potency
devotions.requirement: The vampire has The Familiar Stranger active on herself when she uses this Devotion.

rollResults.success: The victim perceives the vampire as a person he deeply fears. For as long as the Nosferatu remains in his presence, the victim can only apply half his relevant Attribute to resisted and contested rolls with the vampire involving fear (rounding up), and the vampire adds her Nightmare dots to Defense against the victim’s attacks. This illusion only applies to the victim. All others will perceive her as per The Familiar Stranger. This fear is supernatural, not an autonomic response; knowing it’s not real isn’t enough to dismiss it, and the illusion doesn’t even need to make sense in context. The person being imitated could even be deceased. However, unless the vampire knows who her victim fears, she has no control over her disguise, so it can help to do a background check before using this Devotion, or a bit of delving with Auspex.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim is overcome with terror, and loses a Willpower point.
rollResults.failure: The vampire’s disguise is scarier in theory than in practice.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: Not only does the vampire fail to scare her victim, the effect of the Familiar Stranger also shatters, and can’t be used for the rest of the scene.

devotions.name: No One Can Hear You Scream
devotions.translatedName: No One Can Hear You Scream
devotions.summary: Wrap a touched victim in a field that reduces every sound to a whisper.

rollResults.success: The vampire wraps his subject in a field of silence, preventing her from calling out for help or calling attention to herself. All sounds emanating from the victim, be they gunshots or screams, come out as a whisper.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The zone of silence lasts a scene.
rollResults.failure: The victim is as noisy as humans tend to be.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim is not only immune to the vampire’s Devotion, she gains a +3 on any action to call attention to herself, such as calling for help.

devotions.name: Pied Piper
devotions.summary: Turn music into a lure that rewards listeners for following it and leaves them Spooked.
devotions.effect: The vampire’s lure infects her victims with gnawing need to follow the music. Until the Nosferatu stops playing the tune, anyone who follows the sound to its source refreshes a Willpower point. However, if a victim accepts this “gift,” they also gain the Spooked Condition. The vampire can take no other instant actions while she plays her song, but she can apply Defense as usual.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be playing music.

devotions.name: Rampage
devotions.summary: Become a shadowy monster capable of killing many ordinary mortals at once.
devotions.dicePool: Strength + Brawl + Nightmare – number of mortals

rollResults.success: The vampire becomes a thing of shadow and terror, leaving her victims utterly defenseless. She kills a number mortals equal to successes on the activation roll. “Mortal” is anyone without a Supernatural Tolerance trait. For example, a Nosferatu can’t kill ghouls with this Devotion, even though their Blood Potency trait is zero. Furthermore, if any of her victims are armed with fire, they are exempt from her wrath.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: In addition to a tremendous body count, any surviving mortal in the scene who is not allied with the vampire is Beaten Down.
rollResults.failure: The vampire misjudges her human opponents and is in for a violent reply.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire is overcome with a profound remorse, suffering the Guilty Condition. Using Rampage, even on a failure, is a breaking point at Humanity 1 and higher.

devotions.name: Rising Tension
devotions.summary: Turn a watched victim's heartbeat into distracting dread.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Intimidation + Nightmare vs. Composure + Blood Potency
devotions.requirement: The victim must know he’s being watched or followed.

rollResults.success: The vampire seeds a subtle dread into her victim’s mind that makes him clumsy and easier to hunt. He gains the Shaken Condition. As long as the Condition lasts, or until the end of the scene (whichever comes first), he does not benefit from 10-again on Physical actions against the vampire, and suffers her Nightmare dots as a penalty to Perception.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim is so dazed by his sense of impending doom that the first action the vampire takes against him gains the rote quality.
rollResults.failure: If the tension is rising, the victim doesn’t notice.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim thinks the odds are with him. The vampire, however, suffers the Stunned Tilt.

devotions.name: Sign of Terror
devotions.summary: Store a Nightmare power in a Vitae-marked object as a supernatural trap.
devotions.cost: 1 Vitae plus one per extra charge
devotions.effect: The vampire marks an object with an eldritch sign written in Vitae, and imbues it with a power of Nightmare. When placed, the vampire chooses a Nightmare effect to attach to the object (paying all costs), whether the object is a book, door, or corpse. When viewed by anyone except the vampire herself, this power invades the victim’s mind as if the Nosferatu were present. The normal rules of that effect, including resistance, apply as normal. If needed, the Storyteller rolls the vampire’s dice pool. Each point of Vitae beyond the first causes the power to activate an additional time before the duration ends. However, an object cannot hold more charges than its Size (to a limit of five charges).

devotions.name: Terrible Will
devotions.summary: Harden the vampire against passive and active supernatural fear.
devotions.effect: The vampire is immune to the effect of Dread Presence, or similar passive powers of fear. Any rolls to use Nightmare against her are penalized by Resilience dots. Immunity to Dread Presence extends to enhancing any higher tiers of Nightmare.

devotions.name: This Awful Grip
devotions.summary: Bring monstrous strength to bear against objects and armor.
devotions.effect: The vampire’s muscles bloat as she brings her fists to bear on a target. When taking a Brawl or Weaponry action against an object, she ignores Durability equal to her Vigor dots. This applies to general armor in a violent encounter. This strength performance is always alarming. Anyone witnessing a successful use of this Devotion must make a reflexive Resolve + Composure: on a success, they swallow their fear; on a failure, they suffer the Shaken Condition. Unless this is an exceptional success, a victim must resist this fear each time the vampire uses the Devotion in the scene. As this aura of fear is a function of Dread Presence, the vampire can choose not to inflict it on chosen bystanders.

devotions.name: Wicked Grasp
devotions.summary: Distend the vampire's limbs into a terrifying, constricting grapple.
devotions.effect: The victim feels sheer terror as the vampire’s limbs wrap around him. If he has not already acted, his effective Initiative is treated as 1 for the rest of the turn. Once the grapple moves into contested rounds, as long as the vampire holds on, the victim suffers Nightmare dots as a penalty on all rolls to control the grapple.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must activate this Devotion on the same turn she initiates a grapple.

devotions.name: Wretched Bite
devotions.summary: Infect a bitten victim with supernatural despair.
devotions.effect: With his bite, the vampire sends his victim into a spiral of bleak sadness. Assuming she survives the wound, she gains the Despondent Condition.
devotions.requirement: The vampire inflicts damage with a bite in a grapple, or while feeding.

devotions.name: Nightmare Journey
devotions.summary: Project into the Primordial Dream and feed from dream forms.
devotions.effect: While using Twilight Projection, the div enters an unclaimed Chamber in the local Hive and gains a Dream Form capable of using Disciplines and physically interacting in Astral realms. Her body falls into true torpor and loses Blood Potency normally over time, but reaching Blood Potency 0 does not cause Final Death. In Dream Form she may feed from Dreamborn, Horrors, and other Dream Form travelers at one Vitae per two damage, travel through Astral realms normally, and return by reaching the entry Chamber and ending the Devotion, which also ends the torpor.

devotions.name: .22 Solid
devotions.summary: Increase Resilience's damage downgrading.
devotions.effect: Each incoming attack downgrades lethal damage equal to Resilience into bashing after armor. This stacks with Resilience's normal downgrade, so aggravated damage first reduced to lethal may then become bashing. It affects only new damage received while active.

devotions.name: Aegis of Defiance
devotions.summary: Defy mind-altering effects by acting contrary to them.
devotions.effect: While under a supernatural behavioral influence, the vampire names a contrary action and rolls against the original activation successes, or the attacker's supernatural potency when no roll was made. Winning permits the action and ends the influence unless it is applied again. If she detects a contested influence as it is used, this pool may replace her normal resistance and completely reject the effect.

devotions.name: Aura of Cursive Seduction
devotions.summary: Inflict enthralling Conditions when someone lashes out at you.
devotions.effect: When another character lashes out, the vampire may contest with this pool instead of lashing back. Success gives the vampire the Condition the aggressor would normally impose, while the aggressor gains Persistent Enthralled and Quelled. The vampire may also use it when initiating a Seductive Beast lash, using the normal Presence + Blood Potency pool.

devotions.name: BFFs
devotions.summary: Create the convincing facade of a long friendship.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Empathy + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency
devotions.effect: Each success creates one temporary dot of Allies, Contacts, or Mentor represented by the subject. Acting directly against the vampire becomes a Humanity or Integrity 4 violation, or 6 for indirect action; the vampire gains +2 on Social actions and Disciplines against the subject and begins Social Maneuvering one impression better. The subject can break free by spending Willpower equal to activation successes, or freely if the vampire attacks or seriously endangers them.

devotions.name: Call Me Maybe
devotions.summary: Create a temporary Herd.
devotions.effect: At a social gathering where the vampire has a Good or better Impression, each success becomes one temporary Herd dot, even above five. These dots cannot be used in the current or following scene and expire after one use or at chapter end. Only one reserve created by this Devotion may exist at a time.

devotions.name: Colossus
devotions.summary: Massively increase the power of your strikes.
devotions.effect: Each activation success empowers one Brawl or Weaponry attack. Empowered attacks ignore armor, knock ordinary victims back by Strength + Vigor yards or meters, knock them down, and inflict automatic bashing equal to Vigor in addition to normal damage. Against targets at least twice the vampire's Size, the strike instead ignores Durability and adds Vigor as automatic lethal Structure damage.

devotions.name: Hekireki
devotions.summary: Bank Vitae across turns before releasing an empowered attack.
devotions.effect: The vampire spends a full turn and Willpower preparing, without spending Vitae. On later turns she may bank Vitae up to her per-turn limit while doing nothing except defending without Dodge. The final Brawl or Weaponry attack gains +2 dice per banked Vitae, adds Celerity, may receive normal Willpower, adds Vigor as weapon damage, and becomes lethal even to Kindred. The vampire then suffers one bashing damage per Vitae banked.

devotions.name: Holdout
devotions.summary: Meld objects into your body.
devotions.effect: The vampire absorbs an inorganic object into her body. She may hold one object one Size below her, two objects two Sizes below, four objects three Sizes below, or a reasonable number of smaller items. Expelling one is reflexive and may come from any body part; forcing it into a target is a likely surprise attack using Protean + Blood Potency.

devotions.name: If You Can't Duck It
devotions.prerequisites: Four dots divided among Celerity, Resilience, and Vigor
devotions.summary: Bless an object with physical Discipline power.
devotions.effect: Blood smeared on an object grants Celerity as a modifier to its primary action, twice Resilience as added Structure, and Vigor as added Durability; a weapon so blessed deals lethal damage to Kindred. An object can carry only one use of this Devotion at a time.

devotions.name: In Vitae Veritas
devotions.summary: Send Discipline effects through Kindred lineages.
devotions.effect: The vampire immediately follows activation with a single-target Dominate or Majesty power against a Kindred. That power propagates through the target's blood sympathy; subtract each relative's steps of removal from the original successes, then resolve resistance independently. Resisted effects become contested with the same resistance Attribute plus Blood Potency. If the original power fails or gains only one success, the Vitae is wasted.

devotions.name: Kissing Cousins
devotions.summary: Make two vampires count as blood relatives.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Occult + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency, if unwilling
devotions.effect: Two vampires drink from each other and touch the activating Vitae, accepting normal bond and addiction risks. Either may contest if unwilling. Success makes the pair one step closer for blood sympathy; sacrificing one Humanity makes this permanent. Cross-clan targets can never become closer than four steps and cannot be made permanent. The user may be one target.

devotions.name: Knight Commander
devotions.summary: Inspire the Charmed to martial greatness.
devotions.effect: Choose affected allies. Each Vinculum stage toward the vampire grants +1 die to combat actions; Charmed allies ignore the first bashing or lethal point from each successful attack; Enthralled allies may spend one Willpower per turn without losing it. If the vampire exceptionally succeeds on an attack during the duration, affected witnesses also gain Inspired.

devotions.name: Manic Depression
devotions.summary: Force a victim through rapidly shifting emotional extremes.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Empathy + Nightmare vs. Composure + Blood Potency
devotions.effect: The vampire chooses Manic or Melancholic for the victim. Resolving either Condition replaces it with the other until the duration expires. Manic rewards repeating an action but penalizes switching and ends in exhaustion after failure; Melancholic penalizes actions made without Willpower, weakens Speed, Initiative, and Defense, prevents Willpower recovery, and resolves when the last Willpower is spent.

devotions.name: Natural Born Killer
devotions.summary: Read opponents intuitively and answer with gunfire.
devotions.effect: Activate on the first combat turn or in response to surprise. Add Celerity to detecting the ambush, add Auspex as well as Celerity to Initiative, and add Auspex as weapon damage to one successful Firearms or thrown-weapon attack that turn. It may be used only once per scene.

devotions.name: Preserved Blood
devotions.summary: Store your Vitae for later use.
devotions.effect: The vampire places one Vitae in a vessel, rolls, and on success may spend additional Vitae up to successes to determine preservation: one for a night, two for a week, three for a month, four for a year, or five indefinitely. Until that duration expires or it is consumed, the stored blood retains all Kindred properties; failure makes it inert.

devotions.name: Psycho Mantle
devotions.summary: Retaliate with a terrifying Predatory Aura.
devotions.effect: When another character lashes out, the vampire adds Nightmare to her retaliatory Monstrous Beast pool. Success inflicts both Bestial and Frightened rather than only Bestial.

devotions.name: Punching and Fucking
devotions.summary: Exert Majesty through an unarmed attack.
devotions.effect: After an unarmed attack deals damage, the victim contests that damage with Composure + Blood Potency as though it were Confidant. If the victim is Charmed and the vampire knows Loyalty, two Vitae may apply Loyalty instead. Damage dealt through this Devotion does not resolve Charmed or Enthralled.

devotions.name: Rapidity
devotions.summary: Modify another Devotion so it can activate reflexively.
devotions.effect: Assign Rapidity to a suitable instant-action Devotion when purchased; required Celerity equals that Devotion's Experience cost. Paying the extra Vitae makes the linked Devotion reflexive, but only one Rapidity-linked power may activate per turn. Complex speech or physical procedures are ineligible. Rapidity's Experience cost rises from one to three with its Celerity requirement and cannot modify a Devotion costing six or more.

devotions.name: Rock Is Dead
devotions.summary: Strengthen Awe while dulling rival presences.
devotions.effect: Spend Willpower with Awe. Other characters suffer the vampire's Majesty as a penalty to Dominate, Majesty, and Nightmare. A character whose Condition from one of those Disciplines currently affects the vampire is immune, and only one Rock Is Dead penalty applies at once.

devotions.name: Slow and Steady
devotions.summary: Slow a power to convert its Attribute dice into successes.
devotions.effect: Assign this to an instant Discipline power or Devotion when purchased; required Resilience equals the linked power's rating or Experience cost. Activation replaces the instant action with 30 minutes of preparation while any target remains present. The final pool omits the Attribute and converts its dots into automatic successes; resistance remains normal. Cost rises from one to three Experiences with required Resilience and cannot modify a Devotion costing six or more.

devotions.name: Straight Up Fucking Murderer
devotions.summary: Use a maneuver without sacrificing Defense.
devotions.effect: Activate whenever a maneuver would sacrifice Defense. The vampire keeps Defense while using that maneuver and may combine multiple such techniques by paying again for each, but cannot duplicate all-out attack or gain extra actions.

devotions.name: Strength of Empire
devotions.summary: Temporarily steal a physical Discipline from a Vinculum thrall.
devotions.effect: At any distance, each success removes one Discipline dot from a third-stage blood-bound vampire or ghoul and grants it to the user. Nonphysical Disciplines cannot exceed the subject's original rating; Celerity, Resilience, and Vigor may reach the combined ratings, at most one above the user's trait maximum. Normal activation costs remain. A stolen Devotion costs successes equal to its highest prerequisite and is available only while all prerequisites are held. Everything returns when the scene ends.

devotions.name: Sudden Strength
devotions.summary: Add Celerity to Strength while Celerity is active.
devotions.effect: After activating Celerity, add up to Celerity dots to Strength for all pools and derived traits that turn. Strength above the Blood Potency trait limit inflicts one bashing per excess dot at turn end; Vigor's normal Strength bonus does not count toward that limit. If Vitae-per-turn prevents simultaneous activation, Celerity may be paid on the prior turn and both benefits occur on the second.

devotions.name: Talking Circles
devotions.summary: Accelerate a conversation and cut off an opponent.
devotions.effect: Either interrupt another character's Social action with a Social action of the vampire's own, as Celerity can interrupt physical actions, or immediately advance one stage of Social Maneuvering without waiting for the current Impression interval.

devotions.name: The Gun Show
devotions.summary: Empower Majesty after a feat of strength.
devotions.effect: After committing to and succeeding at a feat of strength, the next Majesty activation in the scene gains Vigor as automatic successes. Neither the feat nor the Majesty roll may receive Willpower dice.

devotions.name: Tune In, Tune Out
devotions.summary: Suppress all but one sense to hyperextend the remaining one.
devotions.effect: Choose one heightened sense and suppress at least one of sight, hearing, touch, smell, balance, or taste. Each suppressed sense adds one die to the heightened sense, which also gains 8-again; actions using a suppressed sense suffer –5. Extreme stimulus overloads and removes the heightened sense, deals one bashing, and allows a Stamina roll each turn to recover it. The Devotion cannot be ended early.

devotions.name: Under My Skin
devotions.summary: Assume the appearance of someone under your Majesty.
devotions.effect: A victim carrying a Majesty-derived Condition from the vampire becomes the template for her shape. The vampire copies the victim's appearance and applicable physical Merits, may use up to two dots of the victim's Social Merits per Majesty Condition, and gains +2 per such Condition, maximum +5, to impersonate the victim or defeat scrutiny.

devotions.name: Under My Skin (Greater)
devotions.summary: Exchange appearances with a subject under your Majesty.
devotions.effect: Provides every benefit of Under My Skin and may instead make a willing subject look and act like the vampire, as though that subject possessed and used the basic Devotion on her.

devotions.name: Violent Coercion
devotions.summary: Coerce a subject into a task with the threat of violence.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Intimidation + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency
devotions.effect: Issue a clear task the subject can complete within one hour without realistically risking death or torpor. Success inflicts Coerced. Completing or refusing the task resolves it; refusal or waiting out the hour deals lethal damage equal to Vigor. A subject may carry only one Coerced instance from each vampire, and multiple instances cannot contradict one another.

devotions.name: Borrowed Talent
devotions.summary: Draws an actor's practiced talent into the director's production.
devotions.requirement: The vampire is reading the victim’s thoughts with Lay Open the Mind.
devotions.effect: The vampire temporarily steals a Social Skill Specialty the subject possesses. For the rest of the night, she can play the piano, sing opera, or whatever else her victim might have in their repertoire, depriving him of his special talent. However, the vampire must have at least one dot in the appropriate Skill or else the Specialty has no effect. If the victim has more than one Social Specialty in his traits, the vampire’s player chooses which to copy. The vampire can only use this Devotion once a night.

devotions.name: Dream Casting
devotions.summary: Finds the ideal performer through supernatural intuition.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have inflicted the Dominated Condition on the victim.
devotions.effect: The vampire imbues her subject with a simple social role he must play out over the course of the night, or until he resolves Dominated, whichever comes first. For example, she could force a subject to behave “hysterically,” or “as a lover scorned,” or even “like a fool.” Regardless of his acting talents, the victim will play his part with gusto, adding the vampire’s Dominate dots to any Expression rolls, and ignoring any untrained penalty. If the role involves a Specialty (Acting, Dancing, Singing, etc.) she can imbue her victim with that quality as well, but only if she possesses that Specialty herself, or if she stole one with Borrowed Talent. Fulfilling this role is a temporary Anchor; once a scene, the subject regains a Willpower for playing his part convincingly, or all Willpower if it leads to serious drama.

devotions.name: Spotlight
devotions.summary: Forces attention onto the chosen performer or scene.
devotions.requirement: The vampire afflicts her subject with the Touch of Shadow.
devotions.effect: The vampire inverts the muted effect of Face in the Crowd to make a person, place, or thing grab the attention of everyone nearby. Unlike Majesty, this isn’t a sudden charm offensive; it’s just that people can’t… stop… staring. It’s almost hypnotic. For the rest of the scene, the vampire exceptionally succeeds with a normal success on any action to call attention to her subject.

devotions.name: Talent Scout
devotions.summary: Recognizes hidden capability in a prospective performer.
devotions.effect: The Gottling expands their senses to pick up on a specific vice or vulnerability. This might be an addiction, a harmful secret, or even a hidden talent. The vampire can be fairly specific here (a heroin addiction, a secret lover, an abandoned music career, etc.), but the more specific the trait, the less likely they are to find what they’re looking for. If a person fitting this description comes within the extent of their Kindred Senses for heart beats, the Beast sends up a signal, and the vampire can then use Beast’s Hackles to pinpoint their victim.

devotions.name: Live Wire
devotions.summary: Channels stored electricity through a living target.

rollResults.success: The Shocker converts latent electricity in a living body into Vitae. For each success, she deals a point of bashing damage to a subject and takes half that amount in Vitae (rounding up). A victim can only be harvested this way once per night. Succeed or fail, this Devotion has no further effect on the same victim. For the purposes of the Voltaic Curse, use of this Devotion does not count as feeding from mortals.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire feels reinvigorated, regaining a Willpower point.
rollResults.failure: The vampire’s spark sputters.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire takes no sustenance, and causes painful burns, arrhythmia, or an epileptic episode in her victim.

devotions.name: Surgical Spark
devotions.summary: Applies exact electrical current to heal, disable, or stimulate tissue.
devotions.dicePool: Dexterity + Medicine + Surge – damage to be healed

rollResults.success: The vampire heals bashing damage on her mortal subject equal to successes, up to a limit of his Size. If the subject is experiencing cardiac arrest or arrhythmia, this Devotion also puts his heart back into its usual rhythm.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: Flash! The subject heals all bashing damage.
rollResults.failure: Fizzle.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: Flatline. The vampire compounds the emergency, and the subject now requires immediate medical attention.

devotions.name: Bones of the Manor
devotions.summary: Hardens a Domus and lets the Malocusian feel damage to it.
devotions.requirement: The Malocusian must be within her Haven.
devotions.effect: Once per scene, the vampire can re-direct damage meant for her onto her haven. For every point of damage the Malocusian would take, instead deal a point of Structure damage to the nearest piece of her haven, up to a maximum of the Spider’s dots in Resilience. Windows shatter and floorboards crack as blows hammer home, but the vampire’s flesh remains unmarked.

devotions.name: Steel Shadows
devotions.summary: Animates household defenses through the vampire's will.
devotions.requirement: The Malocusian uses The Familiar Stranger to create an illusion of an object, and must be within his haven.
devotions.effect: By lending a portion of his enduring nature to phantoms created with Obfuscate, the Spider can give them substance enough to affect the environment. An illusory hammer will pound a nail, and an illusory knife will cut meat. Steel Shadows is limited to making solid only simple objects no larger than the vampire himself, with no more than two moving parts. This effect can’t mimic chemical reactions. Objects have the same Durability, damage rating (if any), and Size as real examples of their kind, but only ever a single point of Structure, due to their ephemeral nature. Furthermore, solid as they might be, objects created with this power are not considered real for any supernatural properties they might otherwise have. A wooden stake created with Steel Shadows can still stab and cause damage, but will not render a vampire torpid if it pierces their heart. The same goes for a silver bullet and a werewolf. This Devotion is particularly deadly when used in conjunction with an Oubliette, due to the freedom with which the vampire may use The Familiar Stranger in that environment. A Hermit may only have (Blood Potency) instances of Steel Shadows active at one time.

devotions.name: Spotless
devotions.summary: Erases signs of violence or intrusion from the Domus.
devotions.requirement: The Malocusian must be within her haven.
devotions.effect: Whenever blood spills within the Malocusian’s home, it’s absorbed into the building, vanishing into tiling, wallpaper, and even thick carpeting without leaving a trace. A haven can store up to its dot rating in Vitae this way, and the vampire can spend that blood as if it were part of his own Vitae pool. While the haven can store blood indefinitely, it spoils somewhat being kept in timber and brick rather than within a vampire’s body. Blood stored for less than 24-hours counts as fresh, but after that time it counts as cold human blood.

devotions.name: Written Invitation
devotions.summary: Extends the threshold's welcome or prohibition through a written summons.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must write out the message himself, mixing whatever medium he uses with his Vitae, but the entire text does not have to be written in blood. The effect costs the same regardless of whether the vampire is jotting down a short note or painting a road sign. She then rolls the usual activation for Mesmerize, and spends any Vitae required for Iron Edict.
devotions.duration: The message retains its power to command for
devotions.effect: weeks equal to the vampire’s Blood Potency, after which it becomes mundane writing. The vampire scribes a piece of writing, traditionally a formal letter of invitation, and imbues it with his powers of Dominate. The next person to read the message must roll against the vampire’s successes on Mesmerize; if he fails, he must follow the message to the best of his ability, gaining any associated Dominate Conditions. This command can be as simple as a hand-lettered sign that says “Take Next Left” or as complex a set of directions through the woods to vampire-grandma’s house. After the words have been read once, succeed or fail, the power in them fades and the letters flake and crumble, as if from great age.

devotions.name: Body Colony
devotions.summary: Houses a living insect colony inside the vampire's corpse.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must inflict the Enthralled Condition on the victim.
devotions.effect: A colony of swarming insects slowly grows within the victim, causing a point of lethal damage per day, and will automatically emerge from the victim once their last Health box is filled with damage. Layers of euphoria and loyalty prevent the victim from feeling any discomfort while being eaten alive, but even a cursory examination of their body will reveal something is deeply wrong. Medical intervention can remove the nascent colony and prevent further damage, but will almost certainly require surgery. When in the victim’s presence, the vampire can spend an additional Vitae to force the swarm to exit, inflicting three points of lethal damage as they burrow through the victim’s skin to escape. To represent the Body Colony, use the rules for Swarm Form found on p. 114 of Vampire: The Requiem with the following addenda: The swarm has Health boxes equal to the damage it did to its host before emerging, and uses the vampire’s Animalism + Blood Potency as an attack pool. The swarm counts as a single entity created via Raise the Familiar, but its Stamina counts as 1 when determining that effect’s duration.

devotions.name: Dance of the Honeybee
devotions.summary: Communicates precise directions and intentions through hive movement.
devotions.requirement: Victims must be under the effects of Feral Infection.
devotions.dicePool: Intelligence + Expression + Animalism vs. highest Resolve + Blood Potency in group

rollResults.success: Rather than just steering her mortal and Kindred victims’ feral instincts, the vampire can put them onto more complex tasks. The vampire inflicts the Mesmerized Condition on all characters who failed to resist her Feral Infection, allowing her to issue commands rather than just directing their rage. Her victims will still be in a somewhat atavistic state, but they can comprehend simple orders. This Devotion does not work on werewolves.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The Queen’s authority is absolute. She can issue a command on the same turn as she mesmerizes her victims.
rollResults.failure: The Melissid’s victims continue to rage.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victims turn on their Queen with a single-minded purpose.

devotions.name: Honeycomb Heart
devotions.summary: Stores blood and hive members within a transformed body.
devotions.requirement: The vampire consumes the live larva of the insect she wishes to colonize her body.
devotions.effect: The vampire invites a colony of flying insects to nest inside her dead organs, typically from the order Hymenoptera. It takes a day for the swarm to become large enough to be of use, and it remains within the vampire for as long as she wishes. She can call forth the hive as an instant action, causing insects to emerge from her mouth and nose in a buzzing hoard. Outside her body, the swarm has Health equal to the vampire’s Stamina, and can attack her enemies similar to

devotions.name: Form of the Trickster
devotions.summary: Assumes the bloodline's elusive animal shape for flight, sabotage, or escape.
devotions.effect: Once a night, the vampire can transform into another person. They can be real or imaginary and of any gender, but they can’t have any qualities beyond the human limit. To create a flawless imitation of a real individual, the Rotgrafen must consume their blood within the same night. Otherwise, she takes circumstantial penalties on any Social rolls to fool those familiar with the original, as defined by the Storyteller. This Devotion can bestow Giant and Small-Framed (Chronicles of Darkness, pp. 47 and 49), and either level of Striking Looks, but Sanctity of Merits does not apply. However, it can also temporarily remove these Merits, in which case it does apply if the vampire permanently redefines her form. Transformation lasts until the vampire chooses to revert to her default, but she can only take on one new face per night. She can also spend a Willpower while resting in her Unmarked Grave to redefine her default body. Note that the vampire’s Physical Attributes and Skills remain the same, so she should be careful to play into her altered physique if she’s undercover.

devotions.name: Doctor's Orders
devotions.summary: After Lay Open the Mind succeeds, use Dominate within the subject's mind without eye contact, speech, or a shared language.
devotions.effect: While the Surgeon is accessing the thoughts of another, she can activate this Devotion to use her powers of Dominate directly within the mind of her victim, without the need for eye-contact or verbal commands. This also overcomes any language barrier between the vampire and her victim, but the Surgeon must still roll to inflict the Mesmerized Condition and pay any associated costs for other levels of Dominate. Victims view commands given to them with this power as coming from within their own mind, and so will go to great lengths to justify their actions, even if they make little sense.
devotions.requirement: The Surgeon must successfully use Lay Open the Mind on the victim.

devotions.name: Aegis
devotions.summary: Interposes supernatural command and endurance against an attack.
devotions.effect: Once per scene, the vampire can willingly suffer one point of aggravated damage to ignore all damage from a single source. She wills her Resilience to the site of the injury, condensing the harm into a single grievous wound. This Devotion functions against all sources of damage save sunlight, and cannot be combined with other effects of Resilience.

devotions.name: Beast Avatar
devotions.summary: Projects the authority of Animalism through the vampire's own body.
devotions.requirement: The subject must be the vampire’s ghoul
devotions.duration: As long as the animal remains a ghoul.
devotions.effect: The vampire uplifts an animal to sinister levels of intellect. When creating an animal ghoul, he can split a number of dots equal to Animalism among the creature’s Mental Attributes. These dots can be divided in any combination, but they cannot exceed the vampire’s own Attributes, or an upper maximum of five. If the vampire raises his Animalism later in the chronicle, new dots apply to the animal’s Attributes the next time he feeds it. Uplifted animals often develop strange quirks as the Vitae distorts and expands their minds, but the blood bond will keep them loyal. However, some might become Faithful (p. 147) given enough time and Vitae… This Devotion has no activation cost if the vampire knows the Beast King Merit (p. 109).

devotions.name: Blink
devotions.summary: Crosses a short distance too quickly for ordinary perception.

rollResults.success: The vampire issues a one- or two-word command without the need for eye contact. The victim must follow this command for turns equal to successes, or until completion, whichever comes first. If this command would put the character in obvious danger or provoke a breaking point, she can resist it by spending a Willpower, but otherwise the Ventrue’s Beast is too powerful to ignore. Unlike the usual applications of Dominate, the victim is fully aware of her body’s betrayal. A victim cannot be affected by this Devotion more than once per scene.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The Ventrue’s words cut through his victim with ease. He refreshes the Willpower he spent into this Devotion.
rollResults.failure: The victim shrugs it off.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: Not only does the victim ignore the vampire’s command, she’s immune to Dominate for the rest of the scene.

devotions.name: Dissociate
devotions.summary: Separates a subject from an emotion, memory, or immediate impulse.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must know the identity of at least one of the victim’s Touchstones.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Intimidation + Dominate vs. Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The victim detaches from her topmost attached Touchstone. This lasts the rest of the night or until the victim suffers a breaking point, whichever comes first. The vampire can only use this Devotion on a victim once a night.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim detaches from all of her Touchstones.
rollResults.failure: The Devotion has no effect.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire is confronted with the monstrousness of actively driving her Kindred away from Humanity. She suffers a Humanity 1 breaking point.

devotions.name: Feet of Stone
devotions.summary: Makes the vampire impossible to move against her will.
devotions.effect: The vampire applies her Resilience dots as a bonus to any action to remain standing upright as a result of force. If no roll is required, she always remains standing. This Devotion has no effect on rolls that strictly represent balance, like walking the edge of a building.

devotions.name: Hive Nexus Gestalt
devotions.summary: Coordinates several servants as one directed collective.
devotions.requirement: All members of the gestalt must be willing Kindred participants. The vampire must be touching each participant at the same time to activate the effect.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Intimidation + Vigor – number of subjects
devotions.duration: One night per Vitae spent at activation The vampires form a temporary hive mind, combining their mutual brain power into something greater than its parts: • Add up the characters’ collective Intelligences, to a limit imposed by the highest Blood Potency. For example, three characters with Intelligence 2, one of whom has Blood Potency 6, would treat their collective Intelligence as 6. • When a gestalt member makes a Mental Skill roll, use the highest Skill in the group. • All Willpower is pooled, and can be transferred between characters reflexively. If a member of the gestalt suffers a breaking point, all characters must roll to resist detachment if they are of equal or greater Humanity. Characters are considered to have the equivalent of a second step blood bond with each other for the duration, overriding any natural Vincula except a thirdstage bond. The Knight’s Example (Dominate •) Once nobility was linked with martial prowess and the ability to field an army, and many Ventrue haven’t forgotten that heritage. By setting the right example for her troops, the vampire can push them on to greater victories.

rollResults.success: The Ventrue barks a few orders or makes an inspiring battle cry. Allied characters who witness her iron glory gain her successes as weapon damage on their next violent actions. This lasts the scene or until the effect is used up, including if the attack is a failure. The vampire can only use this Devotion once per scene.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire’s followers gain an additional +1 on their weapon damage.
rollResults.failure: The vampire fails to inspire.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire demoralizes her troops, who suffer her Dominate dots as a penalty on their next attacks.

devotions.name: Hounds of Blood
devotions.summary: Sets animals or retainers on the scent of a blood-marked quarry.
devotions.requirement: The creature must have tasted the vampire’s blood at some point, whether as a ghoul or a familiar created with Raise the Familiar.
devotions.effect: The vampire touches the animal and activates this Devotion. The creature can now feed from mortals as a vampire can, using the system for the Assault (Vampire, p. 94), and can store Vitae equal to its Stamina. However, it cannot spend this Vitae, or add to its reserves if it’s a ghoul. Instead, the vampire can feed on the animal’s stored Vitae as if it were human blood or Kindred Vitae, depending on the victim. This does not inflict damage on the animal. The Ventrue is still vulnerable to blood bonds and addiction if she drinks vampire blood with this Devotion.

devotions.name: Knight's Example
devotions.summary: Strengthens followers who witness the Ventrue act according to command.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Intimidation + Vigor – number of subjects
devotions.effect: On success, allied witnesses add the activation successes as weapon damage to their next violent action during the scene; the bonus is spent even if that attack fails, and the Devotion may be used only once per scene. An exceptional success adds one more weapon damage. Failure provides no inspiration; dramatic failure penalizes the followers' next attacks by the vampire's Dominate dots.

devotions.name: Lord of Beasts
devotions.summary: Extends Animalism's authority across a broad gathering of animals.
devotions.effect: The vampire spends a Willpower to grant her new familiar a dot each of Celerity, Resilience, or Vigor, though she must have a dot of the relevant Discipline. Using this Devotion increases the number of Vitae needed to maintain the familiar’s existence by one for each Discipline granted.

devotions.name: Memory Palace
devotions.summary: Organizes memories into a protected, navigable mental structure.
devotions.effect: The Ventrue enshrines a memory in his blood, instantly placing it at the back of his mind. He doesn’t forget it — not exactly — but he can no longer think of it, protecting it from Auspex and other memory-retrieval powers. This memory is tied to a specific stimulus when the Devotion is first activated, be it a symbol, word, or some other visual or audio trigger. The vampire will recall the memory when the stimulus is encountered, even if that memory would have been suppressed or overwritten by supernatural means. The vampire can store a number of memories equal to Blood Potency at any given time.
