If Blood Potency decreases while the Ventrue is at her storage maximum, her player chooses which memory is unlocked. A stored memory can be up to a scene’s worth of information.

devotions.name: Messenger's Blessing
devotions.summary: Ensures a command or message reaches its intended recipient intact.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must use Entombed Command on her servant.
devotions.effect: Anyone who attempts to harm the vampire’s servant must first succeed on a reflexive Resolve + Blood Potency roll, penalized by the vampire’s Dominate dots. On a failure, they cannot attack, wasting a turn. This aura applies a number of times equal to the Ventrue’s Resilience. Once the total averted attacks against the messenger equal the vampire’s Discipline dots, or the sun rises (whichever comes first), the effect ends.

devotions.name: Rope-a-Dope
devotions.summary: Absorbs an opponent's pressure before turning it back.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Athletics + Resilience vs. Stamina + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire leeches vitality through any attacks inflicted upon her by the victim. Each time she takes injury from her opponent, she inflicts a stacking –1 modifier on his Physical actions as she drives him to exhaustion. At any time, or whenever this penalty would exceed –5, the vampire can wallop her opponent, gaining the penalty as a bonus on her attack. Once she attacks the opponent this way, the effect of this Devotion ends.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim also suffers the Drained Condition.
rollResults.failure: The victim feels a moment of enervation, but ignores it.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim is energized and takes a +2 on all attacks against the vampire for the rest of the scene.

devotions.name: The Message
devotions.summary: Embeds supernatural authority in a transmitted communication.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have inflicted the Mesmerized Condition the victim.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Expression + Dominate vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire curses/blesses her subject so that anyone he speaks with knows when he’s telling the truth; anything short of an exceptional success on a Subterfuge roll is treated as a failure. This effect doesn’t apply to lies of omission, and only comes into play in terms of what the subject believes to be a fact. If he really thinks the sky is green, it comes off as true. If you’re using the optional Malkovian bloodline (p. 96), this Devotion does not affect rolls penalized by their bane.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The effect applies to lies of omission, as others get a nagging feeling they haven’t heard the whole story.
rollResults.failure: The subject can tell as many lies or truths as she likes.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire curses herself with this effect for the rest of the scene.

devotions.name: Rumor of Dread
devotions.summary: Spreads fear through reputation before the vampire arrives.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Intimidation + Dominate vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The victim becomes a viral rumor mill. Anyone who encounters him experiences an effect similar to Dread Presence (Vampire, p. 135), but the epicenter of this fear is not the victim himself, but rather a rumor of the vampire’s design. Subjects will make flimsy justifications for where they heard this gossip, or use tortured logic to explain how they came up with/upon it. Similar to Dread Presence, witnesses cannot spend Willpower to argue against this rumor until the original victim departs their presence. For the rest of the night, they add the Ventrue’s Nightmare dots to any roll to spread it as gossip. The vampire has no control over where or how the subject will spend his night, though she can easily Dominate him into taking a particular route.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire’s rumor is particularly insidious. The duration lasts for his Blood Potency dots in additional nights.
rollResults.failure: The vampire’s rumor is a nonstarter.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The rumor is about the vampire, as determined by the Storyteller.

devotions.name: Soul Transfer
devotions.summary: Moves consciousness between prepared vessels under strict conditions.
devotions.requirement: The subject must be the vampire’s ghoul.
devotions.duration: As with Possession After successfully using Possession, the vampire spends a Vitae to send the possessed subject’s soul to her own body for the duration. All the usual rules of Possession apply, though the subject cannot return to his body without the vampire first vacating it. Treasured Servant (Resilience • •) A king must sacrifice for his people — that’s what it means to rule. Kindred using Treasured Servant make this literally true, allowing them to suffer harm that could incapacitate or kill a lesser creature.
devotions.effect: The vampire can accept a number of Health boxes of damage dealt to their ghoul equal to Blood Potency per scene. This damage can be negated with Resilience once the vampire receives it. She can absorb damage from any distance, and always knows when her servant takes a wound. However, unless she can see her ghoul, she won’t know the source, amount, or type of damage prior to accepting it.

devotions.name: Unseen Master
devotions.summary: Issues effective commands without revealing the commander.
devotions.effect: The vampire activates this Devotion when she succeeds in taking a victim’s body with Possession, creating a cloak around her soul while she controls her meat puppet. Anyone with supernatural powers of perception or revelation must engage in a Clash of Wills to reveal her presence, but even then, this only applies to active searching; passive effects simply fail. In addition, those who might be clued-in by odd behavior from the victim suffer the Ventrue’s Obfuscate dots on mundane Empathy rolls to notice any personality changes, or any other out-of-character behavior.

devotions.name: Voice in the Blood
devotions.summary: Carries a command through blood sympathy.
devotions.requirement: The vampire inflicts the Mesmerized Condition on a mortal, then feeds them a point of Vitae (included in the cost).
devotions.duration: The implanted command endures in the mortal’s
devotions.effect: blood for nights equal to Blood Potency, or until someone feeds from them, whichever comes first. The vampire implants an Iron Edict into the mortal victim’s blood. The first vampire to feed from the vessel can resist the command with Resolve + Blood Potency, contested by the number of successes the Ventrue gained when inflicting Mesmerized on the vessel. On a failure, the vampire consuming the imprinted blood gains the Dominated Condition. The Ventrue is immune to her own uses of this Devotion.

devotions.name: What's Mine Is Mine
devotions.effect: The vampire bleeds on an object and forms a pseudo–blood tie with it. The vampire is mystically aware if the object is disturbed from the last place she left it. She can maintain a number of connections equal to twice her Blood Potency and can remove a connection by creating another.
devotions.summary: Asserts supernatural ownership over a person, place, or object.

devotions.name: Aerial Cocoon
devotions.requirement: Hiding spot has the vampire's Size
devotions.summary: Use Unmarked Grave between concrete or metal walls as a protective cocoon.
devotions.effect: An alternate Unmarked Grave ( Vampire: The Requiem Second Edition, p. 139), for vampires adapted to living in the high rises of Singapore. This Devotion does not cost additional Vitae for the character to submerge herself into concrete or steel.

devotions.name: Bend Space
devotions.summary: Teleport to a visible or familiar place.
devotions.requirement: She must arrive in a space equal to or greater than her Size.
devotions.effect: Using this Devotion allows the Kindred to cross vast distances in an instant. For 2 Vitae, she vanishes from her current location and appears in any point she can see with unaided sight. A point on the horizon would qualify, but a remote location viewed through her data-tablet would not. For 2 Vitae and a point of Willpower, she may cross to any location she has previously visited, or has seen before. This transportation happens in scant seconds, allowing the masters of the Dominion to cross from station to station in heartbeats.

devotions.name: Memetic Menace
devotions.summary: Alter recordings of yourself to inflict Swooned or Frightened.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Expression + Nightmare or Majesty vs. Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.dramaticFailure: Onlookers see the vampire for what she is, a monster lurking in the night. Rather than be inspired to love or fear her, they are driven to hunt her down.
rollResults.failure: The camera captures her image and nothing else.
rollResults.success: Fear or desire wells up within the onlooker’s mind. He gains either the Swooning Condition ( Vampire: The Requiem Second Edition, p. 306) or the Frightened Condition (Vampire: The Requiem Second Edition, p. 304).
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The target cannot get the vampire out of his head, exchanging whichever Condition he would have gained for Distracted instead, which lasts for a number of days equal to the vampire’s Blood Potency. Night Without End

devotions.name: Best Served Cold
devotions.summary: Gain +3 to attacks against the person who harmed you.

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The fury of the Beast overwhelms the vampire and she enters frenzy.
rollResults.failure: The Beast accepts the pain and moves on.
rollResults.success: Fury rises within the vampire, empowering her actions against her enemy. She adds three additional dice to attack and damage against the enemy who harmed her. She may only enact her vengeful rage against one opponent at a time. This effect ends when the enemy is killed or defeated, or until the end of the chapter, whichever comes first.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: As a success, and the vampire also regains a point of Willpower.

devotions.name: Distant Control
devotions.summary: Issue commands and make Social rolls through a known target's mind.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be aware of her target’s location.
devotions.effect: With this Devotion, the vampire no longer needs to be physically present to issue a command or engage in social encounters. She speaks into the minds of her targets, and makes all social engagement rolls as if she were present. This ability persists until the end of a social encounter and does not cost 2 Vitae per action.

devotions.name: Wrack the Mind
devotions.summary: Inflict the Agonized Condition.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Intimidation + Dominate vs. Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The target shrugs off the vampire’s control, either fleeing the scene or becoming aggressive.
rollResults.failure: The vampire’s power fails to take hold.
rollResults.success: The target gains the Agonized Condition (above).
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: In addition to taking the condition, the target also suffers the vampire’s Blood Potency in bashing damage. Rain Falls

devotions.name: Between the Walls
devotions.summary: Fit through Size 2 spaces and add Obfuscate to ambush rolls.
devotions.effect: This Devotion allows a vampire to ooze into spaces as small as Size 2 and move through these cramped quarters at her normal Speed. When hunting, add her Obfuscate dots in bonus dice to any ambushes made from tiny, hidden spaces. Otherwise this allows her to use Unmarked Grave ( Vampire: The Requiem Second Edition, p. 139) in any space into which she can fit.

devotions.name: Blood Scenting
devotions.summary: Identify a target's Clan, Blood Potency, and Disciplines.
devotions.effect: The vampire scents the air near one of the Kindred and makes the listed roll.

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire leaps to whatever conclusion would be most socially inconvenient.
rollResults.failure: Scenting the target’s blood identifies them as one of the Kindred, revealing their clan at Storyteller discretion, but nothing more.
rollResults.success: She identifies her target’s clan, Blood Potency, and any Disciplines she may know.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: In addition to the benefits of the success, she also identifies any blood bonds the target may have, and any hidden Disciplines or Devotions she may currently be utilizing.

devotions.name: Flush Out
devotions.summary: Inflict Frightened and drive hidden subjects into the open.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Subterfuge + Nightmare vs Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.dramaticFailure: Instead of a flight reflex, the prey instead is driven to fight, reaching for common banes — fashioning swift torches and wooden stakes.
rollResults.failure: The prey resists the influence and stays hunkered down in their hiding place.
rollResults.success: The target gains the Frightened Condition and flees their hiding place to a location of the vampire’s choosing. If there are multiple targets the vampire wishes to terrify, roll against the highest Composure + Blood Potency of the assembled targets.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: As a success and also the victims suffer –2 dice to all attack actions against the vampire.

devotions.name: Vile Blood
devotions.summary: Make your blood poisonous to feeders and combatants.
devotions.effect: If being fed on by another vampire, the Kindred using this Devotion pays the cost and instead transforms her blood into acidic poison. Her target takes a lethal level of damage for every point of Vitae he would have consumed. In combat, after she has taken any levels of damage she may use this Devotion to force festering blood from her wounds, allowing her to inflict the Poisoned Tilt ( Chronicles of Darkness , p. 286) with any of her attacks.

devotions.name: The Give-and-Take
devotions.summary: Gift a vessel Physical Discipline dots while stealing Vice recovery.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must feed on the victim.
devotions.effect: As she feeds (with The Look or otherwise), the vampire recycles power back into her vessel. The victim gains two dots of the vampire’s physical Disciplines for the rest of the night, spending Willpower instead of Vitae when needed. However, for the same period, the vampire automatically steals any Willpower the victim might gain for fulfilling a Vice. The vampire does not have to be present to gain the Willpower.

devotions.name: The Look
devotions.summary: Turn exceptional emotional influence into psychic feeding.
devotions.effect: Once per subject in a scene, if the vampire exceptionally succeeds on a mundane roll to provoke emotion, whether positive or negative, she steals a point of Willpower from the victim and converts it to Vitae. If the victim has no Willpower to lose, he takes a point of lethal damage instead. If using this Devotion fulfills a Mask or Dirge, the vampire may choose to gain another point of Vitae instead of Willpower. Beloved with Blood Potency high enough to require Kindred blood for sustenance can use this Devotion to feed on humans, but only Vitae taken from Willpower is palatable.

devotions.name: The One That Got Away
devotions.summary: Become a sleeping victim's temporary ideal and Vice.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must feed on the victim while he sleeps.
devotions.duration: One night per dot of Blood Potency
devotions.effect: When the victim wakes, he’s convinced the vampire bears a physical or personal resemblance to the person of his dreams. The victim gains a new Vice of sacrificing (work, money, favors, etc.). In addition, the vampire has Exceptional Success on three successes instead of five on actions to incite the victim’s emotions.

devotions.name: The Pledge
devotions.summary: Pledge to a vessel, granting Social Merits and recovering Willpower through passion.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must feed on the victim.
devotions.effect: If the mortal consents (e.g., she can’t be blood bound or subject to Dominate, Majesty, or other forms of coercion), the vampire feeds, paying the activation cost as he does. Both characters gain the Promised Condition.

devotions.name: Infectious Bite
devotions.summary: Infect a mortal with the Nosoi blood sickness.
devotions.effect: With the expenditure of a vitae and a successful contested roll, a Nosoi may infect a mortal with his favored disease, even if this disease is not normally transmissible. Type 1 diabetes isn’t infectious, but his bite can permanently inflict it on a target. Drawback : The Nosoi has the Addicted Condition, which cannot be resolved by any means: an addiction to the blood of someone suffering from their favored disease. Additionally, Infectious Bite doesn’t exactly make Nosoi fun party guests. The bloodline closely guards the truth of this ability, rarely using it except to expand their dependent Herd.

devotions.name: Plague Doctor's Mask
devotions.summary: Use Touch of Shadow to mask blood-sickness symptoms.
devotions.effect: Plague Doctor’s Mask modifies a Nosoi’s Touch of Shadow. By spending an additional point of Vitae, she can mask the symptoms of a single blood-detectable illness within a target. If a mortal has more than one such malady, the Nosoi may spend additional Vitae to mask additional symptom sets. No opioid relieves pain more thoroughly than the Plague Doctor’s Mask. This power neither cures symptoms nor alleviates them; it is possible for a person to profoundly hurt themselves when they can’t feel pain from joints swollen by an autoimmune disease, for example, should they spend the scene running around. A doctor or other person who examines the mortal will be surprised to find clear eyes, a lack of fever, an even heartbeat, etc., unless they succeed on a Wits + Medicine roll assisted by appropriate equipment. The Mask can’t hold up to a CAT scan and won’t fool supernatural powers which provide assessments of health, but the Mask fools any unassisted Medicine roll as the observer’s eyes slide past obvious symptoms.

devotions.name: Tiny Guardian
devotions.summary: Bud off intelligent and loyal insect servants.
devotions.effect: Each Vitae spent creates one Size 0 insect or arachnid. The Nosoi can command this insect or arachnid as though using Animalism. The guardian is part of the Gangrel, and accordingly the Nosoi can perceive everything at the insect’s location. The guardian acts quasi-independently but according to the Nosoi’s desires; new commands can be given at any time, but the guardian responds to changes in circumstance with the Gangrel’s intelligence and a perfect understanding of her will. If a spider is sent to follow a stranger through her hospital who then leaves and gets into a car, the spider knows that the Nosoi wants him followed, and does so. There is no maximum range on these guardians; if the man being followed boards a plane, that spider may also board the plane and will not disintegrate due to range as with the merit Swarm Form. Drawback: Guardians are part of the Nosoi and sending them out into the world is potentially both visible and dangerous. For each guardian deployed, not only must the Gangrel spend one Vitae, but when the guardian is created, a finger joint on her dominant hand disappears. With one guardian created, the smallest joint on her pinky goes missing; with two, the smallest and second-smallest, and so on; those digits become whole again when the devotion ends. As the guardians are still part of the Nosoi, if they are destroyed, she takes 1 lethal damage. Lastly, the guardians must return by sunrise; she takes 1 lethal damage for each guardian she hasn’t drawn back into herself by night’s end.

devotions.name: City Attunement
devotions.summary: Touch the city to see through its eyes and enable other Scion Devotions.
devotions.effect: By spending a Vitae and resting one or both hands on a building exterior or paved street within the city, the Harbinger renews his link to Her. Most Harbingers do this upon exiting their havens nightly. Harbingers may not be linked to more than one city at a time. In the case of a metropolis, the Harbinger is linked to the greater metropolis and not a given neighborhood: She is not Fishtown, She is Philadelphia. All Scions of the First City may learn this ability at no cost.

devotions.name: Incriminating Evidence
devotions.summary: Search your city for evidence of a touched subject's wrongdoing.
devotions.cost: Varies; use of this devotion is tiring. The first use within a scene is free; additional uses cost 1 Vitae each.
devotions.effect: After touching a subject that night, the Harbinger uses Spirit's Touch outdoors and lets the city guide him toward physical evidence of that subject's wrongdoing. Each activation success provides one environmental clue. The power locates evidence rather than explaining the secret, bypassing locks, or identifying an exact door; Obfuscate causes a Clash of Wills. Repeated uses may narrow the destination but still incur their normal costs and risks.

devotions.name: Our Mother's Mind
devotions.summary: Seek and impede a quarry through your city.
devotions.effect: The Harbinger smears her Vitae onto her feet and walks barefoot through the City, following Her signs toward a single target. The player declares a target to the Storyteller in a short phrase, for example: “Randall the Gangrel” or “that mime I saw last night” or “the person responsible for the fire downtown.” The City guides the Harbinger with Her sounds and sights; the Storyteller is encouraged to lead her as with Incriminating Evidence. The surface thoughts of passersby leak into her mind in a traceable trajectory. Sirens wail to her left when she should turn. Motor oil trails up an exit ramp like a neon arrow. For every success, she is led her Blood Potency number of city blocks toward her target, following the city’s directions like a bloodhound on a scent. If the target leaves the city, she is led to where they exited. Upon failure, the Harbinger is aware she has failed; she receives no guidance from the City. In addition, the City acts to impede the Harbinger’s target: for every success, the target’s non-combat dice pools and Speed are reduced by 1 for the duration of the effect. Lights change against him and those sirens are a distracting wail which keeps him from noticing the Harbinger in pursuit. This devotion leaves traces of the Harbinger’s vitae on the ground, which may pose a danger to her from the city’s other denizens. Drawback: To perfect the City, the Scion must be willing to destroy imperfections at every personal cost. For each success, the Harbinger must temporarily sacrifice access to a level of Contacts, Allies, Retainer, or Resources. The Storyteller determines how access to these merits is temporarily lost and is encouraged to be creative: a Retainer hospitalized due to a car accident; bank accounts temporarily frozen due to administrative error or Police Allies jailed. The Scion regains access to these merits one week after use of this devotion. Players may choose not to utilize all their successes.

devotions.name: Shapeshifting
devotions.summary: Copy physical features from a vessel for a night.
devotions.effect: The Kindred can copy one small feature (e.g., facial features, hair color, birthmarks, voice, etc.) from a victim from whom they’ve fed. Each Vitae spent when activating the devotion allows the vampire to alter an additional feature. The Vardyvle cannot change their size to become taller or smaller to match the look of the victim. If they attempt to recreate or modify a body part which they don’t have, they can make it appears as if they have the organ. However, they cannot use it. After one night, the effect fades, and the vampire looks like her usual self. The Vardyvle does not immediately know how to act or talk like the person she is mimicking, and anyone who knows the person well will suspect there is something wrong. They might not know they are dealing with a doppelgänger, but the Vardyvle suffers –2 to Social rolls against people with close ties to the victim.

devotions.name: Ghost Skin
devotions.summary: Perceive and interact with ghosts during Twilight Projection.
devotions.effect: When activating Twilight Projection, the vampire can spend a Willpower to attune her form with ghosts, allowing her to see and physically interact with the dead. Treat her traits as the same as in her physical form. The vampire is ejected back to her body if she takes full lethal damage and meets Final Death if the damage is aggravated. By default, she can still only use Auspex in this form, but if she knows Pierce the Veil (below), she can spend a Vitae on activation of that Devotion to access other Disciplines.

devotions.name: Pierce the Veil
devotions.summary: Use Auspex to perceive ghosts and Willpower to affect them with Disciplines.
devotions.effect: The vampire perceives any ghost present within the extent of his Kindred Senses and knows its Rank with a reflexive Wits + Occult roll. He can see or speak to any wraith hidden in Twilight form (provoking a Clash of Wills if necessary). By default, he can only use Auspex on ghosts, but if he spends a Willpower at activation his focus is keen enough that he can use other Disciplines as well, but he is still limited in that he cannot physically interact with them.

devotions.name: Séance
devotions.summary: Force a ghost to Materialize at its Anchor.
devotions.dicePool: Resolve + Occult + Auspex vs. Resistance + Rank

rollResults.success: The ghost teleports to her Anchor if not already present and gains the Materialized Condition for the rest of the scene, which cannot be ended prematurely unless the ghost loses all Corpus boxes to lethal damage.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The Condition lasts the rest of the night.
rollResults.failure: The ghost refuses the call.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire inflicts the Open Condition on himself.

devotions.name: Null Space
devotions.summary: Use Vitiate without touch inside Lord of the Land or Oubliette.
devotions.cost: Half the Vitae spent on Lord of the Land or Oubliette (round up)
devotions.requirement: The vampire marks an area for the purposes of Lord of the Land or Oubliette
devotions.duration: One week per dot of Blood Potency
devotions.effect: An unwelcome visitor entering the area must spend a Willpower. If he does not or cannot, he gains the Beaten Down Tilt if violence breaks out. Once every 10 minutes, if she’s present, the vampire can spend a Vitae to force this choice again.

devotions.name: Flesh Form
devotions.summary: Consume a human body to imitate its appearance and voice.
devotions.effect: The Nhang becomes identical to her victim in both look and sound but does not necessarily gain the ability to adopt the person’s demeanor or attitudes without prior study. The Nhang’s transformation lasts until she decides to return to her original form. The Nhang must spend the Vitae cost to maintain the shape each night when she awakens or otherwise revert to her normal state. For each week the Nhang remains in her stolen form, the body ages by a decade. There is nothing she can do to prevent this, as the flesh she consumed decays inside her. The Water Serpent may retain the form long after it would naturally die based on the rate of aging, but she soon begins to look like a shambling corpse.

devotions.name: Water Hibernation
devotions.summary: Use Unmarked Grave while fully submerged in water.
devotions.requirement: The vampire is fully submerged in water.
devotions.effect: The vampire remains submerged under water without surfacing for as long as she desires. If the water evaporates or is otherwise removed, the Kindred is damaged, taking one point of bashing damage when uncovered. If the vampire is fully exposed, she becomes susceptible to sunlight.

devotions.name: Not So Special
devotions.summary: Suppress another vampire's Clan-specific Disciplines.
devotions.dicePool: Resolve + Occult + Vigor vs. Blood Potency + Stamina
devotions.effect: If successful, the victim cannot access a number of dots in the chosen Discipline per Vitae spent, starting with the highest level. This also affects associated Devotions. If a Discipline effect is already active, this provokes a Clash of Wills. The effect continues if the victim wins the clash, but he cannot activate the power again if it expires naturally. Conditions inflicted with a Discipline (e.g., Mesmerized) do not count as active effects.

devotions.name: Sea Witch's Gift
devotions.summary: Regain legs for an hour while ignoring the Nereid Bane.
devotions.effect: By spending a Vitae, a Nereid using this devotion sheds her tail for an hour and regains her lost legs. She may spend additional Vitae to continue the effect without being compelled to return to the water. Sirens are deeply uncomfortable on land, and the expenditures necessary for prolonged time ashore make it likely that, if forced to stay two-legged, she will become ravenously hungry.

devotions.name: Siren's Sweet Visage
devotions.summary: Conceal abnormalities and weaken resistance to persuasion or intimidation.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Empathy + Majesty vs. Blood Potency + Composure
devotions.effect: No matter how distended her body might be from human norms — jellied flesh no longer being pushed inward by deepsea pressure, skin so pale that even other vampires gasp — this devotion hides her abnormalities completely, functioning similarly to Familiar Stranger, except the Siren does not need to take on a visage other than her own. While using this Devotion, the Nereid also becomes strangely compelling, drawing attention to herself wherever she goes. Those affected by Siren’s Sweet Visage suffer a die penalty equal to her successes when resisting her Persuasionor Intimidation-based Social maneuvers.

devotions.name: Hounds of Hell
devotions.summary: Hone the Predatory Aura through the Kerberos Beast.
devotions.effect: When pursuing the Beast's aspect after using Predatory Aura, replace the usual +2 bonus with Blood Potency and add the relevant Three Heads of Kerberos rating to lashing-out pools.
devotions.source: Onyx Path Blog: The Jaws of the Beast

devotions.name: Ba
devotions.summary: Wear a shadow and become a Twilight being.
devotions.effect: Become immaterial while touching a shadow at least your Size. Move at half Speed along solid objects; only fire, sunlight, Pseshkf, ephemeral attacks, and effects that harm ephemera can affect you, but harmful effects inflict two extra lethal damage.
devotions.source: Onyx Path Blog: The Shadow and the Asp

devotions.name: Iteru
devotions.summary: Slip between contiguous shadows and empower a Dodge.
devotions.effect: Emerge anywhere along the same patch of shadow; once per scene a Dodge using Iteru gains rote quality.
devotions.source: Onyx Path Blog: The Shadow and the Asp

devotions.name: Pseshkf
devotions.summary: Coat an object in frozen darkness and wield it through Tyet.
devotions.effect: Add Blood Potency to Durability and Vitae spent to Structure. Coated weapons gain +1 weapon rating against physical targets and Blood Potency weapon rating against noncorporeal targets.
devotions.source: Onyx Path Blog: The Shadow and the Asp

devotions.name: Tyet
devotions.summary: Expel and shape a cloud of supernatural darkness.
devotions.effect: The cloud extends Blood Potency yards per Vitae spent; the Khaibit may shape all connected shadows to distract or deceive.
devotions.source: Onyx Path Blog: The Shadow and the Asp

devotions.name: Udjat
devotions.summary: See perfectly in total darkness and ignore blindness from injury or supernatural powers.
devotions.effect: Spending Vitae reveals spirits, Strix, angels, and other Twilight beings and prevents Strix possession for the scene. The first clear manifestation of Obtenebration forces witnesses to roll Resolve + Composure or gain Shaken.
devotions.source: Onyx Path Blog: The Shadow and the Asp

devotions.name: Bitter Blossom
devotions.summary: Turns a victim's regret into an immediate supernatural affliction.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Empathy + Nightmare vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire inflicts the Depressed Condition on her victim. If she’s fed on this subject with her bloodline gift, or has mundane knowledge of his past failures, crimes, and sins, she can choose to focus this emotional state on any such event she’s aware of. Otherwise, the victim will fixate on a plausible incident in his recent past that could serve as the source of his mood. The vampire can also use this effect in tandem with Lay Open the Mind, tying the Condition to a memory the victim would have otherwise treated as neutral or positive, tainting it with negativity that was never there before. Alternatively, she can fish for an unhappy memory, dredging up the Guilty Condition to go along with Depressed.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: Depressed lasts for nights instead of hours.
rollResults.failure: The vampire fails to make the victim any more miserable than he already is.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire’s power backfires. She gains the Depressed Condition.

devotions.name: Sense the Sin
devotions.summary: Reads the grief and guilt carried by a target.
devotions.cost: Varies; the first use in a scene is free, but subsequent uses in the same scene cost 1 Vitae each.

rollResults.success: The vampire can tell how much Humanity or Integrity a victim retains. Activated alone, this power can only target a single subject at a time, but if the vampire knows Dread Presence, he can use that Discipline to bring his victims’ worst sides closer to the surface, then use this effect to pick out the person with the highest or lowest trait in a crowd. Each Suicide King experiences this information differently. One might see his subject being slowly covered in an amount of bile proportionate to their misdeeds; another may catch a whiff or brimstone or have to watch as her subject’s flesh begins to rot. At Storyteller discretion, Sense the Sin can be used on other supernatural denizens of the night, but successfully interpreting things like a werewolf’s Harmony or a changeling’s Clarity may require a successful Intelligence + Occult roll.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire’s insight is acute. He gains a symbolic vision of his subject’s most recent breaking point. Situation Modifier The vampire has fed from the victim in the past night. +1 The vampire knows the victim’s Mask and/ or Dirge (or equivalent). +1 The victim has no remaining Willpower. +2 The victim is under the effects of the Guilty or Depressed Conditions. +2 The vampire witnessed the victim enduring a breaking point in the same night. +3 The victim has regained Willpower through the use of one or more Anchors in the past 24 hours. –2 The vampire has the Dependent Condition toward the victim. –3
rollResults.failure: The vampire fails to see how the subject transgressed.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: No one could be that innocent. The vampire gains the Obsession Condition for the rest of the night, focused on uncovering the subject’s (real or imagined) misdeeds.

devotions.name: Tearstained Vision
devotions.summary: Draws prophetic insight from sorrow and tears.
devotions.effect: For the duration, the vampire can see a lingering aura of negativity inherent to the objects around her. She might perceive certain objects bleeding in a room where someone experienced a nasty break up, or see black flames dancing over everything touched by a murderer in a crime scene. The more negative the associated emotion or act, the more intense the imagery. The vampire gains no insight into what caused this aura unless she uses The Spirit’s Touch, but she gains the 8-again quality on that Discipline if the object was associated with a breaking point.

devotions.name: The Yawning Void
devotions.summary: Overwhelms a target with the emptiness behind unresolved grief.
devotions.requirement: The victim must have the Depressed or Guilty Conditions.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Intimidation + Nightmare vs. Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The victim is thrown into a deep despair, gaining the Self-Loathing Condition.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim is so devastated that they also gain the Broken Condition for the rest of the night.
rollResults.failure: The vampire doesn’t invoke the victim’s self-hatred.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire’s victim instead feels a deep sense of self-satisfaction over having endured past trials. They regain a point of spent Willpower.

devotions.name: Incite
devotions.summary: Intensifies a chosen sensation until it becomes impossible to ignore.
devotions.cost: Varies; the first use in a night is free, but subsequent uses cost 1 Vitae each.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Medicine + Celerity vs. Stamina + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The victim gains the Inflamed Condition. If the vampire feeds from a mortal character with Inflamed, she gains one additional Vitae without inflicting lethal damage.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: Inflamed lasts the rest of the night.
rollResults.failure: The victim feels a slight tingling.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim is immune to les arts licencieux for the rest of the night.

devotions.name: Induce
devotions.summary: Creates an intense sensation without an ordinary physical cause.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have inflicted the Inflamed Condition on the victim.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Medicine + Majesty vs. Stamina + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire transforms her victim’s general overload of sensation into a single intense one: nausea, arousal, soreness, itchiness, a taste, etc. This bestows the Distracted Condition, which fades when the character ends or resolves Inflamed. As long as Distracted lasts, the vampire gains double the Vitae from a mortal victim without inflicting additional damage. If the vampire’s Vigor dots are higher than Celerity, the Inflamed Condition keys off that Discipline instead.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The cost of the Devotion is refunded.
rollResults.failure: Was that a breeze?
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire suffers one of the above Conditions herself.

devotions.name: Inure
devotions.summary: Hardens the vampire against a repeated source of extreme sensation.
devotions.dicePool: Strength + Medicine + Majesty vs. Stamina + Blood Potency (if unwilling)
devotions.effect: Used on a vampire or a mortal without Inflamed, the Duchagne mutes her subject’s senses. He gains a bonus equal to the vampire’s Resilience dots on all Resistance rolls to resist overstimulation, whether from taste, touch, sight, smell, or sound. This includes rolls to resist frenzy. This does not protect him against damage; it only increases his ability to endure pain or discomfort. Used on a mortal with the Inflamed Condition, the Duchagne instead stretches out his capacity for providing blood. She the vampire’s Resilience dots to Stamina for the purposes of preventing the Inflamed Condition from resolving.

devotions.name: Night Life
devotions.summary: Temporarily restores living vigor and social warmth to the corpse.
devotions.requirement: The vampire activates the blush of life and spends an additional Vitae (included in the cost).
devotions.effect: The vampire gains fine control over normally involuntary physical responses. She can cry, blush, sneeze, give herself goosebumps, dilate her pupils, experience orgasm, or even turn blue from a seeming lack of oxygen. The list goes on. This reaction requires only a thought, and the vampire’s body will follow through. If this is intended to deceive or add depth to a performance, any related Expression or Subterfuge rolls gain the 9-again quality.

devotions.name: Taking the Measure
devotions.summary: Reads a subject's age, health, and physical history through close observation.
devotions.requirement: The vampire successfully uses Uncanny Perception on a human victim in the same scene.
devotions.effect: The vampire adds her Auspex dots to Humanity to negate the penalty on any Social roll to relate to the subject. If the victim had the Swooning Condition toward the vampire when she activated this Devotion, the effect lasts the night. Story Seed: Silver and Gold Despite a certain symbolic duality, the Erzsébet have an icy relationship with the Star-Crossed (p. 52). Maybe Electrum could cure a Cavalier’s bane, but so far, it hasn’t. This has led to conflict, as the Custodians get twitchy when others ask too many questions about their collections. Some Erzsébet have offered to rent Purities for experimentation, but no Sophist has been willing to offer up a loaner. A few Withered wonder if they could be “purified” themselves, but this idea (suspiciously, in the Erzsébet’s eyes) is a non-starter for the Star-Crossed.

devotions.name: Essence Vitale Absolue
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: The essential Ortam ability can be crafted with Vitae from any vampire, creating an intoxicating scent that ensnares minds as it delights them. Smelling Essence Vitale Absolue is the same as having tasted the donor vampire’s blood. It can establish a Vinculum, though it can’t increase an extant one, and it provides no sustenance. Any mortals taking in the scent are helpless against it, but Kindred reflexively resist with Resolve + Blood Potency – Ortam, shaking off the would-be bond with a successful roll. Essence Vitale Absolue is the only Ortam recipe that can be combined with others; this requires the vampire to spend an additional Vitae per dose, but he still only needs to make one roll.

devotions.name: Quicksilver Grace
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: A subtle, promising scent that builds anticipation, keeping the wearer on a knife’s edge of awareness — and dis tracting everyone else. Anyone wearing this scent gains a +5 on Initiative results, and dodge actions gain the 8-again quality.

devotions.name: Shadow's Eyes
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: This recipe creates a sharp, arresting fragrance that awakens the mind to all the little details it might otherwise miss. Anyone wearing the scent enjoys the benefits of the Trained Observer Merit at three dots and can pierce supernatural powers of stealth if they achieve an exceptional success on a Perception roll. Characters who already have Trained Observer at three dots gain a further 2-die bonus.

devotions.name: Tiger Musk
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: A thick, intimidating odor that tells man and beast alike a predator is in their midst. Anyone wearing this scent enjoys the rote quality on all rolls involving the Animal Ken and Intimidation Skills, as long as the target of these actions can smell them.

devotions.name: Authority for Lords
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: A powerful, domineering scent that’s impossible not to notice. This fragrance overpowers minds, making them subservient to the bearer. Reduce the number of Doors the wearer needs to bypass during Social maneuvering by two for anyone who can smell her, and increase her impression level by one, as even the most demanding requests seem reasonable to those under the influence of this scent.

devotions.name: Fond Absence
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: Barely smelling like anything at all (perhaps a hint of poppies), this fragrance isn’t meant to be worn, but rather to be deployed like a weapon. Any mortal who breathes in Fond Absence for more than a few seconds will enter a fugue state, completely forgetting they ever saw the wearer over the course of the scene, filling in the blanks as best they can. This inflicts the Amnesia Condition. Exposed Kindred characters must make a successful Wits + Composure roll to detect the threat and cease breathing before it can affect them; otherwise, they are affected as a human would be.

devotions.name: Haunt's Spite
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: This noxious, cloying odor is meant not to attract, but rather to repel. Anyone except the wearer who is exposed to Haunt’s Spite gains the Shaken Condition, centered on the person or area that’s the source of the scent. Kindred characters can resist with Composure + Blood Potency – Ortam to control themselves, but will still suffer a –1 to resist fear frenzy while they remain in the scent’s presence.

devotions.name: Serpent's Enticement
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: One of the Perfumers’ most popular creations, this sweet, enticing scent lingers behind the wearer, beckoning those who smell it to follow in their wake. Serpent’s Enticement inflicts the Swooning Condition on anyone exposed to it for more than a few seconds. This lasts the rest of the night. Kindred characters can resist with Composure + Blood Potency to shake off the effects, but still suffer a –1 to all further Composure-based rolls while exposed, even if the resistance roll is successful.

devotions.name: Bold Statement
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: A brash and powerful odor, the wearer of this scent seems unstoppable to all in sniffing distance. When she deals damage to someone who can smell her, she can choose to inflict the Beaten Down Tilt on her victim. Kindred can end the Tilt by simply ceasing to breathe, but most humans have no such recourse.

devotions.name: Marble Confidence
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: A fresh, earthy fragrance that boosts the wearer’s confidence and shields his mind from harm. Anyone wearing this scent enjoys the benefits of the Indomitable and Iron Will Merits. If the wearer already possesses these Merits, their effects are enhanced: double the bonus from Indomitable and/or apply the rote quality on contested rolls for Iron Will.

devotions.name: Savage Exemplar
devotions.summary: An Ortam recipe distilling a Discipline's resonance into supernatural perfume.
devotions.effect: Perhaps the most dangerous scent crafted by the Gulikan, Savage Exemplar smells of fresh blood and concen trated fury. A vampire who inhales this scent immediately enters frenzy as if they were riding the wave. However, when this frenzy ends, they gain the Lethargic Condition. Humans and creatures not prone to frenzy who are exposed to Savage Exemplar gain the Fired Up! Condition, below.

devotions.name: Face Lift
devotions.summary: Reshapes appearance with predatory precision.
devotions.effect: The vampire can superficially alter her face and limbs. She can smooth out asymmetry, mold her hair into a style that won’t shift, render her features softer or brighter or more lifelike, or even alter colors. Some Widows create more avant garde alterations outside the human baseline, like fingers with no nails, feathers instead of hair, or skin tones that would be impossible without extensive tattooing. As long as this effect lasts, the vampire adds her Protean dots on any Presence action to establish a first impression and exceptionally succeeds on three successes instead of five. Fashionistas can also bestow this effect on clothing, spilling the cost above on a garment or garments. In this way, they can bestow their fashion sense on allies — and sometimes, victims. Note that the vampire can’t use this Devotion to alter herself so much that this effect would serve as a disguise; she’ll always be somewhat recognizable to those who know her, though creative use of Face Lift might convince someone she has a sibling or an uncanny double.

devotions.name: Dressed to Kill
devotions.summary: Turns clothing and presentation into part of a lethal message.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have succeeded in styling his outfit. This requires Wits + Crafts roll and spreading the cost above over the garment. The effect lasts until the end of the night or until the vampire uses it, whichever comes first.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Expression + Majesty vs. Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The victim suffers the Insensate Tilt ( Chronicles of Darkness, p. 285).
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim also loses a point of temporary Willpower.
rollResults.failure: The distinctive outfit grabs attention, but doesn’t impede reaction.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The Fashionista is too notable, and his mark reacts explosively, either to defend himself or to flee from approaching death with a 5-die bonus.

devotions.name: Cursed Fiefdom
devotions.summary: Makes the Nelapsi's feeding territory itself carry the weight of her legend.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must spread Vitae around the area she wishes to claim, marking gateways, exits, and major landmarks. Six Vitae can mark a condominium or apartment building, nine can mark a mansion or large estate, and twelve can mark a small town or downtown center. This marking can be spread over multiple nights, but the vampire must spend every day asleep in the location until the work is complete. The Vitae is absorbed into the areas marked, becoming invisible to Kindred senses.
devotions.duration: One week per dot of Blood Potency, but the effects
devotions.effect: of this Devotion only end when the vampire leaves her territory after the duration expires. Once complete, denizens within the bounds of the Cursed Fiefdom find their surroundings imbued with the glorious allure of Majesty. All residents gain the Delusional Condition, believing they live in perfect harmony and peace despite any evidence to the contrary, be it scenes of horrific violence or macabre scenery. They can resolve this Condition the usual way or by moving away from the Fiefdom, but this requires spending a point of Willpower and succeeding on a Resolve + Blood Potency roll, penalized by the vampire’s Majesty dots. On a failure, each subsequent attempt to leave takes a further cumulative –1 modifier, to a limit of –5. Interlopers perceive the Fiefdom through the lens of Nightmare’s otherworldly terror. Any niceties or luxuries are ignored or forgotten: Unwelcome guests gain the Frightened Condition if they step foot in the territory, unless they succeed on a Composure + Blood Potency roll penalized by the vampire’s Nightmare dots. Each success grants an hour of time before they must roll again. On an exceptional success, they can remain for the rest of the night without fear. The Nelapsi can use Majesty and Nightmare powers reflex ively and at any distance while within her Fiefdom. If another vampire resides in this area already, she can attempt to lash out and break this effect before it forms, taking any bonus she might have from Feeding Grounds. For this reason, Nelapsi are careful where they put down roots, or purge undesirable Licks from their preferred territories.

devotions.name: Purification
devotions.summary: Bind a living mortal's Purity into a repeating 24-hour stasis and harvest Electrum from lethal harm dealt to that Purity.
devotions.cost: 1 Vitae and 1 Willpower to establish; 1 Vitae each week to maintain
devotions.effect: The Star-Crossed anoints her subject’s throat with Vitae, painting an unbroken ring around the neck. She then spends a Willpower and anoints his forehead with another daub of blood. From that point onward, the new Purity’s body is locked in a 24-hour biological time loop. The subject’s body always returns to the exact condition at the end of the night, effectively pausing the progress of aging and any diseases. A Purity heals all wounds she’s acquired at the end of her daily cycle, even if she’s killed. A Purity bearing a wound when the cycle began will regain it at the beginning of each reset if it healed in the meantime. In addition, a Purity’s mental processes are permanently beset by an intense sense of déjà vu. He suffers from a persistent form of the Confused Condition, which cannot be resolved without exiting the loop, becoming a ghoul, or receiving the Embrace. Purity characters take a Beat whenever this endless mental fog causes them significant embarrassment. This effect must be upkept once a week with another anointment. Failure to do so will cause all the time the Custodian paused to rapidly advance upon their Purity within a few minutes. A vampire can have a number of Purities equal to Blood Potency, but any she has the Dependent Condition toward do not count against this limit. Feeding on vampire blood ends this effect.
devotions.requirement: The subject cannot have any level of blood bond to a vampire and must be mortal (e.g., not a ghoul).

devotions.name: Drowned in the Abyss
devotions.summary: When successfully resisting a supernatural power, reflect it back upon its user.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must successfully resist an effect with Silence of Depths.
devotions.effect: The effect is the same as Silence of Depths, except that if the Xiao wins the contested roll to resist, she reflects the power back upon the aggressor. The originating character is subject to all the effects of a regular success of whatever power they were attempting to use on the Xiao, with her as the focus of any Conditions such as Charmed or Frightened. T wo Sides of a Bloody Coin Nothing prevents Apostates from learning Kingjan or Ascended from learning the Heart’s Echoes. In theory, a single Xiao character could have both. However, Storytellers are encouraged to keep in mind the raw hatred and deep philosophical differences between the two groups. Careful thought should be given to the circumstances that would lead to any character possessing both sets of Xiao powers. That said, a character from one side attempting to gain knowledge of the other could be an excellent focus for a story in and of itself.

devotions.name: Ripples in Still Water
devotions.summary: Recognize supernatural emotional manipulation and, with enough successes, identify its source.
devotions.effect: The vampire gains a heightened awareness of her own emotional state. Whenever she resists a supernatural power meant to manipulate her emotions (Majesty, Nightmare, etc.), if she fails the contested action but achieves at least one success on the roll, she becomes aware that she’s being manipulated. If she wins the contested action to resist, she also becomes aware of the source of the influence if it wouldn’t normally be obvious. Note that this knowledge does nothing to counter the effects of a power, but it may grant some leeway in how the vampire reacts to it.

devotions.name: Silence of Depths
devotions.summary: Add Majesty or Nightmare to resistance against emotional supernatural powers and to attempts to break Awe or Dread Presence.
devotions.effect: Whenever the vampire is the victim of a supernatural power that would alter her emotional state, she can activate this Devotion to add Majesty or Nightmare to the resistance roll, assuming she’s aware of the attempt. Alternatively, she can add this Discipline as a bonus to lashing out to break effects like Awe or Dread Presence.

devotions.name: As I Do
devotions.summary: Compels observers to mirror the vampire's poised behavior.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must perform the same action (i.e., with the same dice pool) that the subject is about to attempt.
devotions.effect: The vampire can activate this Devotion during any physical action. Doing so grants a bonus equal to Blood Potency to anyone attempting the same action in the scene on their next turn, provided they saw the vampire’s original action.

devotions.name: Beautiful but Deadly
devotions.summary: Uses supernatural beauty to disrupt an opponent's next physical action.

rollResults.success: The victim’s concentration is shot. He takes successes as a penalty on his next Physical action equal to successes.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The penalty applies for two actions.
rollResults.failure: The victim appreciates the vampire’s beauty but isn’t dissuaded.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire’s perfection misfires and sends her subject into a destructive rage. He takes the 8-again quality on his next violent action.

devotions.name: Drain
devotions.summary: Steals Social Attribute dots while feeding.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be feeding on the victim.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Empathy + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire reduces the victim’s Social Attributes by one dot for each Vitae taken, to a maximum of her own Majesty dots. Attributes cannot be reduced below one. Reducing Composure does not remove Willpower points, but it does reduce the victim’s maximum capacity for the duration. The vampire also gains one of the drained dots for the scene, but she may only possess one stolen dot at a time regardless of how many individuals she’s drained.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The effect lasts the night.
rollResults.failure: The vampire isn’t strong enough drain the victim’s essence.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim’s soul turns the tables on the vampire. He gains the point of Willpower spent to activate this Devotion and the vampire gains the Distracted Condition.

devotions.name: Haymaker
devotions.summary: Launches a struck opponent backward with Vigor.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have successfully attacked the victim with a Strength + Brawl action.
devotions.effect: The vampire hits her opponent with such intense concussive force that he goes flying. For each success on the attack roll, the victim is thrown back a meter. He takes an additional (Vigor) dice of damage if he hits something hard: bashing if it would break and absorb some of the force and lethal if it wouldn’t. The victim is considered Knocked Down if this damage exceeds his total Stamina (Chronicles of Darkness, p. 285). If the vampire doesn’t have enough Blood Potency to use this Devotion in a turn, she must spend a Vitae the turn before.

devotions.name: Hurts So Good
devotions.summary: Converts nearby pain into a Majesty bonus.
devotions.requirement: Someone in the scene must be suffering wound penalties.
devotions.effect: The vampire draws on the pain around him, using it to boost his supernatural power. Apply the highest wound penalty or modifier resulting from pain (such as a Tilt) present in the scene as a bonus to uses of Majesty. This does not apply to the vampire’s own wounds.

devotions.name: Hysterical Strength
devotions.summary: Grants a brief free active use of Vigor in mortal peril.
devotions.effect: Whenever the vampire finds herself in a life-or-death situ ation, for turns equal to Blood Potency, she can use a single active effect of Vigor for free. As a rule of thumb, situations that might invoke this Devotion could be those that provoke fear frenzy with a severe penalty, or that could cause detachment through inaction. The Storyteller is the final arbiter of when this Devotion can come into play.

devotions.name: Instant Superstar
devotions.summary: Inflicts Charmed through eye contact without a roll.
devotions.effect: If the vampire establishes eye contact with a victim, she can use the effect of Confidant on him without rolling. It simply works, and there’s nothing the mark can do about it. However, the Charmed Condition ends in an hour, and the victim will feel a bit disgruntled about anything untoward that might have happened, even if he doesn’t resolve the Condition.

devotions.name: Kingfisher
devotions.summary: Snatches a victim from above and retreats before observers can react.
devotions.effect: The vampire dives off a high place, grabbing a victim and bouncing back up to another high point, faster than the eye can follow. If numbers are required, this Devotion allows the vampire to fall up to (Vigor * 3.5) meters without taking damage and move back up the same distance she fell while carrying her victim with her.

devotions.name: The Hook
devotions.summary: Finds and draws in exactly the kind of person the vampire needs.

rollResults.success: The vampire specifies a type of person, who will present himself or run into her before the end of the scene. Use the sample questions listed for Beast’s Hackles as a guide for the kind of people she can summon. An individual fitting this description must be present in the scene, or the Devotion simply fails.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim feels uncontrollably drawn to the vampire; she gains her Auspex dots as bonus dice on the first Social action she makes with him in the scene.
rollResults.failure: Either the victim is too preoccupied to notice the vampire, or no appropriate victim is present.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: Rather than attracting the attention of someone the vampire desires, she becomes lost in the cacophony of her heightened senses. The vampire suffers –2 to Social actions for the rest of the scene.

devotions.name: Kiss of Death
devotions.summary: Turns the Kiss into a lethal predatory weapon.
devotions.effect: If the vampire bites a victim, she can spend a Vitae to impose the Drugged Tilt ( Chronicles of Darkness , p. 281) or the Intoxicated Condition if this is outside of combat.

devotions.name: Love Bomb
devotions.summary: Floods a subject with sudden, overwhelming affection.
devotions.cost: 1 Vitae, in addition to any cost for the implanted Majesty effect.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Empathy + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire implants a Majesty effect into his subject, which triggers when the correct conditions are met. The subject must be aware of the trigger: “The next time you meet a vampire” won’t function if she’s not wise to the Masquerade but, “When someone says the word ‘Kindred’ to you” does. When the trigger is fulfilled, the vampire’s player rolls to activate the implanted Majesty effect as normal against the character who tripped the trigger, ignoring the need to have inflicted Awe. The vampire activating this Devotion remains the user for the purposes of the Majesty effect.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The charge implanted into the subject is particularly potent and can affect a second victim before expiring.
rollResults.failure: The vampire’s influence fails to take root.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim’s blood sours against the vampire, granting 9-again to resist his Majesty for the scene.

devotions.name: One Night Stand
devotions.summary: Creates an intense but deliberately short-lived emotional attachment.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have inflicted the Charmed Condition on the victim.
devotions.effect: When the victim resolves or ends Charmed, he won’t quite remember who he’s been serving. He’ll know someone beguiled him, but he wouldn’t be able to pull her out of a lineup, or even a fantasy. Most characters will think of this in the same way as getting blackout drunk, and may just forget about the incident entirely. If they don’t, apply the vampire’s Dominate/Obfuscate dots as a penalty on all Mental actions to recall or describe her.

devotions.name: Picture Perfect
devotions.summary: Controls how the vampire appears in captured images.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must bleed a Vitae onto a piece of representational art depicting herself (included in the cost). This object must be physical, like a Polaroid, a painting, or even a sculpture.

rollResults.success: The Daeva imbues the piece with a fragment of her charisma. Anyone who encounters it with equal or fewer Resolve + Blood Potency dots than the vampire’s successes will file it away in the back of their mind as a work of profound beauty. If they later meet the vampire, they gain the Swooning Condition toward her. The vampire can only create one such object at a time. If she creates a new one, the effect on the old one expires.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The duration is weeks instead of nights.
rollResults.failure: It’s nice, but is it perfect?
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The art provokes revulsion in its viewers and the vampire is blissfully unaware. She suffers her own Majesty rating as a penalty on Social rolls with anyone who sees the work in a night, and these characters are immune to her Awe. This penalty lasts a scene.

devotions.name: Potence
devotions.summary: Combines strength and allure into an overwhelming show of dominance.
devotions.effect: For the duration, the vampire ignores Durability when attacking objects, or armor if she’s attacking an individual. If the target of the vampire’s attack has no armor on the relevant body part, she deals lethal damage with her attacks, including to other Kindred. This armor-busting effect even applies to the first-listed active effect of Resilience. However, this provokes a Clash of Wills.

devotions.name: Ring the Bell
devotions.summary: A precise strike leaves the victim dazed and disoriented.
devotions.requirement: The vampire activates this Devotion as she makes a successful Brawl or Weaponry attack.
devotions.effect: The victim goes reeling from a successful attack, taking a penalty to their Initiative score equal to damage dealt for the rest of the scene. This Devotion can only be successfully applied to a victim once per scene.

devotions.name: Snap Punch
devotions.summary: Delivers a startling attack before the victim can react.
devotions.effect: Before the vampire’s player rolls for Initiative, activate this Devotion. The vampire can take a single physical action before any regular actions take place, which does not sacrifice the vampire’s regular action in the first round of combat. If another character also has a power that allows them to pre-empt Initiative (e.g., the active effect of Celerity), a Clash of Wills occurs to determine the first actor.

devotions.name: Speak of the Devil
devotions.summary: Draws a named subject into the scene through gossip and social gravity.
devotions.requirement: The victim must have been affected by the vampire’s Awe within a number of nights equal to Blood Potency.

rollResults.success: The vampire appears somewhere within the vicin ity of the victim, just out of sight. If the victim speaks the vampire’s name aloud within the time period noted above, she’ll be aware of it, and can use this Devotion without spending a Willpower.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire is mystically aware of the surroundings she’s about to appear in, and can pick up the flow of a conversation in progress, or insert herself into the scene in an otherwise dramatic fashion.
rollResults.failure: The Blood lies still in the veins. The Devotion has no effect.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire teleports… somewhere.

devotions.name: Subliminal Message
devotions.summary: Hides a suggestion inside an apparently ordinary communication.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must activate Awe.

rollResults.success: The vampire hides a secret meaning within a the matically related sentence. For example, if she wanted to convey that the Prince seems upset, she might say, “Her Majesty’s outfit is quite… confronting.” Anyone who hears the vampire’s statement will know the hidden meaning, but only if they are under the effect of the vampire’s Awe. The vampire can also choose to convey this message only to certain people.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire’s message is clear as day to anyone listening. They gain her Obfuscate dots as a bonus to conveying this idea subtly for the rest of the scene.
rollResults.failure: The noise overwhelms the signal.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire’s message is garbled and she doesn’t know it, but her listeners think they got it. The Storyteller decides what that means.

devotions.name: Whisper Campaign
devotions.summary: Spreads a supernatural rumor through a social network.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must seed the rumor among at least five individuals before rolling.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Socialize + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire puts a rumor out into the world about her victim, whether for good or for ill. For the duration, the subject gains a dot of the Fame Merit or the Notoriety Condition (Chronicles of Darkness , p. 290), depending on the context. Anyone who gets a good look at the victim will know who they are and what they did.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The effect lasts for weeks instead of nights.
rollResults.failure: Who?
rollResults.dramaticFailure: A nasty rumor forms about the vampire herself, which lasts for the duration above. She gains the Notoriety Condition.

devotions.name: Brick
devotions.summary: Disables or locks a target device through supernatural access.
devotions.effect: The vampire spends a Vitae and Lashes Out (Vampire, p. 92). If successful, she disables all electronic devices in the immediate area with Durability equal to or lower than her successes. The devices power down and refuses to work for the duration. The Oracle can spend a Willpower on success to ensure the effect lasts the night. If someone tries to repair this device before the power expires, Crafts rolls are penalized by the vampire’s Blood Potency.

devotions.name: Reach Out and Touch Someone
devotions.summary: Projects Interface through a remote connection.
devotions.requirement: The victim must first use Digital Whispers on the device.
devotions.effect: A brief burst of electricity lashes out from the device with a range of (Interface) meters, inflicting lethal damage equal to Vigor on a victim, even a vampire. Keen observers or highspeed cameras will see this energy is shaped like raking claws or a striking fist.

devotions.name: Catfish
devotions.summary: Constructs a convincing digital identity that resists scrutiny.
devotions.requirement: If the vampire choses to copy a specific person, she must study him for at least ten minutes.
devotions.effect: The vampire alters her appearance and voice to resemble whoever she wants over electronic media. To observers she remains the same, but all technology perceives her as a flawless copy of her chosen target, be it a specific person or a general ideal; see The Familiar Stranger for guidelines ( Vampire, p. 138). If she uses this Devotion to copy a specific person, it can even to fool devices like digital fingerprint readers and retinal scanners, but the vampire must have fed on the victim of her identity theft at some point in the night.

devotions.name: Re: Search
devotions.summary: Searches connected systems with preternatural speed and intuition.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must mark either her victim or his home with 1 Vitae (included in cost).

rollResults.success: As long as the victim is within the same room as his device, for the rest of the night the player can ask the Storyteller one question per success on the activation roll. These can be questions from the list for Uncanny Perception, or any of the following: Where is my victim right now? What is my victim doing? Who else is with my victim? Where is my victim going?
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire gains the Informed Condition regarding her prey.
rollResults.failure: Connection timed out.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The device provides false information and leaves a traceable data trail back to the vampire.

devotions.name: Kin to the Land
devotions.summary: A 3-dot Lithopedia rite binding the Család to the history and behavior of territory.
devotions.effect: To use this ritual, the vampire spreads the sacrifice at four equidistant corners within her territory, usually art cross streets. This forms the epicenter of the rite. If successful, for the rest of the scene, all mortal residents of the territory are considered thrice removed from the vampire in terms of Blood Sympathy. Those in the epicenter are twice removed. Anyone with a natural blood tie to the vampire finds it goes down a step of removal, or one lower than the one imposed by the ritual if it was higher. This is a one-way connection. It doesn’t allow other Kindred to use Blood Sympathy with the Család if they didn’t have it already. Vampires in the area feel this false connection form, and can reflexively contest it with Stamina + Blood Potency, minus the spell’s Potency. For as long as victims remain in the area, the vampire does not need to spend Willpower to force sympathy.

devotions.name: Lair of the Beast
devotions.summary: A 1-dot Lithopedia rite binding the Család to the history and behavior of territory.
devotions.effect: The vampire smears her Vitae over a central point of her territory. If the casting is successful, for the rest of the night the Család extends her Predatory Aura over the area. Vampires constantly feel her Beast’s presence, and even humans sense a certain atavistic unease. If she remains within the bounds of the territory, the Család can feel trespassing predators touch her aura if they aren’t Obfuscated, and she can lash out at them from a distance by spending a Vitae along with the usual cost, though the victim can still respond. The ritualist can extend this spell’s duration by a night per additional Potency.

devotions.name: Nowhere to Hide
devotions.summary: A 4-dot Lithopedia rite binding the Család to the history and behavior of territory.
devotions.effect: The vampire marks an open-air part of the territory with the sacrifice; removing the mark ends the effect. If successful, Stealth actions in the territory automatically fail for the rest of the night, and Obfuscate doesn’t work unless the actor prevails in a Clash of Wills, penalized by the rite’s Potency. This does not apply to the vampire, and she can obviate the effect on anyone she anoints with a Vitae at casting. Protection ends if they wipe away the blood.

devotions.name: Nowhere to Run
devotions.summary: A 3-dot Lithopedia rite binding the Család to the history and behavior of territory.
devotions.effect: The vampire pours Vitae over a map of her territory and draws symbols of protection and the elements. If the ritual is successful, she can impose an Environmental Tilt on a small section marked on the map, up to the size of a large room or a cross-street. She can use any Environmental Tilt listed in the Chronicles of Darkness Rulebook except Extreme Heat. If the Tilt has degrees of severity, the rite defaults to the lowest, but the vampire can spend additional Vitae to increase it, up to limit equal to her Lithopedia dots. Once the ritual is complete, the vampire must take an instant at some point in the evening to inflict this Tilt on the marked area. This Tilt lasts a scene. The vampire is immune to the Tilt, as is anyone whose name she marked on the map when she cast the spell.

devotions.name: Prince's Wrath
devotions.summary: A 4-dot Lithopedia rite binding the Család to the history and behavior of territory.
devotions.effect: Officially, only Hunyadi Dorján has mastered this ritual, but he suspects one of his eldest childer has mastered it as well. Whether she wishes to share it with her own disciples is another matter. To perform this ritual, the Család must stab her shadow at a central point in the territory. This inflicts her with lethal damage equal to (5 – Blood Potency), to a minimum of one point. She then expends the ritual’s Vitae cost through the wound and onto the ground. She must bear this damage for as long as the ritual lasts, or else the spell is broken. In the event a Hollow Mekhet knows this rite, she must stab her Ka to affect it. If successful, for the rest of the night the ritualist infuses the area with a nightmarish manifestation of her Beast. Every window seems to carry her reflection at the edge of peripheral vision, and predatory animals will attack people at the slightest provocation. The vampire herself is the epicenter of this horror, and gains several benefits. People subconsciously recognize her as the master of the territory, and cannot spend Willpower to defy her in any way. Furthermore, attacking the ritualist is a breaking point at Humanity 3 and higher, or with a –3 modifier in the case of mortals. She can also spend a Willpower to extend social and mental Discipline effects through inanimate objects within her line of sight. In addition, vampires can only choose a flight response if the Család lashes out at them, and any fear frenzy provocations suffer the rite’s Potency as an additional penalty.

devotions.name: Taste the Land
devotions.summary: A 1-dot Lithopedia rite binding the Család to the history and behavior of territory.
devotions.effect: The vampire must feed from a resident of the area before she casts this rite, using his stolen Vitae in the cost. If successful, she receives a vision of the local population and all their various emotions. The Storyteller must provide a general mood for the area as it stands for the night. Typically, a word or short phrase will do: “Tense”, “Bored”, “On the brink”, etc. For the rest of the night, the vampire adds her Lithopedia dots to any Empathy or Persuasion rolls with mortal residents, and can ignore the first door in any Social maneuver if she exploits this mood.

devotions.name: Territory's Wisdom
devotions.summary: A 2-dot Lithopedia rite binding the Család to the history and behavior of territory.
devotions.effect: The vampire feeds on an employee of a business in her territory, spending the blood gained into the cost of this ritual. If successful, she can choose a Mental or Social Skill most appropriate to the site (Medicine for a hospital, Socialize for a nightclub, etc.). For as long as she remains in the bounds of her territory, for the rest of the night she can draw on her sympathetic link to the site, allowing her to spend Vitae on that Skill as she were using Physical Intensity. However, her per turn rate of Vitae expenditure for this effect is determined by Blood Potency or Lithopedia, whichever is lower.

devotions.name: Urban Unrest
devotions.summary: A 2-dot Lithopedia rite binding the Család to the history and behavior of territory.
devotions.effect: A variation of Taste the Land, the vampire can alter the mood of the people in her domain rather than reading it. Just as with that ritual, she must feed from a resident before she casts the spell. If successful, she can instill the area with a mood, as defined above. For the rest of the night, the Család succeeds with three successes instead of five on any roll to exploit this mood in the territory, though this only applies to groups rather than individuals. For example, if she imposes a violent mood, this rite can enhance actions to incite a riot.

devotions.name: Red Tide
devotions.summary: A 5-dot Lithopedia rite binding the Család to the history and behavior of territory.
devotions.effect: To cast this rite, in addition to the usual cost, the vampire must sacrifice a dot of Blood Potency. This returns at the end of the month. As such, characters with only a dot of Blood Potency cannot cast this ritual. Once the ritual is complete, the vampire makes the territory an extension of her Vitae for the night. Dark blood pools in sinks, faucets, and cracks in the infrastructure, and mortals who take lethal damage bleed this substance. Vampires feeding on blood from inanimate objects treat it as cold mortal blood, and every half square mile of the area has about a corpse’s worth of Vitae, give or take.
