Feeding from wounded mortals works as usual. This blood has an enticing scent, almost like a coppery candy. Anyone drinking it gains a first step blood bond to the caster, but an existent blood bond cannot be extended any further. Vampires in the presence of this blood must resist frenzy as if they were hungry (or starving if they are addicted to Vitae), and even humans must succeed on a Resolve + Composure roll to resist tasting it.

devotions.name: Tie to the Land
devotions.summary: A 5-dot Lithopedia rite binding the Család to the history and behavior of territory.
devotions.effect: Resisted by: highest Composure in the area To use this ritual, the vampire must kill a resident of the area, spreading his blood at five equidistant points around her territory. At the geographic center of this pentagon, the vampire spills her own blood. Once complete, the vampire forms a false blood bond with her subjects. All mortal residents of the area gain a first step Vinculum to the vampire or the Vitae donor, or a second step bond if they reside in the epicenter. This lasts the rest of the night. Kindred residents resist the formation of this false bond with a successful Resolve + Blood Potency roll, minus the spell’s Potency. The Coil of the Voivode applies to these bonds, and the vampire can use Kin to the Land to enhance blood ties further.

devotions.name: Beasts' Measure
devotions.summary: Judges another Beast through the Kuufukuji's disciplined hunger.

rollResults.success: The Kuufukuji makes a lightning quick assessment of another vampire. She can tell roughly how much Vitae he has in his system (i.e., full, close to full, half-empty, hungry, starving), and whether he has frenzied in the last 24 hours.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The Storyteller must provide an exact number on the victim’s current Vitae pool.
rollResults.failure: The Beast does not give up its secrets so easily. The vampire cannot use this Devotion on the same subject for the rest of the scene.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The Celibate’s poise cracks as the Beast rages at its failure. In addition to the above, the vampire takes the Tempted Condition.

devotions.name: Wave Form
devotions.summary: Lets the starving vampire yield and redirect force like water.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must activate this Devotion on the same turn she makes a close combat attack. She cannot take any other action.
devotions.effect: The vampire benefits from a single active effect of both Celerity and Resilience as if she had one fewer dots in both Disciplines. For example, with Celerity 3 she could only perform an interrupt action twice in a scene using this Devotion, though she could perform a third with the normal application of Celerity. This does not apply to persistent effects. If the vampire successfully strikes her opponent, he suffers the Knocked Down Tilt from the momentum of her blow. She cannot use the normal effects of these Disciplines in the same turn as she activates Wave Form.

devotions.name: Foot in the Door
devotions.summary: Creates an opening for a Leandros fixation.
devotions.duration: One turn of a Social maneuver
devotions.effect: The vampire bypasses a victim’s social defenses. Each time the Leandros activates this Devotion, she gains a perfect Impression in Social maneuvering, regardless of her actual first impression. This power must be activated each turn of the Social maneuver, or else the impression reverts to its normal level.

devotions.name: Heart Thief
devotions.summary: Steals emotional priority from a subject's existing attachments.
devotions.requirement: The victim must have the Soulmate Condition. Use of this Devotion ends without resolving Soulmate.

rollResults.success: The Leandros drains the light from her victim’s heart. The mortal suffers the vampire’s successes in lethal damage, and gains the Scorned Condition if he survives (see below). Conversely, for the above duration, the vampire’s base damage from sunlight is only a single bashing damage, whatever her actual Humanity rating. The rate of damage is still determined by Blood Potency, but if she does not expose herself to direct sunlight, such as by wearing heavy clothing, that trait is halved, rounding down, when determining frequency (Vampire, p. 102). The Leandros still needs to spend Vitae to “wake” in the evening, but she does not need to resist daysleep and does not take Lethargic.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: In addition to the usual duration, the effect extends by a week.
rollResults.failure: The vampire’s heart can’t take the pain.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim takes the Scorned Condition, but the vampire takes no benefit.

devotions.name: Mr. Perfect
devotions.summary: Presents the exact romantic persona a subject wants to see.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Subterfuge + Obfuscate vs. Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire manipulates her victim into believing she is everything he desires, both socially and physically. The vampire gains the Advanced Action quality on a number of mundane Social actions with the victim equal to Obfuscate.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire has until the end of the night to use up her Advanced Actions.
rollResults.failure: The victim sees through the vampire’s cheap tricks.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire humiliates herself, taking on the appearance of the exact opposite of what her victim wants to see.

devotions.name: Only You
devotions.summary: Makes one attachment eclipse all alternatives.
devotions.requirement: The mortal must be the vampire’s “one” for the purposes of her clan bane.
devotions.effect: The mortal and vampire express their mutual, undying love. This must be consensual, and cannot be supernaturally compelled through Majesty, Dominate, the blood bond, or any other coercive means. Sealed with a kiss, both gain the Soulmate Condition.

devotions.name: Shared Experience
devotions.summary: Shares sensation and emotion across the Leandros bond.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Persuasion + Auspex vs. Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The victim gains the False Memories Condition for the rest of the night, believing she and the vampire once shared an intimate experience. If the vampire succeeds any Empathy or Persuasion rolls with the victim that also evoke this memory, she treats them instead as exceptional successes.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim is so enamored with the vampire that he gains the Swooning Condition.
rollResults.failure: The vampire tries to spark a false memory in her victim, but it refuses to catch.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire believes she and her victim really have shared an experience and references it to the point where she comes off as creepy. She gains the Delusional Condition for the rest of the scene.

devotions.name: Claritudo
devotions.summary: Clarifies a stolen or damaged memory.
devotions.requirement: Used on another, the vampire must feed the subject a point of Vitae.
devotions.dicePool: Intelligence + Medicine + Celerity vs. Resolve + Blood Potency (if unwilling)

rollResults.success: The vampire clears a mind of outside influence. This works on both mundane mind-altering substances, such as alcohol or antidepressants, as well as supernatural effects like Obfuscate or Majesty, though those provoke a Clash of Wills. Claritudo can even suppress the false-love of the Vinculum, but only at the first and second steps (this even applies to any blood bonds formed using this Devotion). Any supernatural attempts to further alter the subject’s mind becomes a Clash of Wills, and consuming mind-altering/addictive substances or Vitae has no effect, although they might remain in the subject’s system. Any effect with a longer duration than Claritudo resumes when this Devotion expires.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: As above, but protection lasts the night.
rollResults.failure: The subject’s mind is too clouded, and the vampire fails to cleanse it.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: Rather than empowering her subject’s brain, the vampire weakens it instead. He gains the Confused Condition.

devotions.name: Memoria Sanguinis
devotions.summary: Reads a memory preserved in blood.
devotions.duration: Nights equal to Blood Potency, or until consumed
devotions.effect: if the vampire spends a Willpower. The Keeper concentrates on a memory he wishes to preserve and spills a point of Vitae into a sealable container, keeping up to a full day’s worth of memories. Anyone drinking the blood gains the memories contained within as if she had just experienced them herself, though she is aware this is not her true recollection. This does not risk blood addiction or the Vinculum. The vampire cannot use draughts on himself. A subject can only benefit from one draught until the associated effect or Condition ends. Depending on the memory bottled, one of the following effects occurs. Neutral memories do not apply a Condition. • E uphoria: Appropriate for memories of pleasure or joy, the drinker experiences a surge of bliss. If the drinker is Kindred, they gain the Sated Condition as the Beast’s growls are muffled by waves of contentment. If mortal, they gain Inspired. • De spair: Memories of horrific acts or terrible loss feel as real as if they had just occurred. The drinker gains the Shaken Condition from the sudden onrush of awful memories. • D istress: The Mnemosyne heightens the emotional impact of memories containing provocative or frightening imagery in order to rouse the Beast. The drinker gains the Tempted Condition or can choose to succumb to the appropriate form of frenzy (such as to ride the wave). If the drinker is mortal, they gain the Bestial Condition. If the vampire knows Esuritio Lethes (below), he can bottle memories earned with that Devotion for the above effects, or create the one listed below. Feeding a draught of stolen memories to the original victim of that Devotion ends (but does not resolve) Amnesia. • E xpertise: By concentrating on stolen memories, the vampire can bottle a benefit gained from Esuritio Lethes. He loses those benefits for himself in the process, but anyone drinking the potion will then gain them, along with attached memories. This is no substitute for actual training or getting to know someone, however, and these bonuses will fade in nights equal to the Keeper’s Blood Potency.

devotions.name: Esuritio Lethes
devotions.summary: Creates a hunger for forgetting.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must impose the Amnesia Condition with The Lying Mind, and then consume a Vitae. This does not break Mesmerized if she only takes one point for the purposes of this Devotion. This risks the Vinculum and blood addiction as usual.
devotions.effect: The Mnemosyne steals memories from the victim. This can be as specific as the password to a secure email server, or as general as what happened to them at last night’s party. The vampire must know roughly what she’s looking for, unless she wants to fish for memories with Dominate. Once she feeds, the vampire gains her victim’s memory as if she had just experienced it herself. This Devotion has two specific effects, depending upon the intention of the vampire. Only one can apply per stolen memory: • T heft of Memory: The vampire steals a piece of information the victim possesses or a stretch of time spanning no longer than twenty-four hours. This process creates an intimate connection between the Mnemosyne and her victim, providing her insight into the victim’s psychology. The vampire learns the victim’s Virtue and Vice (or equivalents) as well as any Persistent Conditions, and gains the 8-again quality on Social rolls with him related to these stolen memories. This also counts as a form of Hard Leverage. • T heft of Skill: The Mind-Thief drains his victim of hours of practice and study, stealing that knowledge for himself. The vampire chooses a Mental Skill the victim has dots in. If the Mnemosyne has no dots in that Skill, he no longer suffers an unskilled penalty. If he does have dots in this Skill, he acquires a Specialty related to her victim’s area of expertise. For the duration of Amnesia, the victim suffers the vampire’s Blood Potency dots divided by two (rounding up) on all uses of the chosen Skill. The mechanical benefits of memories remain for the duration, but a victim does not regain them until he resolves Amnesia, and any penalty from Theft of Skill remains. Should the vampire wish, he can preserve these memories with Memoria Sanguinis, but he must do so before Esuritio Lethes expires. A victim can only be subject to one instance of this Devotion at a time, for as long as Amnesia lasts.

devotions.name: Sanguis Veritatis
devotions.summary: Tests a remembered event against truth carried in Vitae.
devotions.requirement: Drink and spend one Vitae from the subject; normal Vinculum and addiction risks apply.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Empathy + Auspex vs. Resolve + Blood Potency, if unwilling
devotions.effect: Success reveals the extent and cause of the subject's damaged or altered memories and removes False Memories and Amnesia; supernatural alteration also requires a Clash of Wills. The restoration is all-or-nothing, cannot target the user, cannot remove the Mnemosyne bane's False Memories, and cannot recover memories lost naturally to time. Exceptional success restores one Willpower to vampire and subject; dramatic failure gives the vampire False Memories drawn from the subject for a scene.

devotions.name: Blodtrell
devotions.summary: Marks another person as a blood-bound instrument of Norvegi vengeance.
devotions.requirement: The subjects must be the vampire’s ghouls
devotions.effect: In a special ritual, the Norvegus spends a Willpower and then feeds each of his ghouls two Vitae. This does not add to their reserves. Instead, the blood takes the form of a slithering worm that wriggles down their throats, transforming them into nightmarish creatures called blodtrells. The Norvegus adds his Protean dots to a blodtrell’s Physical Attributes or Size, distributing them as he wishes. Alternatively, he can grant the creature a point of general armor for every two dots. These mutations can raise a blodtrell’s Attributes above 5, but they suffer a lethal damage per excess dot when the Devotion ends, as their body collapses from the strain. The physical effect of this transformation is terrifying and grotesque: bones elongate and reshape to allow greater speed, muscles swell to unnatural proportions, and flesh thickens to absorb impacts. Even under heavy layers of clothing, an observer will notice something is off about the blodtrell. If the vampire knows Frakka, below, she can spend two additional Vitae to implant a dart of crystallized blood into a blodtrell’s hand, allowing them to throw a “sturdy” dart as per that Devotion. For the reduration, the Norvegus can see through the eyes of his blodtrells and direct them telepathically, and can coordinate devastating strikes on his enemies. As an instant action, the vampire can designate a number of blodtrells equal to his Blood Potency to act in concert. For one turn, these thralls ignore a single victim’s Defense equal to the vampire’s Auspex dots. The connection between the vampire and his blodtrells is incredibly intimate, and the death of one is a breaking point at Humanity 2 and higher.

devotions.name: Frakka
devotions.summary: Turns outlaw blood into a concealed predatory weapon.
devotions.effect: The vampire must strike her victim with a dart using a throw attack, rolling Dexterity + Athletics – Defense. Darts have a base damage of +1L supernatural damage and have a short range equal to Strength + Athletics + Celerity in meters. Medium range is double that; long range is triple. If the vampire is within close range, she can instead use the dart with the Weaponry Skill. By default, these shards are incredibly brittle and shatter upon impact. If not used within a minute of their creation, they dissolve into puddles of cloudy, pink plasma. However, if the vampire invests two Vitae into a shard instead of one, it sticks in flesh until removed. Being hit with a sturdier dart imposes a 2-die penalty on combat actions due to the pain. This penalty is not cumulative, but might compound into a Wrack Tilt at Storyteller discretion. The vampire can use a solid dart to pin a victim’s limb against a wall or object. To do so, she takes an additional penalty for attacking a specified target, and must equal the victim’s Stamina in successes if she wants to pierce a limb directly, rather than clothing. If successful, this imposes the Pinned Tilt ( p. 53).

devotions.name: Tordenvaer
devotions.summary: Strikes with the sudden violence of a storm.

rollResults.success: The vampire takes a point of aggravated damage as crystallized Vitae explodes from his body, dealing successes in supernatural lethal damage to everything within (Celerity) meters. Mundane Defense does not apply to the vampire’s attack, but victims apply armor as normal, and can take an action to Dodge if they haven’t acted already. Objects downgrade damage successes equal to Durability, with remaining successes affecting Structure. Each meter beyond the epicenter of the explosion halves damage, rounding down. If used while grappling an opponent, damage is doubled on that victim.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: As above, but victims also suffer one of the following Tilts: Blinded (one eye), Leg Wrack (one leg), Arm Wrack (one arm), or Pinned.
rollResults.failure: The vampire fails to summon his blades.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire suffers a point of aggravated damage as his blades grow inward, inflicting the Insensate Tilt from the agony.

devotions.name: Tyvshand
devotions.summary: Steals an advantage through a touch or sleight of hand.
devotions.effect: When he manifests his Predatory Aspects, the vampire can choose to also grow patches of hair-thin needles on his hands and feet. This stacks with any other forms he assumes. These hairs are hollow and function like syringes, allowing the Norvegus to apply the Feed move in a grapple without inflicting a bite. In addition, if the vampire succeeds on a Brawl attack with his bare hands, he can choose to steal a Vitae on a successful hit, assuming the blow wasn’t absorbed by armor or Resilience. This inflicts an additional lethal damage on mortals, and drains a Vitae directly from a vampire’s blood pool. The vampire can also absorb any dry blood he touches, including bloodstains and blood splatter, making it an efficient way to clean up a crime scene. Stale blood yields one Vitae, or two if the stain/pool is greater than Size 4. This does not bypass Blood Potency feeding restrictions. If a victim Breaks Free of the grapple, he suffers a mundane point of lethal damage as the scopulae tear her skin away.

devotions.name: Taharah
devotions.summary: Purifies and protects an anointed attachment.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must anoint an enclosed space with her blood, included in the cost. The space can be about as large as a mid-sized apartment unit.
devotions.duration: One week per dot of Blood Potency
devotions.effect: The sanctum gains the following benefits: • C haracters cannot be provoked to frenzy while inside the sanctum, and entry ends any active frenzies, even those caused by a dramatic failure. If a supernatural power induces frenzy (such as the Coil of the Wyrm) a Clash of Wills takes place. • I nitiating an act of violence within the sanctum costs a Willpower point, which does not add +3 to the roll. Effectively, any violent character is automatically Beaten Down (Vampire, p. 175). This also applies to the Qedeshah. • N o Kindred, except those among the Qedeshah’s anointed, can enter the sanctum without her permission. Crossing the threshold without consent incurs a provocation to fear frenzy, with the vampire’s Majesty dots as a penalty. If the intruder fails, he flees. This effect can only apply to one sanctum at a time. Using the Devotion again dismisses the effect of a sanctum that’s already in effect. However, the vampire can renew this Devotion before its usual expiration.

devotions.name: Lebonah
devotions.summary: Carries influence through sacred scent and smoke.
devotions.effect: The vampire vomits up a mouthful of boiling Vitae that burns with a citrusy white smoke. This inflicts the Qedeshah with a point of bashing damage as her throat and mouth blister. Anyone who smells this smoke (other than the vampire herself) must roll Stamina + Blood Potency – Obfuscate every minute they remain in its presence. Those who fail this roll feel lightheaded and uncoordinated, suffering the Drugged Tilt in any subsequent combat, but gain a +3 on any frenzy provocations. This intoxicating effect is potent but fast acting, purging from a victim’s system at the end of the scene, along with the smoke.

devotions.name: Arcane Sight
devotions.summary: Extends Auspex toward occult traces and workings.
devotions.effect: The vampire can perceive the presence of ephemeral energy in an area. He can identify things like loci, hauntings, and even fetishes. Objects and places take on qualities that reflect their nature: a dagger containing a trapped spirit of war exudes a crackling, wild energy, while a cemetery takes on an eerie blue glow, or a faint rotting smell. Once a scene, the player can ask a number of yes/no/maybe questions equal to Auspex dots about the nature of any phenomena she can perceive.

devotions.name: Butcher's Hook
devotions.summary: Hooks a target's shadow to expose or restrain movement.
devotions.effect: The Mekhet spends a Vitae when activating The Spirit’s Touch while studying a video recording of a vampire obscured by the Lost Visage; he must be touching the screen as the subject appears. He can ask questions about the vampire for the purposes of Uncanny Perception, and the Beast will reveal a symbolic representation of the victim’s identity: a five-pointed star might appear over a recording of the sheriff, for example. If activating The Spirit’s Touch was an exceptional success, the Beast can see behind the Lost Visage, but the vampire is still limited by the quality of the mundane recording.

devotions.name: Cats' Paw
devotions.summary: Uses another person as an unwitting instrument.

rollResults.success: The vampire steals from her mark. For each success, she can acquire a Size 0 or 1 item from a victim that is not the immediate focus of his attention. This might even include intimate objects, such as contact lenses. Alternatively, the vampire can plant items on her victim, such as evidence of criminal activity or listening devices. This does not apply to objects that would be physically impossible to add/remove, or items that are locked to the victim’s body.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire’s speed is such that no item is safe. She can disarm an opponent of objects no greater than Size 3, including those under active attention.
rollResults.failure: The vampire doesn’t manage to acquire or deposit any items, and might be in trouble if the victim notices her looming over him.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire spectacularly miscalculates her attempt and leaves herself wide open. She gains the Stunned Tilt.

devotions.name: Copycat
devotions.summary: Temporarily imitates an observed technique.
devotions.requirement: The vampire uses Touch of Shadow on the victim
devotions.effect: The vampire copies her appearance onto a victim, creating an illusory duplicate. The two are identical twins down to the very last stitch of clothing, and this can even fool technology. If the victim is mortal, he exhibits the exact same signs of vampirism as the Mekhet herself, including a lack of heart rate or breathing. Should the vampire do something to change her own features before the end of the night, such as cutting her hair off or using the Blush of Life, she can choose if this affects her victim as well.

devotions.name: Cutting the Strings
devotions.summary: Severs a supernatural command or attachment.
devotions.effect: While this Devotion is active, the vampire is aware of any attempts to use Auspex on her, or any other supernatural divinations. Any readings trigger a vision of the aggressor. She can spend a Vitae to reflexively lash out at this effect, but the aggressor can choose to respond if he is Kindred, or if he has access to an effect that’s similar to the Predatory Aura.

devotions.name: Encode Vitae
devotions.summary: Stores a message or pattern in blood.
devotions.requirement: The courier has been successfully used as a mnemonic ghoul at least once before

rollResults.success: When and if the ghoul injects the prepared Vitae, he encodes the message in his blood rather than reciting it. Once the ghoul reaches his intended recipient, they must feed from this messenger before the end of the scene, or else the message fades from the blood. Once they feed, they receive the message as if they were experiencing it outside the normal flow of time. This vision can be significantly more detailed than the usual effect of mnemonic ghouls; the only limit is the Mekhet’s creativity or recall.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The experience of receiving this message is enlightening, and the recipient refreshes a spent Willpower.
rollResults.failure: The Vitae becomes dead blood. The vampire must begin again.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The message is garbled and wrong, and the vampire won’t know it. Sample Modifiers: A year old memory (–1), a decade old memory –2, the message is complex or academic (–2), a century old memory (–3), the message is longer than five minutes (–3), the vampire has the Eidetic Memory Merit (+2)

devotions.name: Familiar's Eyes
devotions.summary: Experience the world through the senses of a familiar or animal ghoul.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must feed the animal a point of Vitae, included in the cost.
devotions.effect: The vampire projects his senses into a familiar or animal ghoul, experiencing whatever it does. The vampire can’t influence the animal directly with this power, but it stills respond to Animalism commands or training as normal. However, this Devotion limits the vampire’s own perceptions. He loses any sense projected into the animal, but he can be selective. If the animal is exposed to a sensation that would evoke frenzy, such as exposure to fire or sunlight, the vampire must resist as normal, but with a +2 modifier.

devotions.name: Kuroko
devotions.summary: Moves as an ignored stagehand while enabling another's action.
devotions.requirement: The vampire activates this Devotion at the beginning of the turn she attacks her victim.
devotions.effect: The vampire attacks her victim, but neither he nor any bystanders will recognize that she did the deed. They might see an illusory assailant make a run for it, or just a quick blur and a blood spatter. This attack is incredibly disorienting, inflicting the victim with the Stunned Tilt. This Devotion only applies once per victim in a scene, and does not work on attacks that require sustained contact, such as grappling or feeding.

devotions.name: Out of Sight, Out of Mind
devotions.translatedName: Out of Sight, Out of Mind
devotions.summary: Makes absence erode witnesses' attention and memory.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must smear a point of Vitae (included in the cost) in a central point in the area before the end of the scene. If this Vitae is somehow washed away, this Devotion does not work.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Stealth + Obfuscate vs. highest Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire spends a Willpower and activates this Devotion as she leaves an area. If successful, everyone in the scene forgets she was ever present, gaining the False Memories Condition. All traces of her passing erode: security tapes glitch, written materials vanish or are inexplicably destroyed, and superficial damage to the environment is displaced onto another phenomenon (maybe it was local hoodlums who vandalized the prince’s classic car). Even someone physically harmed by the vampire will be hard pressed to remember what she looked like, defaulting to their own personal prejudices and assumptions. The vampire can choose to exempt specific individuals or items from this Devotion.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The power of the vampire’s Obfuscate wipes away all physical records of her presence, including superficial damage or alterations she inflicted on material items. Any item she damaged but did not destroy “forgets” that it was ever harmed. Scratches and chips replace themselves, paint fades from walls, and cracked glass repairs itself. This does not affect dead or living creatures, who retain any damage inflicted.
rollResults.failure: The vampire is exactly as memorable as normal.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire internalizes her attempt to be forgotten and instead loses her own memory of the previous scene. She suffers the Confused Condition. Sample Modifiers: Groups greater than five (–1), groups greater than ten (–2), groups greater than 20 (–3), the vampire did significant damage or violence in the scene (–5).

devotions.name: Shadow in the Land
devotions.summary: Projects perception through the surrounding territory.
devotions.requirement: The vampire is currently using Twilight Projection
devotions.effect: The vampire’s Twilight form manifests in the material world as a translucent ghost. She can’t touch or manipulate things, but she can inflict any mental or social Discipline she knows as long as it doesn’t require her to spill blood. Others cannot affect her with Disciplines or attacks unless they have the means to do so on ephemeral beings. The vampire can return to Twilight with an instant action.

devotions.name: Terminator
devotions.summary: Pursues a designated target with tireless precision.
devotions.requirement: The victim must be within line of sight
devotions.effect: The vampire choses a single mortal and pursues him at a steady walk. While this Devotion is active, the Mekhet keeps pace with the target, no matter how fast he runs. If the victim hides or escapes line of sight, the vampire instinctively knows which way to go and will catch up with him the next time he slows his pace or catches his breath. This Devotion only functions if the victim remains on foot. However, if he uses a vehicle to escape the immediate area, the vampire still knows which direction to head. At the Storyteller’s discretion, if the victim hasn’t left the immediate area, the vampire might still be able to reach him at a stoplight or in dense traffic. If your chronicle uses the rules for Chases ( Chronicles of Darkness, p. 84), the following system applies: The vampire seizes the Edge for the rest of the scene, no matter how well the victim rolls. The number of successes required to escape the vampire is increased by her Celerity dots.

devotions.name: Timing Is Everything
devotions.summary: Acts at the exact instant an opening appears.
devotions.dicePool: Intelligence + Expression + Auspex vs. Composure + Blood Potency (if unwilling)

rollResults.success: At a predefined point in the night, the subject receives a telepathic message from the vampire, no longer than a sentence or two. This message can impose a Condition as with Lay Open the Mind, but this costs an additional Vitae.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire can impose a Condition for no cost, if she chooses.
rollResults.failure: Lost in the mail.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The message finds its way to the nearest vampire or ghoul. If the vampire knows Dominate 3 (Entombed Command), she can pay an additional Experience to enhance this Devotion. She can now choose to set a condition for the message to arrive rather than a specific time: meeting a certain individual, encountering a code phrase, etc. Sample Modifiers: More than an hour (–1), more than two hours (–2), more than three hours (–3), subject is a ghoul (+1), subject is the same clan (+2).

devotions.name: Twist of Fate
devotions.summary: Turns a narrowly failed moment toward a different outcome.

rollResults.success: The vampire attunes to the immediate future. Before the end of the night, the player can treat a single reflexive or instant action as an exceptional success without rolling. The vampire can only access Twist of Fate once per night, and it does not apply to resisted or contested actions, including attack rolls.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire gains unique insight into his immediate future. She gains the Steadfast Condition.
rollResults.failure: Reply hazy, ask again later.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: Fate delights in laying low the arrogant. One future action this chapter is reduced to a chance die, as determined by the Storyteller.

devotions.name: Wolf's Clothing
devotions.summary: Conceals predatory nature behind a borrowed presentation.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have studied the creature type she’s trying to imitate with Uncanny Perception.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Socialize + Obfuscate vs. highest Composure + Supernatural Tolerance

rollResults.success: The vampire hides herself among a supernatural group. To mundane and basic supernatural senses, she appears to be one of them. She smells like a werewolf, feels like a changeling, or has the subtle aura of a mage. She can even use this effect to give off the vibe of particular Kindred clans or bloodlines if she so chooses. The vampire gains no knowledge of the culture, terminology, or etiquette of the group, but doesn’t stand out if she remains passive. If another creature uses a supernatural power to investigate the vampire’s true nature, it provokes a Clash of Wills.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire’s disguise is so perfect that she gains the 9-again quality on contested rolls to fool supernatural powers, and mundane actions that might reveal her true nature. On resisted actions, the actor suffers the vampire’s Obfuscate dots as a penalty.
rollResults.failure: The vampire is what she is, for better or worse.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire’s lie is exposed, but she is unaware of this fact and leaves herself wide open. The next action the intended dupes take against the vampire ignores her Defense, or her Resistance if it’s a supernatural power.

devotions.name: Annals of Death
devotions.summary: Answer questions about death in a location and foresee deaths.

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The player asks a question as though she had rolled a success; the Storyteller should give false or misleading information.
rollResults.failure: The vampire can glean no bloody history from the place. Could it be that pristine?
rollResults.success: The player can ask the Storyteller one question per success about the history of her current location, as it pertains to the deaths of people, creatures, or supernatural beings. For purposes of this Devotion, a location encompasses a single building or other discrete area of roughly equivalent size, although she may focus on a smaller area such as a single room if she likes. Also, for purposes of this Devotion, “death” includes the Embrace, as well as Final Death. As with similar uses of Auspex, the Beast within provides images and sensations that convey the history. The questions below are samples; the player may — with Storyteller permission — come up with others that fit the criteria. The player may also spend successes to learn who or what will be next to die in her location, if nothing interferes with the pattern in the interim. Each success she spends this way allows her to ask the Storyteller one question about the next death to come, similar to the sample questions given for past deaths. She may mix and match successes to gain information about both the past and the future with one use of this Discipline.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The elder can extrapolate more subtle moments of tragedy from patterns of ruin. For each answer the Storyteller provides, the vampire also learns the nature of any breaking points, Touchstones, and Vices that were or will be involved in the deaths she sees or predicts. Sample Questions • Who was the first (or last) person to die here? The ghostly image of a face in the mirror with a bullet hole in its head. Last words scrawled in blood across the wall. • Is there a factor that connects multiple deaths in this location? A hand reaching out from the shadows to direct the knife. Shimmering lines connecting objects and spaces as if on a map. • Did someone die here within [a given time period]? A set of bloodstained, turn-of-the-century style clothes draped over the arm of a chair. The pages of a calendar flipping backward to a particular date. • Who was the last person to die here that I know personally? The victim’s voice calling out to the vampire for help. A pair of glaring eyes that accuse the vampire from the detached head of a corpse. • What was the predominant emotion surrounding [a specific person’s] death? The seductive scent of heady perfume. A room tinged with the green of envy.

devotions.name: Bones of the Mountain
devotions.summary: Become living stone and combine formidable physical Disciplines.

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire convulses with the pain of an uncontrolled change, transforming into a motionless statue in a contorted pose. She can’t move, act, or speak until her next turn, and must roll to resist frenzy when the effect wears off.
rollResults.failure: No transformation takes place.
rollResults.success: The vampire transforms her body into animate stone, which lasts until she stops paying 3 Vitae per turn. For the duration, she benefits from all active effects of Resilience and Vigor each turn without additional Vitae expenditure, and adds her Protean dots to her effective Resilience. All her unarmed attacks deal lethal damage. If she takes lethal damage in her rightmost Health box, she may reflexively activate Unmarked Grave at no cost regardless of the material’s Durability.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire also becomes immune to the Knocked Down Tilt for the duration.

devotions.name: Celebrity
devotions.summary: Turn a fan's praise into a temporary Social Merit.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have inflicted the Charmed or Enthralled Condition on the target.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Empathy + Majesty vs. Resolve + Supernatural Tolerance

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire’s efforts backfire, causing his victim’s unfettered excitement to turn people off. Any attempt to use the Majesty Discipline on anyone in the general location where the victim lives or spends most of her time lose the 10-again quality until her prerequisite Condition wears off, and further attempts to influence her after that take a -2 penalty until successful.
rollResults.failure: The vampire’s insinuations are too subtle to kindle his victim’s fanaticism.
rollResults.success: The elder fans the flame of his victim’s enthusiasm for him, prompting her to rave about her new best friend at every opportunity and spread his influence. At the end of every scene while the victim is still Charmed or Enthralled, as long as she had reasonable opportunity to engage in conversation with someone, the vampire gains a temporary dot of one of the following Merits: Allies, Fame, Herd, Retainer, Staff, or Status. The effects of this Devotion end when the victim no longer has the prerequisite Condition. Attempts to use the Majesty Discipline on anyone in the general location where the victim lives or spends most of her time gain the 9-again quality, or 8-again if the duration lasts longer than a week (e.g. as the result of The Wish, Vampire: The Requiem Second Edition, p. 148).
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: Attempts to use the Majesty Discipline on anyone in the general location where the victim lives or spends most of her time gain the 8-again quality right away.

devotions.name: Consumption
devotions.summary: Possess a victim over any distance using only your voice.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be currently possessing a valid target using the Dominate Discipline.

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim’s free will asserts itself violently, immediately ending the possession and any other effect or Condition the vampire has inflicted upon her using Dominate or any Devotions that require Dominate.
rollResults.failure: The vampire continues to possess the victim, but nothing more happens. He can try again at a cumulative onedie penalty for each attempt.
rollResults.success: The vampire destroys the victim’s will and leaves her vulnerable to further possession. The victim gains the persistent Enslaved Condition (Vampire: The Requiem Second Edition, p. 303). As long as that Condition persists, the vampire may possess the victim again at a cost of 1 Vitae without a roll and without spending the Willpower cost. As long as the victim can hear his voice, he may possess her from any distance.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: Whenever the vampire possesses the victim’s body he gains a faint impression of her memories, giving him a +2 bonus to any Social rolls he makes while deliberately posing as the victim among people who may know her.

devotions.name: Crush of Years
devotions.summary: Press the weight of centuries upon a target.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Expression + Nightmare vs. Composure + Supernatural Tolerance

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The elder’s mastery of this Devotion comes from centuries of enduring her own slow realization of what immortality truly means, and she brings it all crashing down on her own head. She suffers the Crushed Condition herself.
rollResults.failure: The vampire’s efforts don’t impress her audience.
rollResults.success: Anyone who fails to overcome the vampire’s roll succumbs to the full forbidden knowledge of eternity, and suffers the Crushed Condition.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire regains a Willpower point, having stared immortality full in the face and come to terms with it.

devotions.name: Legion
devotions.summary: Use the senses of all nearby animals of a chosen type.
devotions.requirement: Consume blood from a single type of animal equivalent to 10 Vitae before using this Devotion.

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire forges a connection, but his own Beast overrides his intentions, provoking a fight-orflight response. All affected animals either flee at once in an incredibly conspicuous manner — massive flocks of ravens blacking out the moon, unnatural hordes of cats filling the street — or zero in on the vampire’s location and attack in droves, depending on the animal’s nature.
rollResults.failure: The animal blood fails to take hold and the vampire forges no connection, or the area doesn’t contain enough animals of that type.
rollResults.success: The animal blood within the vampire’s veins forges a connection between himself and all animals of the type she consumed within (Blood Potency) miles. For the duration, he receives passive sensory input from them as vague impressions and flashes, gaining +5 dice to all Perception rolls and rolls to search out or investigate anything in range, as long as the animals have an opportunity to perceive it. In addition, the vampire can spend a Vitae to take an active glimpse, taking over one animal’s senses as an instant action. He chooses a location within range and shuts down his own senses for as long as he likes to ride along with an animal there. By default, he has no control over its actions but can sense anything it can, including things he wouldn’t normally pick up like pheromones or sounds only audible to canine ears. He can switch animals at any time with another Vitae and an instant action. The vampire can use Feral Whispers on any animal he’s currently using for an active glimpse.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: Once per active glimpse, the vampire may make his presence behind the animal’s eyes known to someone in its vicinity. If he succeeds on a Presence + Intimidation roll, resisted by the target’s Composure, the target gains the Spooked Condition without quite realizing why the creature is so unsettling.

devotions.name: Malignant Smog
devotions.summary: Turn Primeval Miasma into toxic gas that inflicts Tilts.
devotions.effect: This Devotion enhances the effect of Primeval Miasma, transforming the vampire from a cloud of hungry smoke to a cloud of toxic gas. By spending 2 additional Vitae when she activates Primeval Miasma, she doubles the maximum diameter of her cloud and can float at her normal Speed. When she activates Malignant Smog, she chooses a Tilt based on the type of gas she becomes. Anyone who enters her Miasma must succeed on a Stamina roll once every (10 – Blood Potency) turns he stays there to avoid falling prey to the Tilt, with its most severe possible effect. If the vampire transforms into mustard gas, she might inflict the Sick (grave) or Blinded (both eyes) Tilt, as blisters and chemical burns cover the victim’s body inside and out. Transforming into a psychotropic inhalant might inflict the Insane or Insensate Tilt, while becoming concentrated smog or tobacco smoke can cause Poisoned (grave) Tilt. The Tilt wears off once the victim spends a number of consecutive turns outside the cloud equal to the elder’s Blood Potency.

devotions.name: Pass Into Yesteryear
devotions.summary: Make others forget those bound to you by Vinculum.
devotions.effect: Whenever the elder feeds his blood to someone, he may bolster it with this Devotion to infuse his own history of self-inflicted ostracism. If his victim suffers the onset or strengthening of the Vinculum from this drink, she gains the Forgotten Condition (see p. 136).

devotions.name: Preternatural Instinct
devotions.summary: Sense danger before it happens and read traces of hostile intent.
devotions.effect: For the duration of this Devotion, the vampire may apply her Defense against attacks she can’t see coming, as long as she’s still able to physically react. Additionally, if she spends a Vitae to move to the head of the Initiative queue, she automatically wins any Clash of Wills that contests her ability to act first unless her foe also uses this Devotion, in which case the Clash occurs as normal.

devotions.name: Spontaneous Ignition
devotions.summary: Set a touched target on fire.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must touch her target.

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire sets herself on fire.
rollResults.failure: The vampire’s victim feels an uncomfortable heat, but does not combust.
rollResults.success: The vampire’s victim catches fire at the torch level for both size and heat (see Vampire: The Requiem Second Edition, p. 103). For each success rolled beyond the result of the victim’s resistance roll, move either the size or intensity of the flame up on the chart by one. The flames burn for a number of turns equal to the vampire’s Blood Potency, but the victim can try to extinguish them sooner by taking instant actions to smother them or put them out with water or a fire extinguisher. Each instant action spent combating the fire reduces it in size by one level on the chart. If it burns for more than one turn, it can ignite flammable objects in the victim’s vicinity.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire enjoys the benefits of a larger and/or hotter flame, as above.

devotions.name: Unbridled Force
devotions.summary: Perform feats of raw strength at a distance.
devotions.effect: For the duration, the vampire may perform feats of raw strength at a distance by simply exuding force with his gestures. He can push, pull, throw, or lift any object within (Blood Potency x 10) yards/meters that he normally could without touching it, so long as he can perceive it, and can make Brawl attacks the same way. No fine manipulation is possible, but he can use his Vigor Discipline to increase his Strength as normal for the purposes of this Devotion. He still must have at least one hand free to direct this force. The vampire may not use this power at anything less than his full strength — he can’t gently slide a bookcase aside, deposit a person lightly onto the ground, or pull his punches.

devotions.name: Kin Maker
devotions.summary: Pijavica magic that infects another vampire with a gestating childe.
devotions.effect: If successful, this Devotion causes the Kindred to erode from the inside, leaving only a shell with a new Pijavica inside. This process takes 4 days, and if the cocoon is disrupted or destroyed before the gestation period is over, the vampire dies. This Devotion can only be used on a willing Kindred with a Blood Potency rating lower than the user’s.

devotions.name: Dead Man's Reprieve
devotions.summary: Prepare a bath that cloaks its occupants' presence.
devotions.effect: The vampire prepares a rare plant in a boiling ritual bath. On success, each success grants one bather Cloak of Night for four hours. Exceptional success instead grants every bather Cloak of Night and Resilience •• for six hours. Failure produces an impure mixture; dramatic failure destroys part of the plant supply, kills one bather, penalizes the next attempt made within a week, and inflicts Fugue on the ritualist.

devotions.name: Body of Will
devotions.summary: Ignore wound penalties briefly and turn new injuries into free Vigor activations.
devotions.effect: For one turn per success, the character suffers no wound penalties. As well, during any turn where he takes damage, he does not need to spend Vitae to activate one effect of Vigor.

devotions.name: Chain of Command
devotions.summary: Plant one Dominate effect in a victim for later use against a designated subject.
devotions.dicePool: Intelligence + Persuasion + Dominate vs. Resolve + Blood Potency
devotions.effect: The victim does not have to resist if he so chooses. If successful, the vampire plants one of her Dominate effects deep within the victim. At the specified moment, he uses the Dominate command as directed. However, this uses the vampire’s dice pool, not the victim’s.

devotions.name: Cloak the Gathering
devotions.summary: Extend Obfuscate to a group within the vampire's aura.
devotions.effect: Cloak the Gathering enhances the effect of Touch of Shadow and Cloak of Night. By paying two extra points of Vitae, the vampire can expand the effect of Touch of Shadow to encompass a number of people equal to his Blood Potency, though subject to the normal Size modifiers of Touch of Shadow. He can also opt to activate Face in the Crowd at the same time. If he also pays the extra cost for Cloak of Night to vanish completely rather than fading into the background, the effect applies to everyone masked by Cloak the Gathering — so for four points of Vitae total he can vanish from sight along with a number of people equal to his Blood Potency. The vampire doesn’t have to touch everyone he takes with him, but they must be within his (Obfuscate + Blood Potency) yards (meters).

devotions.name: Conditioning
devotions.summary: Erode a Mesmerized victim's will over repeated sessions.
devotions.requirement: Victim has Mesmerized; same victim only once every two nights
devotions.dicePool: Wits + Subterfuge + Dominate vs. Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim reasserts his will in a dramatic fashion. He resolves the Mesmerized Condition; he keeps the bonus to resist further Mesmerize attempts for the next week.
rollResults.failure: The vampire cannot get her victim to repeat exactly the same tasks for now.
rollResults.success: The victim’s will bends before the vampire. He gains the Subservient Condition (p. 306).
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim’s will bends like grass before the storm of the vampire’s commands. Mark an extra cross when applying the Subservient Condition. Each time the vampire inflicts the Subservient Condition on a character, his player should put a cross or other mark above one of his Willpower dots, starting from the left. Each dot can only have one mark. If the Subservient Condition is allowed to fade naturally, remove the rightmost cross. When each of the character’s Willpower dots has a mark above it, he exchanges the Subservient Condition for the Enslaved Condition (p. 303).

devotions.name: Cross-Contamination
devotions.summary: Blend awe and terror into a disorienting emotional aura.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Empathy + lower of Majesty or Nightmare
devotions.effect: Once active, this Devotion confuses everyone in the vampire’s immediate presence, forcing their emotions to swing between adoration and disgust. This causes a handful of effects: • They become confused and disoriented, not sure what to think or feel. This reduces their effective Composure by one dot. • The vampire becomes a beacon for the crowd’s attention. Looking away from her requires a Composure + Blood Potency roll, contested against her successes. The victim must only meet the vampire’s successes. • Any rolls to resist Persuasion- or Intimidation-based Social maneuvers lose the 10-again quality. • A character may not have Awe or Dread Presence active at the same time as Cross-Contamination.

devotions.name: Cult of Personality
devotions.summary: Broadcast Loyalty across a crowd.
devotions.effect: If successful, this Devotion washes the effects of Loyalty over the crowd. It affects any character with fewer Composure + Blood Potency dots than the vampire has successes. Those afflicted gain the Enthralled Condition.

devotions.name: Enchantment
devotions.summary: Redirect Loyalty to another person, place, or object.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Empathy + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency
devotions.effect: If successful, this Devotion works as Loyalty, but the vampire can designate a source for the Enthralled Condition instead of focusing it on herself. All the other parameters remain the same, but the victim insists on defending and cherishing a different person, place, or thing. She has to somehow communicate the desired subject of the Enchantment to the victim for this Devotion to work.

devotions.name: Enfeebling Aura
devotions.summary: Trade Majesty dots to suppress a victim's physical Disciplines for the scene.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Intimidation + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency
devotions.effect: If successful, this Devotion temporarily removes dots of the victim’s Celerity, Resilience, and Vigor, in whatever combination the vampire wishes. The vampire removes dots one-for-one along with her Majesty dots for the scene, up to her successes. For example, she can sacrifice three dots of her Majesty, losing access to them for the scene, to remove two dots of Vigor and one dot of Resilience from her victim for the scene.

devotions.name: Force of Nature
devotions.summary: Assume multiple Protean advantages and redistribute Physical Attributes.
devotions.effect: When activating Force of Nature, the vampire gains as many of the advantages of Predatory Aspect, Beast’s Skin, and Unnatural Aspect as she wishes, without Vitae costs. She can adopt additional modifications or shed existing ones as a reflexive action. As well, with an instant action, she can shift a number of Physical Attribute dots equal to her Protean to other Physical Attributes. These change derived traits, and can exceed her normal limitations. The effects of Force of Nature last for the scene.

devotions.name: Foul Grave
devotions.summary: Project predatory aura while resting in an Unmarked Grave.
devotions.effect: While the vampire does not fully maintain all his senses, he’s vaguely aware of those nearby. He gets a brief mental glimpse of mortals in the vicinity, and still feels the auras of Kindred. While in his Unmarked Grave, he can activate predatory aura normally, but it costs a point of Vitae in addition to the Willpower required if the victim is Kindred.

devotions.name: Gargoyle's Vigilance
devotions.summary: Gain complete vigilance over a haven while remaining still.
devotions.requirement: Remain stationary for at least ten minutes in a Safe Place
devotions.effect: This Devotion requires the vampire to remain completely still, in a location reflected by the Safe Place Merit (see p. 123). She has to be stationary for at least ten minutes before this Devotion offers its benefits. While stationary, she has full use of her Auspex abilities, centered on any single spot of her choosing within the haven. Having full awareness, she may change the spot at will. She receives +5 to any rolls to detect intruders. If she decides to move against an intruder, she gains +5 to her Initiative for the scene. As well, she does not need to spend Vitae to activate her Resilience. With a point of Willpower, this Devotion may be used while the vampire slumbers. An advanced version of this Devotion exists, utilizing Protean 5, costing 4 Experiences. This version allows the vampire to become a statue, immune to fire and sunlight while remaining stationary.

devotions.name: Hint of Fear
devotions.summary: Use Face of the Beast as a rapid reflexive glance.
devotions.cost: 1 Vitae plus Face of the Beast's cost
devotions.dicePool: None; roll Face of the Beast normally
devotions.effect: This Devotion allows the vampire to use Face of the Beast as a reflexive action. This requires a second point of Vitae, so the vampire must be able to spend two vitae in a turn to use it without preparation.

devotions.name: Juggernaut's Gait
devotions.summary: Become briefly immune to all damage.
devotions.effect: This Devotion requires the vampire spend five Vitae per turn she wishes to remain immune to harm. During this time, all damage — bashing, lethal, aggravated, even damage caused by the fire or by sunlight — is absorbed into her blood before it reaches her skin. She takes no damage from any source. Note that this Devotion does not allow the vampire to spend additional Vitae; she must be able to spend five in a turn to use Juggernaut’s Gait without preparation. She can spend the first four on preceding turns, and the fifth when she wishes to evoke the protection. However, invoking the Devotion is reflexive, and the Vitae may be spent after an opponent makes a successful attack roll.

devotions.name: Quicken Sight
devotions.summary: Perceive fast events in slow motion and react accordingly.
devotions.effect: When activated, Quicken Sight lasts for a turn. The vampire can examine the details on fast-moving items, and respond to things outside the normal human spectrum. She can read multiple pages of text in three seconds. She can apply her Defense to ranged attacks, and can benefit from aiming instantly. Vampire: the Requiem

devotions.name: Reason's Salon
devotions.summary: Suppress predatory aggression within a prepared gathering place.
devotions.effect: The vampire must spread his Vitae about the location (usually a building or clearing) he wishes to calm. Throughout the evening, vampires within suffer the user’s Resilience dots as a penalty to all predatory aura rolls. As well, they add the same number to any rolls to resist frenzy.

devotions.name: Riot
devotions.summary: Drive a wide area into selfish, destructive bedlam.
devotions.effect: When activated, Riot overwhelms a wide area (a city block, or half mile), and everyone within it. Anyone with a lower Composure + Blood Potency than the vampire’s successes suffers from the Bestial, Competitive, and Wanton Conditions. The victims burst into aggressive, base behaviors. This is not animalistic behavior; it’s destructive, short-sighted, and selfish. It causes a bloodbath of massive proportions. Use of this Devotion is considered a Humanity 1 breaking point.

devotions.name: Shared Sight
devotions.summary: Temporarily lend Auspex dots to another person.
devotions.effect: When activating this Devotion, your character may impart to another a number of dots of her Auspex equal to or less than the successes rolled. The recipient has full access to the abilities granted, but cannot use the lender’s dice for activation. to the borrower must make rolls with just Attributes, Skills, and any Auspex dots he may have. The imparted dots last for the remainder of the scene. During this time, the lender loses that many dice from all Auspex rolls.

devotions.name: Shatter the Shroud
devotions.summary: Destroy a concealment effect after winning a Clash of Wills.
devotions.effect: Activate this Devotion any time your character wins in a Clash of Wills roll (see p. 125) to pierce a hiding ability. Not only does your character win the Clash of Wills, but the victim’s hiding effect ends immediately. He can re-activate it normally on the next turn, if applicable.

devotions.name: Stalwart Servant
devotions.summary: Lend Resilience through Vitae to a servant.
devotions.effect: Once the subject feeds, the vampire imparts her own Resilience dots onto him. He still needs to spend Vitae to activate the Resilience, but he receives one as part of the invocation. He cannot benefit from this Devotion if he already has Resilience at an equal or higher level than the vampire. This Devotion lasts one night. The vampire may maintain a number of subjects equal to her Blood Potency. The drinker gains the passive benefits of Resilience, and the vampire does not lose access to the Discipline.

devotions.name: Subsume the Lesser Beast
devotions.summary: Project the vampire's mind into a predatory or scavenging animal.
devotions.requirement: Feed 1 Vitae to the animal; included in the cost
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Animal Ken + Animalism – animal Resolve

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The animal throws off the vampire’s attempt at control. For the rest of the night, the vampire manifests a number of physical tics akin to the animal’s behavior. Any Social rolls suffer a –2 penalty.
rollResults.failure: The vampire cannot take total control of the animal yet.
rollResults.success: The vampire takes over the animal’s body for one night per success. She uses the animal’s Physical Attributes and Skills in place of her own, and cannot use her own Physical or Combat Merits. She can stay awake during the day by spending a point of Willpower at dawn, and takes no damage from sunlight; if she does not spend the Willpower, she returns to her body. She cannot use any Disciplines or Blood Sorcery while in the animal’s body, but can use any of its senses, natural weapons, or forms of locomotion. While she commands the animal’s body, her own body lies in a torpor-like state, awaiting her return — though she must spend a point of Vitae every night to remain active. If the vampire remains in the animal’s body for so long that her body slips into torpor, she immediately snaps back into her body.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire can still access some of the power of her blood even in the animal’s body. She keeps access to Auspex when in the animal’s body.

devotions.name: Summoning (Dominate)
devotions.summary: Compel a previously Mesmerized subject to travel to the vampire.
devotions.requirement: Mesmerized the victim within the last year
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Persuasion + Dominate vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim knows that the vampire wants her to go to him, and does everything in her power to actively avoid him, using her sense of where he is to aid her.
rollResults.failure: Something prevents the victim from coming to the vampire’s side.
rollResults.success: The victim knows where the vampire is and has a sudden compulsion to travel to him. She will travel to meet him by the most direct means available to her, stopping only for necessities. The compulsion lasts for the rest of the night from the vampire’s perspective — if he’s calling someone from the other side of the world, the effects last until sunrise wherever he is.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim’s compulsion lasts throughout the day and for all of the next night as well, long enough for many international journeys — or at least for the victim to find a way to smuggle herself overseas.

suggestedModifiers.situation: The vampire knows exactly where his victim is.
The vampire has no idea where his victim is, but knows that she is within the same domain.
The victim dislikes the vampire and resents being summoned.
The victim is over 500 miles away, or despises the vampire.
The victim is on the other side of the world.

devotions.name: Summoning (Majesty)
devotions.summary: Compel a previous subject of Awe to travel to the vampire.
devotions.requirement: Used Awe on the victim within the last year
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Persuasion + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim knows that the vampire wants her to go to him, and does everything in her power to actively avoid him, using her sense of where he is to aid her.
rollResults.failure: Something prevents the victim from coming to the vampire’s side.
rollResults.success: The victim knows where the vampire is and has a sudden compulsion to travel to him. She will travel to meet him by the most direct means available to her, stopping only for necessities. The compulsion lasts for the rest of the night from the vampire’s perspective — if he’s calling someone from the other side of the world, the effects last until sunrise wherever he is.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim’s compulsion lasts throughout the day and for all of the next night as well, long enough for many international journeys — or at least for the victim to find a way to smuggle herself overseas.

suggestedModifiers.situation: The vampire knows exactly where his victim is.
The vampire has no idea where his victim is, but knows that she is within the same domain.
The victim dislikes the vampire and resents being summoned.
The victim is over 500 miles away, or despises the vampire.
The victim is on the other side of the world.

devotions.name: Sun's Brutal Dreamscape
devotions.summary: Make a sleeping Kindred victim share the vampire's sunlight wounds.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Empathy + Nightmare vs. Composure + Blood Potency
devotions.effect: Once used successfully, this Devotion remains active for a number of nights equal to the successes rolled. While it is active, the victim, selected by touch, suffers every sunlight wound the vampire takes, so long as the victim is asleep when the damage occurs. The vampire still takes the damage. This damage can awaken the victim. A victim so awakened wakes with the Frightened Condition (see p. 303).

devotions.name: The Wish
devotions.summary: Temporarily exalt a consenting mortal before binding them in lasting enthrallment.
devotions.requirement: Mortal target freely agrees and feeds from the vampire; usable once per character
devotions.effect: To use this Devotion, the victim must agree to the terms; three nights of power, but he willl belong to the vampire afterward. The terms can be that vague, but must be stated and agreed to, without any supernatural coercion. The victim must feed from the vampire as part of the agreement. When the deal is struck, the victim gains a number of advantages for three nights: • He gains two levels of Celerity and Vigor. He can activate them by spending Willpower instead of Vitae. • He gains three levels of Majesty. He can activate these with Willpower instead of Vitae. • He needs no sleep, and can go without food and water without issue. At the end of the period, he gains the Persistent Enthralled Condition. It persists indefinitely.

devotions.name: Touch of Deprivation
devotions.summary: Temporarily deny a touched victim one sense or one known Auspex ability.
devotions.requirement: Touch the victim
devotions.dicePool: Intelligence + Medicine + Auspex vs. Resolve + Blood Potency
devotions.effect: To activate this Devotion, the vampire must touch his victim (see Touching an Opponent on p. 177). If successful, the vampire denies the victim’s chosen sense for the remainder of the scene. This Devotion can be used to deny the victim one of her Auspex abilities, if known.

devotions.name: Undying Familiar
devotions.summary: Make a living ghouled animal rise under Raise Familiar when killed.
devotions.effect: Activate this Devotion and Raise the Familiar at the same time, when feeding an animal Vitae. As long as the animal remains ghouled, this Devotion remains in effect. If the animal dies while ghouled, it immediately rises under Raise the Familiar, but its undead existence is measured in weeks instead of nights.

devotions.name: Wet Dream
devotions.summary: Seed a sleeping victim with intertwined fear and desire.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Empathy + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency
devotions.effect: If successful, this Devotion takes effect when next the victim sleeps. His frightening and arousing dreams cause the both the Spooked and Swooning Conditions (see p. 305 and p. 306). The vampire chooses the subject of both Conditions. The victim sheds each Condition individually. However, the two Conditions only give one Beat, and only once they’re both resolved.

devotions.name: Vermin Flood
devotions.summary: Call a destructive plague of small animals over a prepared area.
devotions.requirement: Spread Vitae over an area no larger than a small house or alley
devotions.effect: To activate this devotion, the vampire must spread her Vitae over an area no larger than a small house or an alleyway. Once activated, every animal of Size 2 or lower immediately swarms with the speed and intensity of the vampire’s Celerity and Vigor (persistent effects only). This includes any vermin, cats, birds, and insects. They wash over the area, tearing, chewing, and destroying. Everything in the area but the vampire takes lethal damage equal to the vampire’s Animalism dots each turn. This ignores any non-magical armor. Characters moving in the swarm move at half Speed. The vermin will not leave the affected area for the remainder of the scene. Only a very large fire will slow the swarm, and even then, only in the area aflame.

devotions.name: Wraith's Presence
devotions.summary: Project a false image elsewhere while using Cloak of Night.
devotions.effect: Activate this Devotion when using Cloak of Night. The vampire projects an exact image of the desired subject in another place she can see. The image stays mostly still unless the vampire concentrates on moving it. It’ll make the necessary motions to appear realistic — for example, an image of a human will breathe. The image cannot talk or make noises. The image vanishes as soon as anyone touches it. Breaking this effect without touching the phantom uses the normal Clash of Wills rules (see p. 125).

devotions.name: Bezoar Thorns
devotions.summary: Shapes swallowed material into defensive thorns.
devotions.requirement: Before he activates Protean, vampire must consume inorganic material with Size equal to the points he wants to use to enhance his Discipline.
devotions.effect: While manifesting bestial traits through Predatory Aspect, the Baetyl can augment his adaptations with materials he’s recently devoured. These changes look even more unnatural than normal Protean adaptations, with talons of iron growing out from the Termite’s fingers or new sensory organs made from camera lenses and plastic emerging from his face. When activating Predatory Aspect, the vampire has a number of points to spend on the enhancement of her adaptations equal to Auspex dots: • For one point, the Baetyl applies a +1 modifier on any action that uses the adaptation. This can be applied multiple times for a single adaptation, or spread out over multiple traits. • For two points, the Baetyl only needs three successes to achieve an exceptional success when rolling a Skill associated with his adaptation. If the adaptation doesn’t have a specific Skill, choose one (with Storyteller approval). • For three points, the Baetyl gains the rote quality on a single Skill associated with his adaptation.

devotions.name: Chimera
devotions.summary: Builds a hybrid body from several consumed materials.
devotions.requirement: The vampire uplifts a dead animal with Raise the Familiar and spends additional Vitae (included in the cost) coated over a piece of inanimate material.
devotions.effect: The vampire merges her subject with the inanimate material. At base, it gains two points of general armor and a level of Size. In addition, for each dot of Protean, the vampire can apply a permanent adaptation from Predatory Aspect, manifesting as unnatural protrusions of metal, stone, or plastic, depending on the material she fed the creature.

devotions.name: Stone Specter
devotions.summary: Merges an altered body into masonry and mineral surfaces.
devotions.effect: Whenever the vampire enters her Unmarked Grave, she retains her sense of the surrounding world as long as she remains awake, and she can use any Auspex power she knows on people and objects who walk near her hiding spot. If the vampire enters daysleep while in this grave, she can spend a Vitae to trigger a single Auspex power she knows at some point in the day, with the exception of Twilight Projection. The trigger must involve a person or object within (Blood Potency) meters of the Unmarked Grave, but otherwise the condition can be as specific or as broad as the vampire likes. For example, it might apply to a specific person, or only ghouls, or just anyone wearing a particular brand of cologne. If this condition isn’t met before sundown, the Vitae spent is wasted. If it goes off, the vampire must pay the usual cost of the power and her player must make any appropriate roll. Information gained this way takes the form of a prophetic dream that the Baetyl will remember upon waking up.

devotions.name: Wisdom of Stones
devotions.summary: Reads impressions held in swallowed stone.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must consume an object with her bloodline gift and spend an additional Vitae (included in the cost).
devotions.effect: Instead of a bonus to Auspex, the vampire gains access to the effect of the Dream Visions Merit ( Vampire, p. 111) as if she had rolled a success. If a character shed blood on this object, the vampire can ignore the usual restriction of having to use the effect on a stranger. The Baetyl can only use this Devotion once per night.

devotions.name: Fata Morgana
devotions.summary: Weaves a compelling mirage through voice and performance.
devotions.effect: For the rest of the scene, the vampire can use Obfuscate effects with her voice rather than via touch. Use the system for Touch of Shadow, applying any costs from other Obfuscate effects as normal. She can use her Discipline on any object or person she can see within (10 × Blood Potency) meters; all she needs to do is paint a word picture of the desired effect, though the result is limited by her level of Obfuscate. For example, she can’t make a door look like a castle gate unless she knows The Familiar Stranger.

devotions.name: Siren's Lure
devotions.summary: Draws listeners toward the Cerrid's song.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must perform music or recite poetry in a performative manner.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Expression + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency (highest in a group)

rollResults.success: Anyone who hears the vampire’s music will be drawn to her, moving through whatever means they can until they reach the source of the tune. However, if the vampire stops playing, the effect ends.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victims also gain the Swooning Condition toward the vampire.
rollResults.failure: Yeah, they’re not falling for that one.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire’s music takes on a sinister edge she didn’t intend, and passersby will be sure to keep as far away as possible.

devotions.name: Song of Myself
devotions.summary: Uses performance to reinforce identity against supernatural control.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must perform for the victim for at least a few minutes.
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Expression + Majesty vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire becomes the victim’s only focus. He must spend a Willpower to even look away unless the Cerrid dismisses him, and for as long as she keeps playing, normal successes using Majesty powers on the victim are treated as exceptional; rolled exceptional successes apply an extended duration to the effect, as if the victim had a blood bond to the vampire.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: In addition to the above, treat the victim as if he had a first-stage Vinculum to the vampire for the duration.
rollResults.failure: Don’t quit your day job.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim becomes hostile to the vampire, and any subsequent performances will sound like nails on a chalkboard to his ear. Consider their impression of the vampire Hostile for the rest of the night.

devotions.name: Fated Strike
devotions.summary: Invokes a Crúac-charged attack at the moment fate opens.
devotions.requirement: This Devotion can only be used with unarmed attacks, or when attacking with melee weapons no larger than Size 1. Natural attacks granted by Protean count as unarmed.
devotions.effect: Before an appropriate attack, the vampire can activate this power to ignore an amount of her victim’s Defense equal to her Protean dots. If she does, she cannot use the active effect of Vigor to add damage to the attack if it’s successful, as she’s modifying her limbs for flexibility rather than strength.

devotions.name: Paths of Blood
devotions.summary: Reads possible routes through violence and sacrifice.
devotions.requirement: The animal must be at least Size 1 and one of the vampire’s stored forms granted by Beast’s Skin.
devotions.dicePool: Dexterity + Animal Ken + Animalism – animal’s Stamina

rollResults.success: The vampire rapidly dissolves into nothing and then bursts forth from the body of a nearby animal in an explosion of gore. The vampire must have unbroken line of sight to the subject and be able to see it with her naked eye, but these are the only restrictions on how far she can travel using this power. This does no harm to the vampire, but the animal always dies.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire finds traversing the paths of blood and bone particularly natural. Her next use of this power on the same type of animal costs no Vitae.
rollResults.failure: The vampire stays exactly where she is.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The animal emerges from the vampire’s body, with disastrous results. The Stormcrow takes unavoidable aggravated damage equal to the creature’s Size as something tries to claw its way out of her from the inside.

devotions.name: Therian Excision
devotions.summary: Cuts a destructive impulse away from another vampire's Beast.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Intimidation + Animalism vs. Resolve + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The victim loses access to her feral nature; she gains the Beastless Condition.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The victim becomes Beaten Down until his Beast returns. This applies to social interactions as well as violence.
rollResults.failure: The other Beast proves more persistent than expected.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The Daimonion’s Beast howls in frustration as it fails to tear out its supposed lesser. The Daimonion immediately falls to frenzy with a goal appropriate to the cir cumstances, usually trying to prove its dominance in other ways.

devotions.name: Blood-Eye Gaze
devotions.summary: Reads lunar and predatory truths in blood.
devotions.effect: A bloody haze covers the Dead Wolf’s eyes, and his vision gives way to what lies in the Hisil. The vampire now sees the shape of the local Shadow, as well as any spirits in his vicinity. When he activates this power, the Namus-Ur can choose to have it apply to both eyes or only one.
