Using both eyes leaves him completely blind to the physical world, whereas using one allows for vision in both worlds at once, but imposes a –2 on all sight-based actions due to conflicting imagery. The vampire may deactivate the power as a reflexive action at any time.

devotions.name: Hunter's True Form
devotions.summary: Assumes the bloodline's perfected hunting shape.
devotions.effect: The vampire transforms into a hulking, fur-covered hybrid of man and beast, though he more resembles the classic Hollywood wolfman than the eight-foot terrors Uratha can become (unless, of course, she also manifests the Moon’s Blessing of Sublunario). While in this form, the vampire gains a level of Size, one point of general armor, adds Protean to Intimidation-based rolls, and does not need to be in frenzy to attack with his fangs without a grapple. The first time the vampire activates this Devotion in a scene, he must immediately resist frenzy as if provoked to anger. Even if the vampire succeeds at reigning in his Beast, the boiling rage he feels in this form imposes a –2 on all Mental actions, and to all Social rolls not based on Animal Ken or Intimidation. If the Dead Wolf possesses the Moon’s Blessing, he does not suffer this penalty when using Insight Skills.

devotions.name: Vessel of Bone and Blood
devotions.summary: Takes on a werewolf-like vessel without importing werewolf rules.
devotions.requirement: The mostly intact corpse of a creature Size 2 or larger, or many smaller corpses with equivalent mass.
devotions.action: Extended (target is five successes, with each roll representing ten minutes of sculpting, carving, and tinkering)

rollResults.success: The Dead Wolf successfully crafts a crude effigy that invites a nearby spirit in Twilight to use it as a mouthpiece into the material world. If the vampire knows the name of the spirit he wishes to speak to, he can incorporate it into the crafting of the totem, and only that spirit may speak through it. Otherwise, any spirit in the vicinity can use the totem to communicate. This effigy lasts a single night before crumbling into a pile of rotting offal unless the vampire invests a point of Willpower into its creation, in which case, the item retains its properties until it’s destroyed. Note that while the totem allows communication between the Namus-Ur and spirits, it does nothing to bridge understanding. That said, Dead Wolves have their own ways of interpreting spirits (see Sublunario, above).
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The totem is especially well crafted and allows clear communication between spirit and vampire, even if they would not normally share a language.
rollResults.failure: The vampire creates nothing but failed taxidermy.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: Something about the vampire’s creation deeply offends the local spirits, and he suffers bouts of mis fortune for the rest of the night as they torment him from behind the veil.

devotions.name: Barn Raising
devotions.summary: Turns family cooperation into supernaturally efficient collective labor.
devotions.requirement: The victim must have the Mesmerized Condition when the vampire activates this Devotion, and she must then implant an Iron Edict trigger using Entombed Command, paying all necessary costs.
devotions.effect: The vampire’s victim becomes a vector for her commands. Others won’t carry out her orders with the same single-mindedness, but they’ll feel an urge to help. If the victim undertakes a task while under the effect of the Dominated Condition, up to (Blood Potency × 2) people within the vicinity will find their way over to check things out. Anyone who helps the victim gains a Willpower for their effort. Those who accept this Willpower suffer a –3 modifier to resist the vampire’s Dominate powers for the rest of the night.

devotions.name: Interloper
devotions.summary: Marks and punishes an outsider intruding on family ground.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must smear a point of Vitae on the subject (included in the cost). Oberlochs usually spit on their victims.

rollResults.success: Any mortal stranger who sees, hears, or smells the victim must resist the effect of Feral Infection (Vampire, p. 127), applying the vampire’s successes as a penalty. On a failure, the subject of this Devotion becomes the target of the bystander’s rage until he’s dead or the scene ends, whichever comes first. Anyone who suffers this frenzy effect won’t quite remember what happened when they come out of their rage, and they’ll dismiss any signs of violence until they have a chance to clean up. At that point, they just won’t think about it at all.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: Bystanders will attack the victim until he’s dead or the end of the night.
rollResults.failure: People might look at the victim a little funny, but they won’t bother him unless he bothers them.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim takes on an aura of innocence, and the vampire suffers a 5-die penalty on all actions to turn people against him, including Disciplines. He cannot be the subject of this Devotion for the rest of the night, and he cannot be made the target of a normal use of Feral Infection.

devotions.name: Christine
devotions.summary: Awakens the Ride to act in defense of its owner.
devotions.requirement: The vampire merges into her vehicle using Unmarked Grave.
devotions.effect: As long as she benefits from Unmarked Grave or until the next sunset (whichever comes first), the Verlice can control the vehicle she resides in, allowing her to perceive her surroundings and operate the vehicle as if they were in the passenger seat. This allows her the added protection of a metal frame, as well as the ability to move about in the daylight, provided she can remain awake.

devotions.name: Know the Road
devotions.summary: Lets the bonded Ride find a viable route through unfamiliar territory.
devotions.effect: The vampire senses obstacles along roughly Auspex × 5 miles of road and exceptionally succeeds on three successes when driving around them. She also knows the correct route to her chosen destination without learning details about the places crossed, adds Auspex to navigation actions, and cannot be surprised while following that route.

devotions.name: Scavenge
devotions.summary: Cannibalizes nearby wreckage to repair the Ride.
devotions.requirement: Anoint the replacement part with the vampire's blood.
devotions.effect: The vampire replaces a damaged component of her Ride with a scavenged part that fits and functions regardless of its normal size or type. Mundane repairs are still required, but Protean adds to relevant Crafts rolls. The improvised component works until sunrise, when another Vitae or a proper replacement is required.

devotions.name: Hold Together
devotions.summary: Keeps a damaged Ride functioning past ordinary failure.
devotions.duration: Scenes equal to successes Roll Results Success: The vampire’s Resilience dots are applied to the vehicle’s Durability, and he ignores penalties from environ mental hazards on Drive actions. This also obviates the effect of any moderate damage to the Ride, though it can’t account for grievous damage like missing tires or a removed brake line. Exceptional Success: The Verlice and his vehicle are truly one, operating at peak efficiency. The duration lasts for the current night and the next. Failure: The car is no worse for wear, but it’s no better either. Dramatic Failure: Something critical within the vehicle breaks instead of being protected. Reduce the Ride’s dice modifier by three until it can be repaired. Know Road ( A u s p e x •••) When all you have is the road, knowing where you’re going and how to get there becomes life and death. Verlice in remote areas know they can’t rely on technology to save them, so they cultivate this Devotion to fill that gap.
devotions.effect: The vampire gains an understanding of any obstacles on the road in her path, which might take the form of downed trees, spike strips, serious ice or snow, or anything else that could slow her progress. This understanding extends for roughly (Auspex × 5) miles and allows the vampire to exceptionally succeed on three successes for Drive actions to navigate obstructions. The vampire also gains an inherent understanding of the route she needs to take regardless of distance. This under standing manifests as a fundamental feeling that the route is correct, but it doesn’t impart knowledge of the areas she needs to move through. She gains her Auspex dots as a bonus to any actions related to navigating to her destination, and she cannot be surprised en route.

devotions.name: Murmur
devotions.summary: Reads an omen from the behavior of a flock.
devotions.cost: A Humanity breaking point based on six minus uses this story
devotions.effect: Each success grants the Advanced Action quality to one future roll related to the prophecy. The Devotion cannot be used again until its duration ends or all granted actions are spent. Dread Presence can give one action to another character, while Face of the Beast can transfer all of them. Exceptional success also grants 8-again to one action; dramatic failure attracts a Strix before the story ends.

devotions.name: Bloom
devotions.summary: Forces rapid plant growth through blood and spores.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have infected at least one fully blood-bound mortal with her spores within the last month.
devotions.effect: If the vampire suffers a death blow, she can activate this Devotion to — for lack of a better term — explode, caking the area in viscera. For all intents and purposes, she’s dead. However, over the next night, one of her thralls will experience an agonizing transformation as his body mutates into a facsimile of his master’s, replacing his mind with hers. Once she comes to herself, she regains all traits. For all intents and purposes, she’s undead. Once the transformation is complete, the vampire suffers a Humanity 1 breaking point. Each time she uses Bloom again in a story, the detachment roll suffers a cumulative –1 modifier.

devotions.name: Spore
devotions.summary: Releases the Yarilo's controlling spores; this basic expression is free to the bloodline.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have the blush of life active.
devotions.effect: Once per scene, the Yarilo can spew out a continuous cloud of microscopic spores as she breathes and speaks. Any mortal who inhales theses spores over the course of the scene becomes trivially susceptible to the vampire’s Dominate effects, applying half her Protean dots as a penalty on all rolls to resist. The vampire can affect a number of individuals in a scene equal to her Blood Potency plus one.

devotions.name: Harvest
devotions.summary: Reaps stored vitality or influence from infected growth.
devotions.cost: 1 Willpower, plus one Vitae per victim after the first
devotions.requirement: The vampire must have implanted her spores in all potential victims using Spore within the same scene.
devotions.effect: The vampire can apply Mesmerize to all characters who were exposed to her spores in the area; use the highest resistance trait in the group to contest the activation roll. She must still spend Vitae and make separate rolls for other effects of Dominate.

devotions.name: Sprout
devotions.summary: Creates a new plant extension linked to the Yarilo.
devotions.requirement: The must inflict the victim with the Mesmerized Condition and then use the Spore Devotion on him.
devotions.action: Extended (target is ten plus the victim’s Resolve, and
devotions.effect: each roll represents half an hour of time). The usual results of exceptional success, failure, and dramatic failure for an extended action apply to this action. Once she achieves the required successes, the victim becomes a cipher, totally incapable of acting under his own will. In effect, the Mesmerized Condition becomes persistent, and it can only be resolved if the victim suffers aggravated damage to his head. This Condition applies for the requirements of other Dominate effects, so the vampire has no need to use Mesmerize on the victim. In addition, the spores implanted in the victim’s bloodstream warp his flesh into plant-like protrusions, granting the equiv alent of a permanent Predatory Aspect adaptation (vampire player’s choice). If the vampire knows Unnatural Aspect, she can apply an adaptation from that power as well.

devotions.name: Battering Ram
devotions.summary: Crash through barriers at full speed by reducing their Durability by Resilience.
devotions.effect: If the vampire runs into an object, he can inflict his Resilience dots as a penalty to that object’s Durability. He can crash through walls, break down doors, or shatter weapons used to harm him, but he must be running his full Speed.

devotions.name: Body of Steel
devotions.summary: Turn absorbed attacks back against weapons and unarmed attackers.
devotions.effect: The vampire spends a Vitae if she’s successfully attacked, and any Health levels absorbed by her Resilience are inflicted upon the melee weapon that hit her, dealing damage to its structure. A weapon destroyed this way inflicts (Resilience) dice of bashing damage on the wielder as it shatters in his hand. Characters making unarmed attacks against the vampire take damage directly if she uses this effect.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must absorb incoming damage with Resilience.

devotions.name: Brood Mother
devotions.summary: Birth a temporary flesh-minion from the vampire's own body.
devotions.effect: The vampire births a mobile minion from her own flesh. This creature is Size 2, has a Physical dice pool equal to the vampire’s Protean + Blood Potency, and Health equal to the vampire’s Stamina (including Resilience). Its Defense is half its master’s, rounding up, and it acts after the vampire’s turn in combat. In addition to the cost, the vampire can spend additional Vitae to provide the creature with a Vitae pool, up to an amount equal to its Health. It can spend this Vitae as if it had Blood Potency 1, and it can use Physical Intensity and the active effects of the vampire’s physical Disciplines. It can also manifest its master’s current Predatory Aspect adaptations. When the vampire births this creature, mark off her rightmost Health dot; she cannot regain this dot until she reabsorbs the creature or its remains, or she enters daysleep. At the end of the duration, the creature becomes an inert pile of flesh. In addition to Health, the vampire recoups any remaining Vitae in its system.

devotions.name: Consume
devotions.summary: Absorb a drained mortal into the vampire's body and borrow the victim's knowledge.
devotions.effect: The vampire draws the victim into her body, completely absorbing him, and knowledge flows between the two. She gains all stored Willpower the victim had and, for the duration, can use any of his Mental and Social Skills if they are higher than her own. If the vampire wishes to consume a new victim before the duration expires, she must spend a Vitae to messily regurgitate the previous victim’s bones and partially digested viscera beforehand.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must drain a mortal victim of blood to the point of death.

devotions.name: Earthen Insight
devotions.summary: Learn the rhythms of an area while resting beneath it.
devotions.requirement: Rest for one hour in Unmarked Grave within the area
devotions.effect: The vampire enjoys the 9-again quality for all Drive, Stealth, Streetwise, and Survival rolls made within the area, as well as any Perception rolls. The area in which these bonuses apply is centered on where he used Unmarked Grave, and is equal to a radius of (Blood Potency × 3) kilometers.

devotions.name: Elastic Visage
devotions.summary: Freely reshape cosmetic features and redefine the vampire's default form.
devotions.effect: The vampire can take fine control over her physical form: facial features, hair length/color, irises, skin tone, voice, fat, musculature, sexual characteristics, and so on. Changes don’t have to be particularly human, and the vampire can add bizarre flourishes (extra eyes, spare fingers, unnatural skin tones, etc.), though these alterations offer no benefit beyond aesthetic. As a rule of thumb, she can gain or subtract about a foot of height and 50 lbs from her frame, but these changes aren’t enough to affect traits. This Devotion can bestow Striking Looks 1 or 2, but this costs a Willpower. Sanctity of Merits does not apply. It can also temporarily remove Striking Looks, in which case, Sanctity of Merits does apply if the vampire permanently redefines her form. Transformation lasts until the vampire chooses to revert to her default. She can also spend a Willpower while resting in her Unmarked Grave to redefine her default form.

devotions.name: Endow the Familiar
devotions.summary: Grant a raised animal familiar limited Protean transformations.
devotions.cost: 1 additional Vitae with Raise the Familiar
devotions.effect: The familiar’s body warps, gaining two dots of Protean. The creature cannot raise this Discipline, but it can change adaptations as Kindred can. The vampire can also use this Devotion in conjunction with Undying Familiar (Vampire, p. 148), imbuing a ghoul with this effect when and if it dies.
devotions.requirement: The vampire spends an additional Vitae when uplifting an animal with Raise the Familiar (included in the cost).

devotions.name: Flesh Crafting
devotions.summary: Command a Mesmerized subject's flesh into a new appearance.
devotions.duration: Indefinite on humans; one night on vampires
devotions.effect: The system works the same as Elastic Visage, but the vampire can only use this Devotion on other characters. Alterations created with Flesh Crafting can be preserved with Willpower during daysleep, as with other changes to a vampire’s form. On humans, they’re permanent until the vampire feeds or anoints the subject with another Vitae. Each notable change to a body part takes a turn of contact to effect.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must inflict the Mesmerized Condition on the subject, who must also consume or be anointed by a Vitae (included in cost).

devotions.name: Flesh Sculpting
devotions.summary: Sculpt a subject's Physical Attributes, Size, and bodily Conditions.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must inflict the Mesmerized Condition on the subject, who must also consume or be anointed by a Vitae (included in cost).
devotions.duration: Indefinite on humans; one night on vampires

rollResults.success: The vampire can shift the subject’s Physical Attributes and alter his Size with the following restrictions: • The total number of dots moved and Size levels altered cannot exceed her own Protean dots. • She cannot reduce an Attribute below one dot. • She cannot reduce a character’s Size below 3 or above 7. • She cannot exceed trait limits imposed by Blood Potency and human physical limitations. • She cannot delete Attribute dots, but she can inflict persistent Conditions like Blind, Crippled, or Mute ( Chronicles of Darkness, pp. 288 and 290). Each Condition/Tilt counts as a discrete alteration. For humans, this form is permanent until the vampire feeds/ anoints her with another Vitae. Vampires revert in daysleep but can preserve their new forms by spending a Willpower per each dot/Size level altered. Some Gangrel learn to perform this Devotion on themselves, but this requires a vampire to know Beast’s Skin and to spend an additional Experience on top of the price above. The system is the same as the above, but she does not subtract Stamina from the activation roll, and she does not need to inflict herself with Mesmerized.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire refreshes a Willpower point from the sheer elegance of her work.
rollResults.failure: The subject’s body rejects such gross alteration.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: Something awful happens. The Storyteller has free rein to get icky.

devotions.name: Forced March
devotions.summary: Maintain Celerity's maximum running speed for hours.
devotions.effect: The vampire can move at the maximum Speed allowed by Celerity for the duration. Except for reflexive actions such as Perception, she can do nothing but move in this time. If the vampire stops for any reason, she must reactivate this Devotion. However, any potential assailants must match her Speed or else they have little chance of catching up to her.

devotions.name: Frog Prince
devotions.summary: Transform another character into an animal for the night.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Animal Ken + Protean vs. Stamina + Blood Potency
devotions.requirement: The victim must consume or be anointed by a Vitae (included in cost). If the vampire wants to bestow an animal form she doesn’t have memorized, she must consume blood from such a beast on the same night.

rollResults.success: The subject transforms into an animal for the rest of the night or until the vampire feeds/anoints her with another point of Vitae, whichever comes first. If the Gangrel has the Swarm Form Merit ( Vampire, p. 114), she can bestow that effect as well.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The transformation lasts for additional nights equal to the vampire’s Blood Potency.
rollResults.failure: The victim’s body resists the vampire’s alteration.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire is forced into her own animal form for the rest of the scene and loses access to her other Protean powers.

devotions.name: Gorge
devotions.summary: Swell the body with a temporary reserve of Vitae.
devotions.effect: The Gangrel floods her flesh with Vitae, bulging like a wellfed tick. Swollen with blood, she can store up to her Resilience dots in extra Vitae. While swollen, her skin takes on a crimson hue and a taut appearance that’s unsettling to look upon. This Devotion cannot be used again until the vampire’s Vitae pool contains fewer points than her normal limit.

devotions.name: Graft
devotions.summary: Attach stolen limbs, organs, or bones and use them as part of the vampire's body.
devotions.effect: The vampire attaches a limb his body, torn or removed from its original host, which he can now use as if it was his own. Each limb added grants +1 to Dexterity and Strength; extra organs or bones apply +1 Stamina. However, he can only apply extra parts to his body equal to his Blood Potency dots plus one. The duration above can be reset each night by spending one Vitae per part the vampire wants to keep attached.

devotions.name: Inner Rage
devotions.summary: Escape supernatural coercion by surrendering to an uncontrollable frenzy.
devotions.effect: When the vampire fails to resist Dominate, Majesty, Nightmare, or a Devotion requiring any of these Disciplines, she can activate this Devotion. Doing so causes her to ignore the effects of the Discipline or Devotion targeting her, but she enters frenzy as if she had dramatically failed to resist. She cannot ride the wave or otherwise influence this frenzy, even with the Coil of the Wyrm.

devotions.name: It Will Not Die
devotions.summary: Ignore wounds and briefly remain active when torpor should take hold.
devotions.effect: The vampire can spend one or more Willpower dots to ignore an equal number of Health levels of any damage type. In addition, once per scene, if she would fall to torpor for any reason, he can spend a Willpower point to remain active for a number of additional turns equal to Resilience. However, even if damage in the character’s last Health box is healed in these turns, he will still enter torpor when the duration expires. This Devotion does not function against damage dealt by sunlight or personal banes.

devotions.name: Regeneration
devotions.summary: Repair aggravated wounds without resting at the cost of severe lethargy.
devotions.effect: The vampire can heal any number of aggravated damage she has without resting, manually pressing her flesh back together through painful, ad hoc surgery. However, this is an enormous strain on her dead physiology: Whenever she uses this Devotion, the vampire gains the Lethargic Condition, which ends without resolving in scenes equal to the amount of aggravated damage healed.

devotions.name: Sheep's Clothing
devotions.summary: Memorize and assume the physical form of a mortal drained to death.
devotions.effect: When the vampire drains a mortal to death, he can memorize his form. Just like transforming into an animal, he takes on the Physical traits (Attributes, Skills, Size, Speed, and Health) of the person he’s copying, but none of her memories or personality. Sheep’s Clothing cannot replicate cosmetic changes such as piercings, tattoos, or other body modifications. Other than this restriction, the form the vampire adopts is a perfect replica of his victim at the time of her death. Forms gained with Sheep’s Clothing count towards the number of Beast’s Skin forms the vampire can know at one time.

devotions.name: Walk It Off
devotions.summary: Ignore a personal injury Tilt for a few turns.
devotions.effect: Ignore a Personal Tilt while the affected body part remains attached.

devotions.name: Aura of the Crone
devotions.summary: Lets nearby blood sorcerers use the vampire's Majesty as ritual Potency, or increase equal Potency by one.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.effect: Anyone casting a blood sorcery ritual within the vampire’s presence while this Devotion is active can use her Majesty dots as the ritual’s Potency instead of the usual system. If these numbers are equal or Potency would be higher, increase it by 1. (If you’re using the Ritual Discipline system from Vampire: The Requiem, on an exceptional success, the bonus to Potency adds to the result rather than replacing it.)

devotions.name: Betrayal of Medea
devotions.summary: While hidden, makes a touched scapegoat appear responsible for the vampire's suspicious actions.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be using Face in the Crowd and be touching the scapegoat.
devotions.effect: The vampire casts suspicion on another for her own activities, creating an aura of misbehavior. Add her Nightmare dots to her Obfuscate for the purposes of penalties to notice or track her, and use the higher of the two in any Clash of Wills against supernatural attempts to spot her. Any failure on a penalized action becomes a dramatic failure, which inevitably makes the victim appear to be the culprit instead.

devotions.name: Bitch-Hammer
devotions.summary: A bare-handed blow that exceeds the victim's Stamina prevents most Willpower expenditure.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.requirement: The vampire must successfully deal any kind of damage exceeding the victim’s Stamina using her bare fists. This requirement is not fulfilled if the subject absorbs enough of that damage with Resilience.
devotions.effect: The vampire punches the victim so hard that they get the will knocked out of them. They can’t spend Willpower except for self-preservation, such as bolstering a Resistance Attribute.

devotions.name: Dance of the Swarm
devotions.summary: Questions a local insect swarm to map a neighborhood and improve navigation, searching, and danger detection.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be within the presence of a swarm of insects.

rollResults.success: The swarm responds to the vampire and flies or crawls off in every direction. They return within minutes, using pheromones, waggle dances, or other basic means to communicate a general map of the area to her. This provides the Acolyte with the layout of about a neighborhood’s worth of space, including anything that might be notable to that particular insect — bees will reveal flowering plants, for instance. For the rest of the night, add Animalism to any roll to navigate, search, or spot danger within the area.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The insects convey more intricate details, revealing secret compartments, hidden predators, and perhaps hints of the supernatural that prickle their instincts.
rollResults.failure: The swarm ignores the vampire.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The Acolyte comes off as a threat. The insects are likely to attack her (see the Swarm Tilt on p. XX), or at least cause a distraction.

devotions.name: Folly of Theseus
devotions.summary: Calls mortals within range toward the vampire with an irresistible sense of destiny.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone

rollResults.success: For the duration, mortal characters within (Blood Potency × 15) meters will feel a strong compulsion to seek the vampire, whose location they will inherently know within that area. The vampire can lure up to a number of victims equal to her Majesty/Nightmare dots, but she can’t specify characters unless she’s met them before. She also can’t use this effect on any character with a blood tie or bond to her. This experience is similar to feeling as if one’s destiny is calling, something the victim must do. If they answer this call, they gain a Beat (or a Willpower point if the victim is a Storyteller character), but they can’t then ignore this compulsion. If they instead ignore the call, victims must spend a Willpower or gain the Guilty Condition. A character can only be affected by this Devotion once per night.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: A vampire refreshes a Willpower point of her own.
rollResults.failure: The labyrinth is too foreboding.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: All victims learn the vampire’s location and enjoy +3 on any violent action against her for a single turn of their choosing before the end of the scene.

devotions.name: Grounded Sorcery
devotions.summary: Contests an incoming Ritual Discipline and corrupts its effect even when it succeeds.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.effect: When affected by a Ritual Discipline, the vampire can acti vate this Devotion. Make a Clash of Wills versus the offender; the vampire’s player benefits from the 8-again quality and gains a bonus as if it were a permanent effect. If the vampire prevails, the magic doesn’t affect him. However, regardless of whether he succeeds, the effect corrupts and spreads, taking on strange forms and affecting bystanders or the caster herself. By default, this also inflicts the dramatic failure effect of the offending power (though it may still suc ceed), applying it to the closest individual hostile to the Acolyte. The Storyteller can warp the effect as it suits the situation.

devotions.name: Hekau
devotions.summary: Reads the collective thoughts of a crowd to answer a scene-specific yes/no/maybe question.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be in the presence of at least 100 living people within an area the size of a small city block.

rollResults.success: The vampire opens up her mind to the thoughts of all characters in her immediate vicinity. She can’t listen in on individuals, but she can filter through the mass for information. She can ask a yes/no/maybe question about the current scene, including about characters present. If the Storyteller answers “maybe,” the vampire takes a Beat, but only once per chapter. The vampire can only use this Devotion once per scene.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire can ask two questions.
rollResults.failure: Too much noise, not enough signal.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The Storyteller doesn’t have to answer the question truthfully, but she also doesn’t have to lie.

devotions.name: Instrument of Blood
devotions.summary: Replaces a Predatory Aspect adaptation with a small flesh-and-bone tool of limited Availability.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.effect: When using Predator’s Aspect, the Acolyte can activate this Devotion to replace an adaptation with a piece of equipment, with an Availability rating no greater than her Protean dots and a Size no greater than about 2. This object must be fleshly in some way: For example, she might sprout a chime candle out of fat and sinew from her forearm, produce dander that works like salt to ward off the dead, or just create a ritual knife made of sinew and bone. This object always has the “metaphysical” qualities of the mundane example, though it never counts as a bane. This equipment inflicts a point of lethal damage on the vampire if it’s destroyed, or aggravated if it’s burned. Otherwise, it can be returned to her flesh when Predatory Aspect ends.

devotions.name: Invigorating Draft
devotions.summary: While feeding from a living victim, converts filled Health boxes into healing even when the blood provides no Vitae.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.requirement: This Devotion must be used in conjunction with the Feed move.
devotions.effect: When feeding from a living victim, the vampire heals 2 bashing or 1 lethal damage for every two Health boxes she fills, regardless of whether she gains Vitae or not. This applies whether the victim is human or animal, as long as it’s alive. Even a hoary elder can find warm libations tapped from beasts and men restorative, should she deign to stomach them. When healing this way, bashing damage is always healed before lethal. If the vampire heals any damage, she always inflicts the Drained Condition in addition to Scarred.

devotions.name: Lost in Hindsight
devotions.summary: Warns of an unseen hostile observer and reflexively enables a known Obfuscate power.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.effect: Roll Wits + Empathy + Auspex as a reflexive action whenever someone with hostile intent for the vampire (whom she’s not already aware of) lays eyes upon her or otherwise is about to sense her, including through supernatural means. On a success, she becomes aware of the wicked gaze and can spend a Vitae to activate any of the first four levels of Obfuscate that she knows (in addition to its usual cost). This works like Dodging; it consumes her instant action for the turn but can be done in response to someone else’s action. On an exceptional success, this is reflexive.

devotions.name: Maiden's Innocence
devotions.summary: Rewrites the preceding scene so the vampire physically chose another plausible course, without undoing spent traits or Conditions.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone

rollResults.success: The Acolyte physically removes herself from a situation, altering the minds of everyone present and even the flow of destiny itself. She reappears somewhere she could have reasonably been if she’d done something different in the previous scene that wouldn’t require any other rolled actions: Instead of walking into an ambush, she might have chosen a different alleyway; instead of making a fool of herself with a poorly written speech, she ended up spending extra time preparing in her room. However, this doesn’t undo any temporary changes to her form (like damage, Conditions, or Willpower loss). A vampire can only invoke this Devotion once per night if she’s successful. Using this Devotion (or at least using it too often) is a Humanity 2 breaking point at the Storyteller’s discretion; there’s nothing human about robbing Fate.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire fools even herself. Any damage she took during the scene is removed, as well as any nonpersistent mundane Conditions gained in that time.
rollResults.failure: The Witch has already chosen her destiny.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire makes things worse. The Storyteller decides where she ends up instead, inevitably relying upon bad choices being made. Perhaps she dropped her weapons before heading into the ambush from another direction or didn’t arrive for her important speech at all.

devotions.name: Mark of Betrayal
devotions.summary: Marks a touched victim so others perceive a fearful or disgusting false narrative about him.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.dicePool: Manipulation + Subterfuge + Nightmare vs. Composure + Blood Potency
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be touching the victim.

rollResults.success: Apply the Delusional Condition to the victim, but rather than affecting his perception of the world, it changes how others view him. This should always involve fear, paranoia, disgust, or similar emotions, but the details can otherwise be anything that suits the Condition: Perhaps others believe the victim is keeping people tied up in his basement. As with the Grand Delusion, this can’t define how someone reacts to the belief.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The Condition lasts for additional nights equal to Blood Potency.
rollResults.failure: Seems fine to me.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The victim shrugs off the false narrative. He’s immune to this Devotion and the vampire’s Nightmare for the rest of the night.

devotions.name: Mother's Dance
devotions.summary: A defensive Celerity interruption used to Dodge or move no longer consumes the vampire's instant action.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.effect: When using Celerity to interrupt an opponent’s action, the vampire can activate this Devotion. If she does, and if the action is to Dodge, move, or take another purely defensive act (at the Storyteller’s discretion), it does not use up her instant action for the turn. This Devotion can never be used to inflict harm, such as Fighting Styles that apply weapon damage to Dodge or that create danger in a character’s wake.

devotions.name: Raise the Witch's Familiar
devotions.summary: Enhances a corpse animated with Raise the Familiar, granting access to the vampire's Obfuscate and supernatural danger sense.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.requirement: The vampire must feed an extra Vitae (included in the cost) to a corpse animated with Raise the Familiar.
devotions.effect: The vampire can memorize the shape of any animal ghoul he creates without needing to drain it, and he can immediately exchange one of his forms for a new one without resting in his Unmarked Grave, though he must still spend 1 Vitae as normal. If he created an animal ghoul before learning this Devotion, he can memorize its form the next time he feeds it Vitae. This Devotion also allows the vampire to take on the shapes of animals normally inaccessible to the Beast’s Skin, such as prey animals or animals that exceed the normal Size limit (to a limit of 10). A vampire with Sheep’s Clothing ( Wild Hunt: Gangrel , p. 106) can spend an additional Experience to upgrade this Devotion to apply to his human ghouls as well, though he must spend a point of Willpower to memorize their forms, in addition to the usual Willpower cost of creating a ghoul.

devotions.name: Sharing the Familiar's Form
devotions.summary: Memorizes an animal ghoul's shape without killing it and expands the forms available to Beast's Skin.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.effect: The vampire memorizes the shape of any animal ghoul she creates without draining it and may immediately replace a Beast's Skin form by spending the usual Vitae. Existing animal ghouls can be memorized when next fed. The learned forms may be prey animals or reach Size 10. With Sheep's Clothing, one additional Experience upgrades the Devotion to human ghouls, whose forms also require one Willpower to memorize.

devotions.name: Soul Scab
devotions.summary: Sacrifices part of the vampire's emotional self to resist the Crone's consuming influence.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.requirement: The vampire fails a detachment roll without losing her last dot of Humanity in the process.
devotions.effect: Reaching deep into her soul, the vampire embraces a shard of her monstrous divinity, accepting a bane to ignore the kind of breaking point that provoked her Humanity loss. This curse doesn’t count toward her total for obviating certain breaking points, doesn’t inflict a penalty on future detachment rolls, and doesn’t grant a Beat. A vampire can only have one bane granted by this Devotion at a time.

devotions.name: Spiritual Journey
devotions.summary: Projects a vampire subject's consciousness beyond the limits of the body.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.requirement: The subject must be a vampire and must consent to the effect.

rollResults.success: The vampire grants her subject the effect of Twilight Projection. This operates under all the usual rules.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: Per the exceptional success effect of Twilight Projection.
rollResults.failure: The subject is too bound to the here and now.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire using this Devotion suffers the dramatic failure effect of Twilight Projection.

devotions.name: Taweret's Protection
devotions.summary: Protects a chosen subject with a ward carried in the Blood.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.duration: One week per Blood Potency dot
devotions.requirement: The subject must be anointed with a point of the vampire’s Vitae (included in the cost).
devotions.effect: The Acolyte can spend Vitae up to her Dominate or Resilience dots (whichever is higher) while painting another character with her blood; the subject can be living, dead, or otherwise. For each point spent, she “stores” an active use of Resilience in the subject and can set a trigger that activates it as if the other character had used it. This needn’t be a condition the subject is aware of. For instance, it might activate if he’s cursed from afar with a harmful ritual. If the duration expires before all uses are triggered, they are lost. By spending a Willpower, the Acolyte can choose one trigger that she imbued in the subject that will also provide the passive benefits of Resilience for the rest of the night. A vampire can only use this Devotion on a subject once before it expires.

devotions.name: Unshakable Advance
devotions.summary: Keeps a war-Witch advancing through injury and supernatural opposition.
devotions.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be actively fighting an enemy and fail to resist Dominate, Majesty, Nightmare, or a similar mental/social effect that inflicts a Condition.
devotions.dicePool: Resolve + Socialize + Resilience – the other vampire’s Discipline dots (or equivalent)

rollResults.success: The vampire manages to delay the onset of the inflicted Condition for the duration; he becomes immune to further attempts to apply it as long as this grace period lasts. If he or another character manages to kill or incapacitate the character who inflicted the arrested Condition before his protection runs out, it fades without resolving.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire resolves the Condition if he (and only he) kills/incapacitates the character who inflicted it, gaining a Beat.
rollResults.failure: The vampire’s will is overcome despite his struggling.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire’s mental fortitude is feebler than he thought. Conditions that resolve after suffering damage require twice as much to do so, and other Conditions must be resolved twice before the vampire is rid of them.

devotions.name: Blur
devotions.summary: Conceals a blood-bound human operative with the vampire's Obfuscate.
devotions.requirement: The vampire can only use this Devotion on humans she has a blood bond with. She must touch them to use this effect.
devotions.effect: The subject benefits from the Lost Visage in reflections and video recordings like a vampire but is otherwise visible to direct sensory detection.

devotions.name: Almost Human
devotions.summary: Extends the blush of life, appears human to supernatural senses, and offsets Social penalties with humans.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must be using the blush of life.
devotions.effect: The vampire extends the benefits of the blush of life for the duration. In addition, she registers as human to all supernatural senses, including Auspex, and offsets any Social penalties she might suffer for relating to humans by her Obfuscate dots. Should the vampire frenzy, this effect ends.

devotions.name: Bluster
devotions.summary: Prevents supernatural powers from uncovering the vampire's weaknesses.
devotions.effect: Any attempts to use supernatural powers to uncover the vampire’s weakness, whether her greatest fear, her banes, or anything that would otherwise be used to exploit her, fail automatically; this includes Auspex. Note that this effect can’t prevent good old-fashioned footwork from uncovering any cracks in the armor — it’s pure puffery on the part of the Beast. The fact that the vampire seems to have no weakness is certain to seem suspicious, but it’s very annoying in the short term.

devotions.name: Apex Predator
devotions.summary: Draws predatory attention and blood-sympathy responses toward the vampire.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must take some action to draw attention to herself, whether it be shouting a challenge, breaking a nearby object, or just punching someone in the face.
devotions.effect: Any attempts to lash out will be directed at the vampire using this Devotion regardless of the intended target. If another vampire frenzies in her presence, they must attack her regardless of what provoked the frenzy. A vampire using Beast’s Hackles will always detect the Carthian as the greatest potential danger in the room, as his Beast fixates on her to the exclusion of all else. Seeming so fearsome has its benefits, and as other vampires anticipate danger from the Carthian, her own Beast becomes especially skilled at driving fear into the hearts of her foes. She adds her Vigor dots to any Discipline or Devotion rolls using Nightmare or Obfuscate.

devotions.name: Bullet Time
devotions.summary: Adds Celerity to Firearms attacks for the scene.
devotions.effect: The vampire adds her Celerity dots to Firearms attacks for the duration.

devotions.name: Guardian Vigil
devotions.summary: Makes ambush detection a rote action and rewards a failed ambush with a free Celerity effect.
devotions.effect: The vampire treats any Perception action to detect an ambush as a rote action. If someone fails to ambush him, he can use an effect of Celerity that would normally cost Vitae for free.

devotions.name: Death Mask
devotions.summary: Feigns Final Death to natural and supernatural senses for a week.
devotions.effect: The vampire seems to all supernatural and natural senses to have met her Final Death. Her body begins to rot and decay as it would according to her true age, stopping just short of turning to ash, instead leaving behind a desiccated corpse. She can end this effect at any point with a reflexive action, and her body will regenerate back into its formerly undead state. The vampire can still move while this Devotion is active without ending it, though the effect will be rather alarming to bystanders. If the vampire also knows Auspex 3, she can purchase an upgraded version of this Devotion for 3 Experiences. If anyone attempts to pry through her memories or uncover the means of her “Final Death” through supernatural means, she can falsify the information the investigator uncovers with Manipulation + Subterfuge + Auspex, contested by the investigator’s Resolve + Blood Potency.

devotions.name: Husk
devotions.summary: Accelerates feeding dramatically, at the risk of leaving a conspicuous and potentially lethal wound.
devotions.requirement: Must be used to modify the Feed move.
devotions.effect: The vampire adds the lower of their Celerity or Vigor to her Blood Potency when determining the amount of Vitae she can take from a human victim per turn during violent feeding, though she can choose not to use this effect. This is an extraordinarily violent, cruel method of feeding, doubling all penalties from the Scarred Condition. If the vampire chooses to take three more Vitae than her Blood Potency in one turn, the bite leaves a gaping wound that’s both noticeable and potentially lethal. Until the victim receives medical attention, she must make a Resolve + Stamina roll every 10 minutes or will suffer another point of lethal damage as they bleed out.

devotions.name: Got My Back
devotions.summary: Calls allied predators through the Beast when the vampire is threatened.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must activate this Devotion on the same turn she invokes blood sympathy.
devotions.effect: The vampire’s blood sympathy dice pools are doubled when communicating pain or fear to those she has a blood tie with. She can’t control how they might react, but remaining where they are rather than going to her location costs a point of Willpower, and attempting to bring further harm to her costs another.

devotions.name: It's Who You Know
devotions.summary: Reads a subject's aliases, Contacts, Allies, and potentially damaging social connections.
devotions.requirement: The victim must be human.

rollResults.success: For each success, the vampire learns any names or aliases her subject goes by, along with any Contacts or Allies they have. This effect is not penalized by Anonymity.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire learns a damaging piece of information about one of the subject’s Social Merits, if applicable. If not, she learns it about her prey.
rollResults.failure: This guy’s clean. Too clean.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The vampire’s information is entirely, dangerously false: a political alliance that doesn’t exist, a trusted confidant allying with a hated enemy, etc.

devotions.name: Just Fucking Book It
devotions.summary: Combines speed and endurance to escape a losing confrontation.
devotions.effect: As long as the vampire keeps running and takes no instant actions, she ignores the Vitae-per-turn costs of using Celerity, Resilience, and Vigor. Should she take any other instant action beyond running, this effect ends.

devotions.name: Knockout
devotions.summary: Drops a witness without leaving a corpse.
devotions.effect: The vampire activates this Devotion on the same turn he successfully attacks a mortal with Brawl. Instead of the usual injuries, he deals a single point of bashing damage, and the victim falls unconscious for hours equal to the Carthian’s Vigor dots.

devotions.name: Last Man Standing
devotions.summary: Removes cumulative Defense loss and permits one reflexive Dodge per turn while cornered.
devotions.effect: The vampire steels himself against difficult odds. He no longer takes a penalty to his Defense each time he is attacked in a turn, and he can dodge one attack per turn as a reflexive action. He applies his Resilience as a bonus to riding the wave, and if he does fall into frenzy, his Beast can’t be goaded to flee under any circumstances. He will fight to the Final Death.

devotions.name: Mutation
devotions.summary: Redistributes dots among the three physical Disciplines for the scene.
devotions.effect: The vampire can redistribute up to (Blood Potency) dots of her physical Disciplines between each other, though none can be reduced lower than one dot or exceed five.

devotions.name: Lying Eyes
devotions.summary: Makes a sincerely believed statement supernaturally convincing and can impose Contrary on a doubter.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must make a statement she knows or believes to be true. This can’t be an objective fact like “the sky is blue” or “Kindred drink blood.” It must be something at least partly open to debate.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Subterfuge + Obfuscate vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire exudes untrustworthiness. The victim takes the Contrary Condition.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The vampire adds his Obfuscate dots to his Subterfuge score for the rest of the scene.
rollResults.failure: The vampire is recognized for his honesty. For once.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The Devotion turns on the vampire. He’s incapable of actively lying for the rest of the scene.

devotions.name: Operant Conditioning
devotions.summary: Conditions a subject to react violently to a chosen trigger.
devotions.requirement: The vampire can only use this effect after being the subject of a Discipline or Devotion, whether mental, physical, or social. The character doesn’t need to be aware of this effect, but the player can evoke it on her behalf.
devotions.dicePool: Presence + Intimidation + Nightmare vs. Composure + Blood Potency

rollResults.success: The vampire instills a sense of lingering dread in her foe, tied to whichever Discipline was used on her. If the other vampire attempts to use that same Discipline or a Devotion derived from it in the scene, he suffers her Nightmare dots as a penalty to the roll. If he ever fails to use it, he loses access to it until the next scene. The vampire can learn an upgraded version of this Devotion if she gains another dot of Nightmare and pays an additional Experience. This extends all durations to a night but requires her to also spend a Vitae.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: The repulsion is overpowering. The victim must spend a point of Willpower each time they even attempt to use the affected Devotion.
rollResults.failure: A brief shudder runs down the subject’s spine, but any sense of fear is gone as fast as it came.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The dread the vampire intended to evoke turns inward. If she uses Nightmare or a derived Devotion before the end of the scene, she gains the Frightened Condition.

devotions.name: Power in a Union
devotions.summary: Strengthens physical teamwork and leaves the group coordinated for the rest of the night.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must use this Devotion in conjunction with a teamwork action using a Physical Attribute where she is the primary actor.

rollResults.success: Each character other than the vampire working on the teamwork action gains her Vigor dots as a bonus to their own actions.
rollResults.exceptionalSuccess: Each member within the teamwork action also takes the Steadfast Condition.
rollResults.failure: Like herding cats, man.
rollResults.dramaticFailure: The Beast rages against the idea of acknowledging lesser predators. The vampire cannot participate in any teamwork actions with the other characters for the rest of the night.

devotions.name: Trick Shot
devotions.summary: Executes an extraordinary Firearms maneuver before a target can retaliate.
devotions.effect: The vampire adds half his Celerity dots (rounded up) as damage to a successful Firearms attack. He also ignores any range penalties or penalties from cover he would ordinarily take.

devotions.name: Uplift
devotions.summary: Feeds a revenant five Vitae to preserve Vitae through daysleep and temporarily grant further Kindred-like benefits.
devotions.requirement: The vampire must feed a revenant the Vitae cost. This will not create a blood bond or cause Vitae addiction, for better or worse.
devotions.effect: The subject gains something close to the benefits Kindred enjoy. The revenant no longer loses all Vitae upon waking from daysleep and appears to be an ordinary vampire of the Devotion-user’s clan. The subject can act against her benefactor, but she must spend a point of Willpower the first time she tries to harm him in the scene. Even if she does so, any actions she takes against him suffer the vampire’s Animalism dots as a penalty.

devotions.name: Sawbones
devotions.summary: Uses supernatural endurance to survive and repair otherwise catastrophic bodily harm.
devotions.effect: The healing capacity of the Blood kicks into overdrive. Any Medicine rolls to treat the vampire’s wounds add his Resilience as a modifier, and he can heal aggravated damage not caused by sunlight as though it were lethal damage.

devotions.name: Skulk
devotions.summary: Bypasses passive supernatural effects that would alert their users to the vampire's intrusion.
devotions.effect: The vampire occults her metaphysical presence. Any passive supernatural effect that would alert its user to her intrusion in an area, such as Lord of the Land, fails to detect her, bypassing any Clash of Wills. This does not apply to active searching, such as with Auspex. The vampire is still entirely visible through mundane senses unless she uses another Discipline or Devotion.

devotions.name: Witch Hunt
devotions.summary: Examines an unknown supernatural being as a potential enemy and reveals useful weaknesses.
devotions.requirement: The vampire uses Uncanny Perception to reveal a creature as a supernatural creature and then spends an additional Vitae (included in the cost).
devotions.effect: The vampire smells out all possible predefined forms the creature possesses. Each flickers through her aura over the course of a few seconds. Her keen senses also pick out the potential strengths of this potential foe, learning which of the subject’s forms she should fear the most.

lashes.name: Iron Joy
lashes.summary: Offer a mortal the pack's emotional high while protecting him from other predators.
lashes.procedure: With this Lash, the Unchained can offer a fleeting sense of their emotional highs to temporarily stun, seduce, or entice a mortal, while also keeping him safe from the will of other predators. The vampire makes a scratch to draw the mortal’s blood, then makes a matching scratch on herself, mingling their blood with clasped hands or bloodied kisses. This costs a Vitae.
lashes.outcome: The blood offering obliterates other thoughts or goals in the subject’s mind. They become compliant and suggestible, eager to obey the pack. In addition to the usual effects of drinking Vitae, for the next week, any pack member using mental or social Disciplines on the subject treats a normal success as an exceptional success. However, the subject’s pleasure in submission hardens his will, adding the vampire’s Blood Tether dots as a bonus to all Resolve rolls (except when resisting the pack’s abilities).

lashes.name: Shared Feast
lashes.summary: Bind a mortal's feeding to the pack through a shared vessel of blood.
lashes.procedure: To establish this Lash, the vampire and a mortal subject feed from the same vessel of blood. The vessel must include one Vitae each from at least two members of the pack, including the one initiating the Lash. Performing this ritual does not risk blood bonds, but it does risk addiction.
lashes.outcome: Once a night, the mortal regains a point of Willpower for being fed upon. In return, the pack member who granted this feeding gains double the Vitae she normally would. This effect lasts for feedings equal to Vitae spent into the Lash.

cruacRites.name: Boyar's Caul
cruacRites.summary: A 1-dot Yagnatia Crúac rite bargaining with the gods and spirits of the land.
cruacRites.effect: The ritualist spreads the sacrifice over her face and enters daysleep. At the next dusk it has become an ectoplasmic mask resembling someone important to her current schemes. Intelligence + Occult interprets the omen; on success she may ask yes/no/maybe questions equal to the rite's Potency. If she knows Auspex, she may use The Spirit's Touch once that night to ask questions from Uncanny Perception. Wearing the caul grants +3 to Investigation rolls to identify or locate its subject. It turns to ash at night's end.

cruacRites.name: Awaken the Dukh
cruacRites.summary: A 4-dot Yagnatia Crúac rite bargaining with the gods and spirits of the land.
cruacRites.effect: The vampire bargains with the spirit of an object no larger than Size 5. The spirit gains limited control of its physical form, allowing simple tasks and movement, with a dice pool of Crúac + Size + Potency. The Storyteller decides which actions are possible. An appropriate oblation renews the pact before it expires. The spirit is not compelled to obey, but spattering the object with Vitae ends the rite early and returns it to the Shadow.

cruacRites.name: Divine Right
cruacRites.summary: A 2-dot Yagnatia Crúac rite bargaining with the gods and spirits of the land.
cruacRites.effect: Before the end of the night, the vampire may invoke this blessing when someone openly questions or defies her authority. That action automatically fails and the challenger gains the Guilty Condition. The rite applies a number of times equal to Potency, then ends.

cruacRites.name: Hawthorn Barrier
cruacRites.summary: A 3-dot Yagnatia Crúac rite bargaining with the gods and spirits of the land.
cruacRites.effect: Hawthorn branches placed across an aperture create an invisible Essence ward. Without the vampire's permission, mortals cannot cross; Kindred must roll Resolve + Blood Potency, penalized by the rite's Potency. Failure requires resisting fear frenzy. A Kindred who succeeds and crosses without permission takes lethal damage equal to the Boyar's Crúac dots. One casting can ward multiple apertures within line of sight if enough branches are available. Branches from mandragora grant 9-again to the casting roll.

cruacRites.name: The Mother's Blessing
cruacRites.summary: A 3-dot Yagnatia Crúac rite bargaining with the gods and spirits of the land.
cruacRites.effect: The subject's next childe begins with a first-stage blood bond to the sire that lasts until the sire releases her, but remains immune to the sire's full Vinculum and to any other Yagnatia's blood bond during that tutelage. The childe gains 8-again to rolls to initiate or detect blood sympathy with Yagnatia. The blessing applies to one Embrace, can affect a vampire only once per lunar month, cannot be cast on oneself, and only works on Boyars.

cruacRites.name: Vessel of the Dukh
cruacRites.summary: A 5-dot Yagnatia Crúac rite bargaining with the gods and spirits of the land.
cruacRites.effect: Using a human corpse no more than one night dead, the ritualist creates a Brief Nightmare. A Minion needs no extra successes, a Horde needs three, and a Lone Terror needs five; the extended action's normal roll limit still applies. The Storyteller chooses suitable Dread Powers, excluding Firestarter. The Horror is vulnerable to fire like a Kindred, animalistic but loyal, and regains Willpower by drinking Vitae or human blood. Recasting before expiration and paying all costs renews it. Creating a new Horror is a breaking point at Humanity 2 or higher.

cruacRites.name: The Red Blossoms
cruacRites.summary: Grow plants into an archway that opens into the Hedge.
cruacRites.source: Changeling: The Lost Second Edition — The Hedge
cruacRites.effect: The vampire feeds plants with Vitae until they grow into an arch through which one of the Kindred can pass into the Hedge.

cruacRites.name: Clotho's Skein
cruacRites.summary: Dreamwalk through daysleep connections to implant a suggestion.
cruacRites.effect: The next time the ritualist rests, her mind remains aware and perceives the dream-threads of every Kindred within one mile. She may designate one target during casting, making that thread obvious, or choose later from vague dream impressions. Success implants one thought or idea: a goal or a changed opinion. It cannot compel self-harm, though it may provoke violence against others, and the target pursues it in their own customary way.

cruacRites.name: Sanguine Augur
cruacRites.summary: Dream cryptic revelations about the last vessel you fed from.
cruacRites.effect: At the next daysleep, receive a cryptic vision revealing one previously unknown fact about the most recent vessel. Each additional Vitae spent either reveals another fact or makes the original vision less cryptic, never both. For Kindred this may reveal Touchstones, bloodline, Merits, or lineage back a number of generations equal to Crúac; for mortals it may reveal life details or Vinculum strength.

cruacRites.name: Wisdom of the Blood
cruacRites.summary: Read prophecies about a subject in a torpid vampire's dreams.
cruacRites.effect: Using a torpid vampire as a medium, ask one question per Vitae spent and receive a brief, truthful prophecy through the target's dreams. Answers remain fleeting and symbolic and may reflect the target's biases; yes-or-no wording does not make them clearer.

cruacRites.name: Donning the Beast’s Flesh
cruacRites.summary: Wear a flayed animal skin to assume an approximation of that beast.
cruacRites.requirement: A garment made from a flayed animal
cruacRites.effect: The wearer approximates the animal's form and retains only Auspex among Disciplines while transformed.

cruacRites.name: Mantle of Amorous Fire
cruacRites.summary: Dance to exhaustion and add Crúac as a Presence bonus for the night.
cruacRites.requirement: Dance and activate Blush of Life as part of casting
cruacRites.effect: The ritualist becomes exhausted, regains Willpower as specified by the rite, and adds Crúac to Presence for the night.

cruacRites.name: Mantle of the Beast’s Breath
cruacRites.summary: Dance to exhaustion, gain Raptured, and add Crúac when riding the wave.
cruacRites.requirement: Dance and activate Blush of Life as part of casting
cruacRites.effect: The ritualist gains the Raptured Condition and adds Crúac to attempts to ride the wave for the night.

cruacRites.name: Pool of Forbidden Truths
cruacRites.summary: Gain Primeval Truths and interpret a prophetic vision.
cruacRites.effect: The ritualist gains the Primeval Truths Condition and may ask for one truthful sentence from the vision per success on the interpretation roll.

cruacRites.name: Bounty of the Storm
cruacRites.summary: Prepare a storm that strikes a future crowd, maims the target, and leaves immense wealth.
cruacRites.requirement: A personal or precious object connected to the target
cruacRites.duration: Triggers between one week and one lunar month after casting
cruacRites.effect: The target suffers Crúac bashing damage, roughly one third of the surrounding crowd dies, and the aftermath provides Resources-equivalent wealth; casting risks detachment at Humanity 2.

cruacRites.name: Curse of Aphrodite’s Favor
cruacRites.summary: Create a three-dose potion that forces a full Vinculum to a chosen subject.
cruacRites.requirement: Feed the victim one drop on each of three consecutive nights
cruacRites.effect: After the third dose, the victim suffers a full Vinculum to the chosen subject rather than to the ritualist.

cruacRites.name: Curse of the Beloved Toy
cruacRites.summary: Bind a slain victim's soul into a cherished keepsake that curses later owners.
cruacRites.requirement: A beloved possession and the death of its owner
cruacRites.duration: Until its invested Vitae is exhausted or the spirit is exorcised
cruacRites.effect: Each invested Vitae can turn one action by the item's owner into a dramatic failure; destroying the item only drives the spirit to another host.

cruacRites.name: Gorgon’s Gaze
cruacRites.summary: Prepare the ritualist's eyes to petrify the first person who sees them.
cruacRites.effect: Each success petrifies roughly one fifth of the victim and inflicts one aggravated damage; five successes petrify the whole body, killing mortals or placing Kindred in torpor.

cruacRites.name: Mantle of the Glorious Dervish
cruacRites.summary: Dance to exhaustion and become an untiring supernatural combatant for the night.
cruacRites.requirement: Dance and activate Blush of Life as part of casting
cruacRites.effect: Gain armor 1 against all attacks, deal +1 damage with attacks, and become immune to ambush and surprise.

cruacRites.name: Shed the Virulent Bowels
cruacRites.summary: Hang a lethal curse over a living victim for up to a lunar month.
cruacRites.requirement: A lock of hair or other sympathetic link
cruacRites.effect: When triggered, the curse fills the living victim's Health track with lethal damage at one point per turn.

cruacRites.name: Birthing the God
cruacRites.summary: Assemble body parts and Vitae to violently birth an undead, flesh-eating god.
cruacRites.requirement: A coven, harvested body parts, and invested Vitae
cruacRites.effect: Invested Vitae purchases Attributes and Disciplines, sets Size at one per five Vitae and Blood Potency at one per three Vitae, while celebrants contribute Skills and suffer the creature's violent birth.

cruacRites.name: Denying Hades
cruacRites.summary: Trap a recently deceased spirit in its corpse between life and death.
cruacRites.requirement: A corpse dead no longer than the ritualist's Blood Potency in days
cruacRites.effect: The corpse returns conscious but decaying and sleepless; the ritualist suffers an unhealable aggravated wound until the corpse rests again.

cruacRites.name: Mantle of the Crone
cruacRites.summary: Assume the Crone's terrible mantle, revealing truths and transforming matter through touch.
cruacRites.effect: Witnesses gain Primeval Truths, the ritualist's touch deals aggravated damage, and Willpower can animate an object as a lizard-like animal for the night.

cruacRites.name: Mantle of the Predator Goddess
cruacRites.summary: Dance to exhaustion and become a divine predator for the night.
cruacRites.requirement: Dance and activate Blush of Life as part of casting
cruacRites.effect: Add Crúac to feeding rolls and as temporary Herd dots; anyone fed from gains the Raptured Condition.

cruacRites.name: Ma'at and Kauket
cruacRites.summary: Invert the spiritual resonance of an area and alter its Resonant Condition.
cruacRites.effect: The rite introduces chaos into an area, reversing qualities it previously encouraged and temporarily altering the Resonant Condition of any locus. The area imposes a penalty equal to the caster's Crúac dots on Social or Physical actions it would previously have aided.

cruacRites.name: Ahmet's Pursuit
cruacRites.summary: Curse a nearby subject through a material focus, inflicting Lost and revealing the target's location for the rest of the night.
cruacRites.effect: Using an effigy or other material focus, curse a victim within one mile with Lost. Even a successful navigation roll, penalized by Potency, sends the victim along the worst route or through the wrong door. The ritualist always knows where the victim runs.

cruacRites.name: Doom of Osiris
cruacRites.summary: Consecrate a bladed weapon so its attacks inflict aggravated damage upon ephemeral beings.
cruacRites.effect: A bladed weapon deals aggravated damage to ephemeral beings and Strix, even while they are in Twilight if the wielder can perceive them. At dawn the weapon turns to sand.

cruacRites.name: Feast of Ka
cruacRites.summary: Force a Hollow Mekhet's Ka to materialize and feed it Essence.
cruacRites.effect: Prepare a meal for a Hollow Mekhet's Ka using foods the vampire enjoyed in life and Vitae. The Ka gains Materialized; if tracking Conditions, the table gains Anchor and Open. If it eats, it gains Essence equal to the Vitae used and cannot manifest to harass the vampire again until her next breaking point, though she may still call it voluntarily. While materialized, it can converse, with its attitude determined by its relationship with the Mekhet.

cruacRites.name: Hand of Seth
cruacRites.summary: Exorcise a possessing ephemeral entity from its host.
cruacRites.requirement: A scrap of the vessel's DNA, such as hair or fingernails.
cruacRites.effect: Force a spirit or Strix out of a body within one mile. A ghost or spirit returns to Twilight, the vessel's ephemeral Conditions are temporarily suppressed, and the entity cannot repossess the victim for the scene. This rite does not affect Claimed.

cruacRites.name: Thrashing of Apep's Coils
cruacRites.summary: Call violent rain over the ritual area and optionally add heavy winds; prepared allies are protected.
cruacRites.effect: Impale the sacrifice with a spear at the climax of the rite to impose Heavy Rain within a mile, covering roughly a half-mile radius. The ritualist and allies carrying Sethite-blessed charms are immune. Adding one Vitae to the sacrifice also calls one level of Heavy Winds. The Sethite may dismiss the storm with an instant action.

cruacRites.name: Gwydion's Curse
cruacRites.summary: Animate nearby plants to attack intruders until sunrise.
cruacRites.effect: Vitae soaked into the earth animates trees and large plants within Potency meters. They attack anyone in reach using Blood Potency for all pools, deal 1 bashing, have Durability 2 and no Willpower, and share a Vitae pool equal to the sacrifice as the ritualist chooses. They may spend one Vitae per turn to heal two Structure.

cruacRites.name: Manananggal's Working
cruacRites.summary: Dismember yourself and animate the separated parts independently until sunrise.
cruacRites.effect: The ritualist cuts off any number of body parts, which move independently and perform tasks. All sacrificed Vitae must be her own. At sunrise the parts return and reattach; a part unable to return bursts, dealing one bashing for a small part, two for a limb, or three for a vital part, then regrows within an hour. Missing useful parts impose appropriate Tilts, and removing much of the body may divide the Vitae pool among the pieces.

cruacRites.name: Scapegoat
cruacRites.summary: Transfer breaking points and acquired banes to a mortal vessel for the night.
cruacRites.effect: Feed the rite's Vitae to a mortal. The ritualist cannot risk detachment, suffer acquired banes, or gain Willpower from Touchstones; the mortal instead suffers those banes and rolls the breaking points with a one-die penalty. When the rite ends, the vampire gains Wanton and suffers −3 to breaking points until it resolves. The rite cannot be performed if the vampire is still immune to a repeated Wanton Condition gained from it that month.

cruacRites.name: Cheval
cruacRites.summary: See and hear through a touched subject.
cruacRites.effect: The ritualist sees and hears what the subject does regardless of distance.

cruacRites.name: Pangs of Proserpina
cruacRites.summary: Provoke supernatural hunger in a distant victim.
cruacRites.effect: A victim within one mile counts as starving for the next frenzy-resistance roll, regardless of recent feeding.

cruacRites.name: Rigor Mortis
cruacRites.summary: Suppress the reanimating force of a vampire's Vitae.
cruacRites.effect: A vampire victim within one mile suffers –3 dice on the next physical action.

cruacRites.name: The Hydra's Vitae
cruacRites.summary: Curse the ritualist's own blood into poison.
cruacRites.effect: Vampires/Strix drinking the ritualist's blood take lethal per Vitae and gain no nourishment; mortals/ghouls take heavier lethal damage.

cruacRites.name: Blood Blight
cruacRites.summary: Mystically destroy blood or Vitae in a victim.
cruacRites.effect: Mortals take ritual Potency lethal damage; Kindred, Strix, and ghouls lose ritual Potency Vitae, usually provoking hunger frenzy checks in Kindred.

cruacRites.name: Blood Price
cruacRites.summary: Redirect blood consumed by a subject to the ritualist.
cruacRites.effect: Whenever the subject drinks blood, up to ritual Potency Vitae go to the ritualist first; excess remains with the subject.

cruacRites.name: Deflection of Wooden Doom
cruacRites.summary: Ward the ritualist against staking.
cruacRites.effect: All attempts to stake the ritualist fail.

cruacRites.name: Feeding the Crone
cruacRites.summary: Transform feeding into a savage supernatural bite.
cruacRites.duration: Until next sunrise or cancelled with 1 Vitae
cruacRites.effect: The ritualist gains no Vitae from feeding but the bite deals +2 aggravated damage.

cruacRites.name: Touch of the Morrigan
cruacRites.summary: Charge the ritualist's touch with lethal force.
cruacRites.duration: Until first use or next sunrise
cruacRites.effect: The first successful touch attack inflicts lethal damage equal to ritual Potency and ends the rite.

cruacRites.name: Willful Vitae
cruacRites.summary: Prevent new Vinculum and blood addiction for the night.
cruacRites.effect: The ritualist is immune to new Vinculum and blood addiction; existing bonds/addiction remain.

cruacRites.name: Prey's Blood
cruacRites.summary: Track a recent vessel by cardinal direction and empower attempts to follow the trail.
cruacRites.effect: Sense the subject's direction and add Crúac to Investigation, Survival, and Kindred Senses rolls to track them.

cruacRites.name: Balancing the Four Humors
cruacRites.summary: Brew doses that protect against extreme environments and Environmental Tilts.
cruacRites.effect: Consumers add the ritualist's Crúac to rolls penalized by extreme environments or Environmental Tilts, except fire and sunlight.

cruacRites.name: Curse of Ahasverus
cruacRites.summary: Make a victim appear as a hostile outsider to every vampire they meet.
cruacRites.effect: Kindred must spend Willpower not to lash out at the victim, and frenzy resistance near them is penalized by Potency.

cruacRites.name: Sacrifice of Odin
cruacRites.summary: Maim the ritualist to empower Willpower and resistance for as long as the wound remains.
cruacRites.effect: An aggravated self-mutilation grants +5 from Willpower on actions, +3 to Resistance Attributes, and a chance to recover Willpower spent on mundane actions.

cruacRites.name: Tickblood
cruacRites.summary: Double a victim's Vitae capacity and make their blood unnaturally nourishing.
cruacRites.effect: Feeding from the subject yields two Vitae per lethal damage and the swollen body gains two general armor except against bites.

cruacRites.name: Twisting the Id
cruacRites.summary: Carves an unwanted mundane emotional or mental Condition into a subject for the night at the cost of lethal damage.
cruacRites.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
cruacRites.effect: Carve an unwanted emotion into a subject, inflicting one lethal damage, and choose a mundane nonpersistent emotional or mental Condition. If the subject would suffer it that night, they instead gain Inspired, Steadfast, or Sated. At Crúac ••• with two additional successes, this can replace any Condition, though supernatural Conditions require a Clash of Wills.

cruacRites.name: Fires of Inspiration
cruacRites.summary: Adds Potency to one later Crafts action before dawn.
cruacRites.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
cruacRites.effect: After approaching frenzy while immersed in a creative muse, gain the rite's Potency as bonus dice to one later Crafts action before night's end; that action may be extended.

cruacRites.name: Witch's Locus
cruacRites.summary: Enlivens a small home's spirit, producing occult signs and empowering the ritualist's senses within it.
cruacRites.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
cruacRites.duration: Night; one week at Crúac •• with one additional success
cruacRites.effect: Mark the boundary of an area no larger than a small home. Peripheral supernatural signs impose −2 on Composure rolls and attempts to make a good impression in Social maneuvering.

cruacRites.name: Mantle of the Predator's Eye
cruacRites.summary: Grants Acute Senses and adds Crúac to Blood Potency for relevant predatory perception.
cruacRites.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
cruacRites.effect: After dancing through the ritual and collapsing from exhaustion, gain Acute Senses and add Crúac dots to Blood Potency for the Merit and Kindred Senses.

cruacRites.name: Mark of the Praecursor
cruacRites.summary: Wards a manor-sized area and marks those who spy into it.
cruacRites.source: Agony & Ecstasy: Circle of the Crone
cruacRites.effect: Cover an area no larger than a manor house in warning sigils. Anyone using supernatural scrying or information-gathering on or inside it weeps black tears through mundane coverings until chapter end; exempt up to Potency people. At Crúac •• with one more success, reflective surfaces show the latest unseen offender's face. At Crúac •••• with three more successes, supernatural concealment in the area automatically provokes a Clash of Wills.

cruacRites.name: Barrier of Blood
